data.name: Vatican & Sistine Chapel: Family-Friendly Private Half-Day Tour
data.description: Explore the world-famous Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel with a private guide and learn about Vatican City and the history of the papacy through its extensive collection of art, archaeology and anthropology artefacts gathered by the Popes over the centuries. On your family-friendly private tour, you will: Enjoy the personalised attention of a private tour guide, who will tailor the tour to your family’s interest, to make it engaging for children and teens; Visit parts of the museums not usually seen including the Egyptian Museum, and the Carriage Museum; Explore the Egyptian gallery, to see well-preserved mummies and learn all about Egyptianfunerals; See the amazing carriagepavilion - which still smells of old leather and horses, see centuries-old carriages used by Popes on ceremonial occasions and old horse liveries and uniforms;  Walk down the halls of busts and statues, filled with ancient statues of gods, heroes, and wealthy Roman men and women, to learn all about life and fashions in ancient Rome; See the famous Laocoön and Apollo statues; Walk the galleries of Candelabras - filled with ancient statues, the Raphael Tapestries, and the dazzling 16th century frescoed Maps; Marvel at the astounding works of Michelangelo Buonarroti as you enter the Sistine Chapel; See if you can find some naughty jokes that Michelangelo hid in his art - that the pope didn't see - but your guide will show you; End the tour inside the Vatican Museums, where you can grab something to eat at one of the family-friendly pizzerias, and keep exploring at your own leisure, or exit the museums with your guide.  Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, yet one of the most culturally rich places on earth! The Vatican Museums are home to some of the world's most admired and valued works of art - many of which are frescos and so immovable - such as the Sistine Chapel. Your private, family-friendly tour will ensure you see all the usual highlights of the Vatican Museums, but also some areas not often seen on guided tours that will really engage your younger family members, such as the Carriage Museum and the Egyptian Gallery. The Carriage Museum still smells of horses and is where you will see a huge array of ceremonial carriages, sedan chairs - and the more modern pope mobiles! The Egyptian museum contains fascinating funereal relics of ancient Egypt - including a well-preserved mummy. You'll also see famous statues such as the Apollo and Laocoön in the Belvedere Courtyard, before walking down the long galleries of the RaphaelTapestries and dazzling Gallery of the Maps. Finally, enter the SistineChapel - the awe-inspiring work of Michelangelo, and perhaps the most remarkable masterpiece in the entire history of art. Your guide will explain the meaning, symbolism, and brilliance of Michelangelo's work, pointing out a few hidden jokes that Michelangelo - who often fought with the pope - left in the frescos! Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: Rome  - Walking Tour  - 'Roma Barocca'  - 5 ore
data.shortDescription:
Meet by your local guide and enjoy a guided tour of Rome - the Eternal City (approx. 3 hours). The tour begins at the Trevi Fountain, which has become an iconic spot thanks to the movie ‘La Dolce Vita’, directed by Federico Fellini. The tour will take you to the streets of the old town, visiting famous sites such as the Pantheon; the Palazzo Madama, which houses the Senate of the Italian Republic (entrance not included); and Navona Square, which was built on the ruins of the Domitian Circus. Once the tour finishes you can enjoy the rest of the afternoon at leisure. 

Possibility to reserve half day or full day

data.name: Shared Transfer From the Civitavecchia Port to Fiumicino airport
data.description: For those who want an hassle-free cruise transfer we provide connection with Civitavecchia port and the City center. We guarantee punctual and professional service that will suit all your needs, available 7 days a week. Our driver will wait for you at the pier holding a sign with your name. Forget the stress and enjoy your shuttle transfer comfortably seated in our Mercedes minivan. We are at your disposal. The driver will pick you up at the cruise ship pier, as the service provider has permission to enter the port’s boarding and disembarkation area. Pick-ups and drop-offs are also available from or to hotels or agreed locations in Rome city center. You’ll travel comfortably in a well-maintained luxury vehicle (mini-van for up to 8 passengers). A competent and experienced driver will ensure that you reach your destination safely.

data.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Guided Evening Tour
data.description:
Enjoy an exclusive evening tour of the Vatican. Spend your day exploring Rome, then enter the Vatican Museums when the daytime crowds have thinned.

With fast-track entry, follow an expert guide through the halls, including the Raphael Rooms, Nero's Bathtub, and the famous Laocoön and His Sons. See St. Peter's Dome under the night sky while hearing stories about the Vatican's rich history. End in the Sistine Chapel, viewing Michelangelo's art as evening falls over Rome.

This evening access lets you see the Vatican's art and history without the daytime crowds and heat. Explore the Vatican's treasures in a more relaxed setting.

data.name: Tour SEMI privado  del Coliseo, Foro y Palatino SPAGOLO
data.shortDescription:
Patrimonio de la Humanidad y una de las Siete Maravillas del Mundo. Conoced el Coliseo de la forma más personalizada posible con este tour privado en el que contaréis con un guía en exclusiva. Solo para ti y tu pareja, familia o amigos.

data.name: Unexpected Rome: cycle between Villa Borghese and Villa Ada, discover the magic of the Coppedè district
data.description: Have you ever dreamed of getting lost in a labyrinth of enchanted buildings, hidden in the green heart of Rome? Imagine cycling along tree-lined avenues, admiring masterpieces of art in the open air and letting yourself be enchanted by stories of kings and nobles. With this exclusive tour, we will take you to discover a face of Rome that few know: a magical mix of nature, art and history.Villa Ada and Villa Borghese will open the doors to lush gardens and historic buildings, where you can breathe the atmosphere of a bygone era. And it doesn't end here: we will also take you to the heart of the Coppedè district, a hidden architectural jewel that will leave you breathless. Prepare to be breathless as you immerse yourself in styles that blend together and create a surreal atmosphere.Hop on your bike and get ready to live an unforgettable experience: a guided tour that will allow you to discover Rome in an original and authentic way. Discover hidden corners, admire masterpieces of art, breathe in the lush nature of the villas and be enchanted by the beauty of these places loved by the Romans.Don't miss the opportunity to experience a different Rome! Book your tour now and prepare to create unforgettable memoriesDo you want an even more authentic and personalized experience? Book the “Private Tour” option. You will have the local guide exclusively for you!

data.name: Viva Vivaldi: The Four Seasons in Piazza Navona
data.description: Experience Vivaldi's masterpiece in an arrangement for piano quintet in Borromini's Sacristy of the St. Agnes in Agone Church, a Baroque jewel at Piazza Navona. Entrance at via di santa Maria dell'Anima 30 a. We recommend that you arrive 30 minutes before the beginning of the concert.

data.name: Rome Private Tour with Certified Guide and Must-See Spots
data.description: Discover Rome with this private walking tour, guided by a certified expert. Explore iconic landmarks like the Colosseum, Vatican City, and the Pantheon, or customize your itinerary to include your must-see spots. Stroll through Trastevere, admire Piazza Navona, and indulge in authentic Roman gelato along the way for an unforgettable experience in the Eternal City.

data.name: Semi-Private Vatican Tour with Sistine Chapel and St. Peter’s Basilica
data.description: Vatican crowds and long ticket lines can eat up your day and drain the experience. Skip the wait and explore the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with just 10 guests per group. This semi-private tour offers a more personal experience with a dedicated guide, plus direct entry to St. Peter’s Basilica through the Scala Regia. You’ll end in the basilica, free to explore until you’re ready to take on the rest of Rome.Tour OverviewYou’ll meet your local guide at the top of the stairs near Caffé Vaticano, just across from the Vatican Museums entrance. With skip-the-line access, you’ll head straight inside to explore the treasures of the Vatican without the usual crowds. Your expert guide will lead you through highlights like the Raphael Rooms, Borgia Apartments, and more, sharing the stories behind the art. After your time in the Sistine Chapel, you’ll enter St. Peter’s Basilica through the Scala Regia, where your tour concludes inside one of the most revered churches in the world.Semi-Private Vatican Tour with Sistine Chapel and St. Peter’s Basilica DescriptionYour 3-hour semi-private tour includes:Charismatic, English-speaking guideSkip-the-line Vatican MuseumsPio-ClementinoGalleries, tapestries, maps & moreRaphael Rooms & School of AthensSistine ChapelEnter Scala Regia passagewayMax group size 10Please note that the Basilica is closed on Wednesday mornings due to the Papal Audience and will not be included in tours. Afternoon tours will still include St. Peter's Basilica entry.Pio-Clementino Museum and Nero’s BathtubYour guide will take you to the Pio-Clementino Museum where you'll see three of the most iconic statues in the world. Learn about the myths and legends associated with the Apollo Belvedere, Laocoön and His Sons, and the Belvedere Torso. You'll also visit one of the biggest and oldest bathtubs you'll ever see, made from rare red marble for Emperor Nero to relax in.The Best Galleries at the VaticanYour guide will lead you on through the Vatican Museums, visiting the Candelabra Gallery, Gallery of the Tapestries, and Gallery of Maps. Admire the ancient Roman and Greek statues, the Flemish tapestries created by Raphael's students, and the gorgeous topographical depictions of Italy.At the height of the Roman Empire, pontiffs rarely left Rome. In order to understand the Italian peninsula without endangering his life, Pope Gregory XIII commissioned 40 giant, meticulous maps to be created for his use. Most of these maps measure more than 15 by 16 feet, and the end result is nothing short of spectacular.You'll hear the stories behind these treasures from your expert guide as the Vatican secrets are slowly unveiled to you.Raphael Rooms and The School of AthensRaphael is the epitome of a Renaissance artist. In the period of European civilization immediately following the Middle Ages, a great period of revival in art, literature, and thought occurred. Raphael encompassed the ideals of a Renaissance man and frescoed multiple rooms inside of the Vatican Museums. Among other masterpieces, see one of Raphael’s most famous works of art, The School of Athens.Michelangelo’s Sistine ChapelNo visit to Vatican City is complete without stepping inside the Sistine Chapel. Since speaking is not allowed in this sacred space, your guide will explain the most important details beforehand and provide a helpful reference guide to take in with you.Once inside, the magnitude of Michelangelo’s masterpiece becomes clear. In just four years, he painted over 600 figures across the ceiling and altar wall—scenes from Genesis, prophets, sibyls, and the powerful Last Judgment. The Sistine Chapel is not only a breathtaking artistic achievement, but also the place where cardinals gather to elect a new pope, deepening its spiritual and cultural significance.Please remember that the Sistine Chapel is an active place of worship. Both men and women must cover their knees and shoulders to be granted entry. Rome’s summers can be hot, so we recommend bringing a lightweight shawl or sweater to cover up when needed.Ending Inside St. Peter’s BasilicaAfter your visit to the Sistine Chapel, you’ll follow your guide down the Scala Regia, Bernini’s magnificent ceremonial staircase once used by popes and dignitaries. This route is not open to the general public—only guided groups have access.You’ll step directly into St. Peter’s Basilica, one of the most awe-inspiring churches in the world. Inside, marvel at Michelangelo’s Pietà, gaze up into the dome, and stand beneath Bernini’s bronze Baldachin at the high altar. From here, your guided tour ends, and you are free to explore the basilica at your own pace. Whether you choose to linger longer in the quiet majesty or step back into the streets of Rome, the rest of the day is yours to enjoy.

data.name: The Great Opera Arias Concert at Palazzo Poli
data.description: With a program featuring the great Tosca, Rigoletto, La Traviata and Turandot by Boccherini, Vivaldi, Verdi, Marcello, Puccini, Rossini, Mascagni, Leoncavallo and de Curtis, this opera concert at Rome's beloved Palazzo Poli is sure to set you to return for more. Palazzo Poli is an important sixteenth century palace located in the heart of Rome: It is the palace of the famous Trevi Fountain. The Sala Dante, with its very high ceiling, has excellent acoustics and offers a view of the fountain itself from three balconies accessible to spectators!

data.name: Full-day tour to Florence and Pisa from Rome
data.description: The first stop will be Pisa. Upon arrival, you will go to Piazza dei Miracoli, declared a World Heritage Site and where the Pisan Romanesque-style cathedral is located. In this same square, you will have the opportunity to take the famous photo next to the Leaning Tower of Pisa. After taking the famous picture of the Leaning Tower, you will return to the bus to go to Florence. During the Middle Ages, Florence was an important cultural, economic, and financial center and its streets originated in the second half of the fourteenth century, the Renaissance. The city is replete with history, art, philosophy, and science and there are samples of it in every corner. The tourist leader will take you to a point in the city center and you will have time to make your itinerary and enjoy a city full of curiosities and interesting facts that will allow you to admire Piazza del Duomo, Mercato Nuovo, Piazza della Repubblica or Palazzo Strozzi. You can walk over the Vecchio Bridge and from there reach the Palazzo Vecchio. You will have time to eat on your own and taste the typical Panzanella or Panino col lampredotto.Around 17:30h we will head back to Rome.

data.name: Rome: Limoncello Making Class + Tasting + Pickup
data.shortDescription: Peel lemons and bottle your own limoncello
data.description:
Learn how to make limoncello in Rome. Visit one of the city's artisanal distilleries for a hands-on class. Follow traditional steps from peeling fresh lemons to bottling your own batch. 

Start with an introduction to the process. Get involved in zesting organic lemons, mixing them with alcohol and sugar, and infusing the flavors.

While the limoncello rests, have a tasting session in the private tasting room. Sample Spritz Drink It® with Roman pizza. At the end of the class, bottle a 100-ml creation to take home as a reminder of your trip.

data.name: Day trip to Bologna from Rome
data.description: Bologna is home to the oldest university in the Western world, and is known for its lavish porticoed walkways and squares, its fascinating medieval center and its bustling night life. Bologna is also one of Italian food capitals: great pasta such as tagliatelle, lasagne, tortellini as well as delicacies such as Parmesan Cheese, Balsamic Vinegar and some of the finest cured meats in Italy hail from Bologna and the surrounding Emilia Romagna region. All this makes Bologna a perfect off the beaten path destination for the savvy traveler. Wandering under the ancient porticoes and discovering  architectural masterpieces from a long forgotten past (while tasting from time to time local amazing delicacies) could be one of your Italian trip major delights! You will leave Rome in the early morning when our driver will pick up you at your accommodation and you will be back there in the same evening! An expert local guide will stay with you all the time to show all the secrets of this beautiful little treasure in the middle of our country.

data.name: Galleria Borghese: visita guidata in italiano
data.shortDescription:
La Galleria Borghese è tra le gallerie d'arte più famose a Roma. Questo plesso museale ospita una parte consistente della Collezione Borghese di dipinti, sculture e antichità, iniziata dal cardinale Scipione Borghese, nipote di Papa Paolo V e avido collezionista di opere di Caravaggio, che è ben rappresentato nella collezione con il Ragazzo con canestro di frutta, il San Girolamo che scrive, il Bacco malato e altri.

Nota di merito per il meraviglioso Salone: questo, infatti, presenta un grande affresco sul soffitto della prima sala, opera dell'artista siciliano Mariano Rossi, che fa un così buon uso dello scorcio da sembrare quasi tridimensionale. L'affresco raffigura Marco Furio Camillo che allevia l'assedio del Campidoglio da parte dei Galli.

La prima sala del Salone è la Camera di Cerere, con un vaso di marmo raffigurante Edipo e la Sfinge. La seconda sala ha un soffitto affrescato da Francesco Caccianiga con la Caduta di Fetonte. La terza sala ospita l'Apollo e Dafne del Bernini.

Proprio le opere di Gian Lorenzo Bernini, costituiscono una percentuale significativa della sua produzione di scultura profana, a partire dalle prime opere come la Capra Amalthea con Giove bambino e Fauno (1615) e Enea, Anchise e Ascanio (1618-19) fino ai dinamici Ratto di Proserpina (1621-22), Apollo e Dafne (1622-25) e David (1623) , considerati opere seminali della scultura barocca. In Galleria Borghese sono presenti diversi busti-ritratto, tra cui quello di Papa Paolo V e due ritratti di uno dei suoi primi committenti, il cardinale Scipione Borghese (1632).

data.name: The Galleria Borghese Museum: tickets and guided tour in Spanish
data.shortDescription:
The Galleria Borghese is among the most famous art galleries in Rome. This museum complex houses a large part of the Borghese Collection of paintings, sculptures and antiquities, initiated by Cardinal Scipione Borghese, nephew of Pope Paul V and avid collector of works by Caravaggio, who is well represented in the collection with the Boy with Basket of Fruit, Saint Jerome Writing, Sick Bacchus and others.

Note of merit for the marvellous Salone: this, in fact, features a large fresco on the ceiling of the first room, the work of the Sicilian artist Mariano Rossi, who makes such good use of foreshortening that it seems almost three-dimensional. The fresco depicts Marcus Furius Camillus relieving the siege of the Capitol by the Gauls.

The first room of the Salon is the Chamber of Ceres, with a marble vase depicting Oedipus and the Sphinx. The second room has a ceiling frescoed by Francesco Caccianiga with the Fall of Phaeton. The third room houses Bernini's Apollo and Daphne.

It is precisely the works of Gian Lorenzo Bernini that make up a significant percentage of his production of secular sculpture, starting with early works such as the Goat Amalthea with Child Jupiter and Faun (1615) and Aeneas, Anchises and Ascanius (1618-19) up to the dynamic Rape of Proserpine (1621-22), Apollo and Daphne (1622-25) and David (1623) , considered seminal works of Baroque sculpture. In the Galleria Borghese there are several portrait busts, including one of Pope Paul V and two portraits of one of his first patrons, Cardinal Scipione Borghese (1632).

data.name: Rome: Express Pizza-Making Class
data.shortDescription: Learn all the secrets of preparing Italian pizza in one hour!
data.description:
Take part in a fun pizza-making workshop and enjoy an experience that encapsulates the entire tradition of Italian pizza. Just a few steps from the Vatican, you will learn the art of making and baking pizza from scratch, from maser pizza chefs.

Make and eat your own pizza while drinking Roman wine, with the assistance of a professional chef. Cook at your own work station and learn something new. No matter what your level of skill in the kitchen.

Once your hands-on experience has finished, sit down in a cozy restaurant or the outdoor terrace to enjoy the fruits of your labor. No cleanup!

Join our social table, sip wine with your new friends, take the opportunity to ask your Chef all the tips and tricks about Italian food and the best spot to be in Rome.

data.name: I Love Rome: Hop-on Hop-off Panoramic Bus Tour
data.description:
Soak in the sights and listen to an informative audio tour to learn about Rome's unique history and the stories behind its world famous monuments.

Discover the enchanting city of Rome with an authorized hop-on-hop-off route, approved by the Municipality of Rome to ensure the utmost decorum.

Experience the convenience of a strategically located bus stops, all within a comfortable walking distance from the captivating monuments and iconic points of interest that make Rome truly unforgettable.

data.name: Pompeii & Sorrento tour from Rome with Pickup
data.description: Tour duration: Approximately 12 hours. Embark on an unforgettable journey to Sorrento and Pompeii, blending breathtaking coastal beauty with ancient history. Depart from Rome and travel in comfort aboard an air-conditioned coach, passing through the stunning landscapes of the Amalfi Coast. Morning in Sorrento: Upon arrival, enjoy a limoncello tasting at a local producer and uncover the secrets behind this iconic Italian liqueur. Stroll through Sorrento’s charming streets, filled with artisan shops, colorful ceramics, and scenic coastal views. Afternoon in Pompeii: Continue to Pompeii, one of the world’s most extraordinary archaeological sites. Choose from two tour options: Guided Tour: Walk through perfectly preserved streets, temples, and villas with a professional archaeologist who will bring this ancient city back to life. Learn about the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD and how Pompeii remained frozen in time. Audioguide Tour: Enjoy self-paced exploration with a multilingual audioguide, offering detailed insights into Pompeii’s forum, bathhouses, and iconic frescoes. After your tour, relax on the return journey to Rome, arriving in the evening with unforgettable memories of Sorrento’s coastal charm and Pompeii’s timeless ruins

data.name: Rome Jewish Quarter and Trastevere Food Tour with Rooftop
data.description: Your experience begins in the old Jewish Quarter, one of Rome’s best neighborhoods for foodies. First, you’ll sample the famous Jewish-style fried artichokes, which you’ll eat standing up, in the traditional way. Then head to a local bakery to sample an unexpected and delicious sweet treat that represents the Jewish Quarter’s rich cultural heritage.After that, you'll make your way into the historic center (Centro Storico) where you'll pick up your next street food bite: freshly fried codfish from a beloved local hole-in-the-wall, washed down with a glass of wine.Next, at a hidden gem craft beer bar, delve into the world of Roman brewing with a tasting of locally crafted beers, each imbued with distinctive flavors and stories. You'll pair your beers with cold cuts and regional cheeses. Afterwards, you'll cross the Tiber River into Trastevere and indulge in a trapizzino, a delicious fusion between a sandwich and pizza.Finally, as the sun begins to set, you'll follow your guide to a private rooftop for a delightful finale: crafting your own Spritz against the backdrop of Rome's skyline. With panoramic views and a toast to good company, say "cin cin" to an unforgettable culinary journey through the Eternal City.

data.name: Rome: Pizza, Supplì & Gelato Masterclass + Unlimited Wine
data.shortDescription: Master the art of authentic Italian pizza, creamy gelato and Roman supplì
data.description:
Explore the art of crafting pizza, supplì, and gelato in a hands-on culinary class led by Italian chefs. 

Learn to make traditional pizzas, creamy gelato, and Roman supplì while enjoying bottomless wine to complete your Italian culinary experience.

data.name: Private Rome Evening Walking Tour
data.description: Maximus Tours is proud to offer the most beautiful Private Evening Walking Tour of the Eternal City. See the best of Rome through the eyes of a local, professional guide. Walk the romantic streets at your own pace, ask questions and get unexpected answers. You'll be strolling the city centre from Piazza Venezia to Piazza Navona, the Pantheon, Spanish Steps & finally throw a coin in the Trevi Fountain so you make sure you return. The tour also explores some of the smaller treasures which are off the beaten track and hard to find, but we'll keep these as a surprise. Don't wait until the last minute to book as spaces are limited.

data.name: Semi-private Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with Reserved Access and meeting point
data.description: Discover the masterpieces of Rome on this tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. You won't have to worry about waiting in long lines on this tour! We are here to ensure that you skip the lines and our expert guides will be there to give you an insider's point of view. The afternoon tour is the best option to visit the Museums without the morning crowd. The Vatican Museums No trip to Rome is complete without a visit to the Vatican Museums. Home to 54 different galleries including four statue museums: Museo Pio-Clementino, Museo Chiaramonti, Museo Gregoriano Etrusco and the Museo Gregoriano Egiziano. These museums are home to some of the most famous works of art in the world, with artists including: Leonardo Da Vinci, Michelangelo, Caravaggio, Raphael and Giotto, to name a few. An experience that is sure to inspire the art lover in anyone. The Sistine Chapel The 54th gallery of the Vatican Museums is the famed Sistine Chapel. Completed around 1483, the Sistine Chapel is arguably the most famous chapel in the world due to the artwork located within. View many of the most famous frescoes in the world, including the famous ceiling and "The Last Judgement" painted by Michelangelo. Not only does the Sistine Chapel hold some of the world's most precious works of art, it is still used for religious purposes such as the Papal conclave - the process through which a new Pope is chosen. St. Peter's Basilica A popular pilgrimage site, St. Peter's Basilica is also one of the largest in the world and a shining example of Renaissance architecture. Disclaimer: Please be aware that during the Jubilee Year, certain areas of the Vatican Museums may be inaccessible due to religious ceremonies. data.name: Oratorio Del Gonfalone: 'Italian Cello Masters'
data.description: Experience the magic of Italian cello mastery at the enchanting Oratorio del Gonfalone. 'Italian Cello Masters' is a mesmerizing event that promises to captivate audiences with its exquisite program. Set in the historic and acoustically splendid Oratorio del Gonfalone, this concert is a unique opportunity to savor the rich sounds of the cello in a breathtaking and intimate setting. The program features an enchanting selection of pieces that trace the diverse landscape of classical music. Highlights include Beethoven’s 7 Variazioni su Il Flauto Magico and Bach's Ciaccona, rendered for two cellos. The event will also showcase Locatelli's Sonata, I tempo, and Fauré's evocative Sicilienne e Papillon. This musical journey includes carefully chosen works like Brahms’s Scherzo dalla Sonata F.A.E., Paganini’s Variazioni dal Mose’, and concludes with Bach's Prelude from Suite No. 1, arranged by Gounod.

data.name: Shore excursion from Civitavecchia Port: the Castle of Santa Severa on the beach
data.description: Santa Severa is a frazione of the comune of Santa Marinella, in the provincia of Rome, Lazio. It is a small sea resort on the Via Aurelia c. 8 km (5 mi) south of Santa Marinella and 50 km (31 mi) north of Rome. It takes its name from the 2nd-century Christian martyr. The village includes a small medieval town with a 9th-century castle facing the sea, where the ancient Etruscan port of Pyrgi was once located. The Pyrgi tablets were found here in 1964.

data.description:

What makes this tour special?

• Immersive experience in the Colosseum: Relive the glory days of gladiators and the breathtaking shows that animated the Flavian Amphitheatre.

• Walk on the Palatine Hill: Explore the legendary hill where, according to tradition, Romulus founded Rome and where emperors built their sumptuous residences.

Walk to St. Mark’s Square, the heart and soul of Venice’s historical center. Then admire the magnificence of the western façade of the famous St. Mark's Basilica. See the best of the city and finish your day with a typical aperitivo, or cicchetto, as the locals call it. data.name: Underground Rome: Private Catacombs Half-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the underground world of ancient Rome on this exciting, fascinating, and adventurous tour of the Catacombs and the excavated site of Basilica San Clemente. On your private half-day tour you will:  Travel between sites in the comfort of an air-conditioned private vehicle; Explore the hidden underground of ancient Roman burial sites, streets, houses, and temples with an expert private guide; Feel like Indiana Jones or Lara croft as you explore the awe-inspiring subterranean burial chambers and miles of labyrinthine galleries at the Rome Catacombs; Descend below the unique 12th-century basilica of San Clemente and see the archaeological lasagna that is Rome; Walk around a 4th-century church with original 9th-century frescos offering us a glimpse into a long-lost world;  Step down into a mysterious 2nd-century pagan temple to Mithras, and learn about this secretive warrior cult; Walk in the footsteps of the ancient Romans in a 1st-century subterranean Roman house... where one more surprise awaits! Drive just beyond the ancient city walls to visit the labyrinth of underground ancient Christian burial chambers called the Catacombs, then discover the layers and layers of Rome, excavated below the Basilica San Clemente (near the Colosseum): walk through a pagan temple, an ancient roman house, and an early Christian church - all underground! You will often hear historians and locals alike refer to Rome as a lasagna! On this tour, you will literally walk your way through these layers of history, as you discover the different excavated street levels of Rome and the miles and miles of underground graves, dug for and by the ancient Christians two thousand years ago known as the Catacombs. Driving just beyond the Aurelian Wall, you’ll descend into an extensive and complex web of graves; the Christian catacombs. You’ll walk down galleries lined with rectangular empty niches – each one contained a body once. Your guide will explain the different styles of graves, the burial rituals, and funeral rites, decode the extraordinarily well-preserved frescos and symbolic carvings and talk you through the dramatic sacking of the tombs by Barbarians after the fall of Rome. One of the most evocative things about the catacombs is seeing the pick axe marks and scrapes of the fossari (the gravediggers) in the soft tufa rock and the tiny terracotta oil lamps that lit their way as they dug these dark tunnels. It is a truly fascinating, exciting, and humbling experience entering these unique places with your private guide. In the Basilica San Clemente, you’ll learn why Rome was built layer on layer, not in a day but over several hundred years. You’ll learn why so many Christian churches were built on top of pagan temples and hear the stories of the martyrs depicted in frescos in the Middle Ages. Your guide will talk you through a day in the life of an ancient Roman as you walk through a first-century apartment, and explain the initiation rites of the warrior-like cult of Mithras as you gaze into the inner sanctum and see the original altar of Mithras and the bull. This tour ends at the Basilica of San Clemente, located right next to the Roman Colosseum. Please note: the dress code for this tour must be observed (covered knees and shoulders). The catacombs and excavations are chilly and humid at 13 Celsius, so please bring something warm to wear! Also, due to local regulations, during the visit to the Catacombs, you will be part of a larger group. For the rest of the tour, you will be alone with your dedicated private guide. During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: Rome: Tour of the Roman Forum, Trevi Fountain, Pantheon and more
data.description:
Get ready for an unforgettable journey through the Eternal City with our carefully designed tour! We'll start at the iconic Roman Forum, the beating heart of ancient Rome, where you'll tour the ruins of temples, arches and basilicas that tell stories of power, culture and religion. There you will learn about the daily life of the Romans and the historical events that shaped the Western world.

The tour continues through the charming streets of the historic center, where every corner has something special to offer, with its baroque fountains and vibrant atmosphere, and the majestic Pantheon, a 2,000-year-old temple that is a testament to Roman engineering.

Then, we will walk to the magical Trevi Fountain, a place full of charm and traditions. You'll have the chance to toss a coin into the water to make sure you'll return to Rome someday. While there, you will admire the delicacy of the sculptural details and hear stories about its construction and cultural significance.

data.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel Group Tour
data.description:
Visiting the Vatican Museums is a journey through one of the holiest sites in Christianity. Explore a magnificent collection curated by the Popes, featuring classic sculptures and timeless masterpieces.

Discover works by Raphael, Giotto, and Caravaggio in the Pio Clementino Museum, the Gallery of the Candelabras, the Gallery of the Geographical Maps, the Gallery of the Tapestries, the Raphael Rooms, and the Sistine Chapel.

Marvel at Michelangelo’s breathtaking ceiling and the Last Judgment fresco in the Sistine Chapel. Visit St. Peter’s Basilica, the most famous Catholic church in the world. During spring and summer, stroll through the beautiful Vatican Gardens in full bloom.

By visiting Vatican City, the smallest country in the world and the center of Christian Rome, you'll understand why it is one of the most significant places in human history. Experience the rich heritage and profound spirituality of this iconic destination.

data.name: Vatican at Closing Time with Sistine Chapel
data.description: Exploring the Vatican Museums in the evening alone means missing expert insights, hidden details, and the most immersive way to experience its masterpieces. Skip the lines and let an engaging, passionate guide bring the art to life as you admire Raphael’s School of Athens, the ancient sculpture of Laocoön and His Sons, and Michelangelo’s breathtaking Sistine Chapel frescoes. With fewer crowds and a captivating storyteller leading the way, see the Vatican’s treasures in their most magical settingTour OverviewDon't miss out on this unusual opportunity to explore the Vatican in the early evening when other tourists have gone back into Rome. Your local guide will lead you from the top of the steps at Caffe Vaticano into the Vatican Museums. Their passionate knowledge will bring the art and architecture to life as you explore the Sistine Chapel, the Raphael Rooms, and other areas. This small group tour is ideal for anyone who enjoys adventuring in the evening hours when attractions are less busy.Vatican and Sistine Chapel Night Tour DescriptionYour 2-hour tour includes:A quieter experience with fewer peopleA guided tour of the Vatican Museums and GalleriesRaphael Rooms and School of AthensFree time to explore on your ownAn expert English-speaking guideMaximum group size of 20Evening Tour of the VaticanTake an art history journey with your expert Vatican guide as you walk through the rooms of the most fascinating museums on earth. You'll see works of art in the Pinecone Courtyard and get a great view of St. Peter's Basilica in the evening light, before stepping inside to see some of the world-famous masterpieces kept safely within the Vatican walls.Pio-Clementino Museum and Nero’s BathtubYour tour begins with a visit to the Pio-Clementino Museum, where you'll see three of the most iconic statues in the world. Learn about the myths and legends associated with the Apollo Belvedere, Laocoön and His Sons, and the Belvedere Torso. You'll also visit one of the biggest and oldest bathtubs you'll ever see!Vatican GalleriesEntering in the afternoon after the majority of the crowds have left, you'll follow your guide through the Candelabra Gallery, Gallery of the Tapestries and Gallery of Maps. Admire the ancient Roman and Greek statues, the Flemish tapestries created by Raphael's students, and the gorgeous topographical depictions of Italy. You'll hear the stories behind these treasures from your expert guide as the Vatican secrets are slowly unveiled to you.Raphael RoomsNext on this unforgettable walking tour are the Raphael Rooms. These four galleries are dedicated to one of the true masters of the Renaissance, and you'll find his most famous painting School of Athens displayed here. Take in the stunning frescoes and hear how Pope Julius II commissioned the art, as well as the complex techniques used to create them.The Sistine Chapel at NightYour guided evening Vatican tour concludes in Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel, where the ceiling and the altar wall are adorned by world-famous and inspiring frescoes. Only when you enter the Sistine Chapel is it clear how high the ceiling is and how many paintings are up there. At this point, it is impossible not to appreciate how difficult is must have been for Michelangelo to lay on his back and toil at his masterpiece, year after year.The Sistine Chapel is a place of worship, so visitors are not allowed to speak inside the chapel. Your guide will explain what you'll see in advance and provide you with a map or handout for reference before you enter. Men and women must cover their knees and shoulders before entering, so it's recommended to bring a shawl, scarf, or sweater you can quickly put on.Take Your Time and Explore the CollectionsDepending on your tour time, feel free to explore more of the Vatican on your own after your tour finishes. You can revisit your favorite works of art or simply wander around to enjoy the incredibly peaceful atmosphere of the museums without the daytime crowds.

Focus on the most important masterpieces in the massive museum to cover the galleries without getting overwhelmed, and end with time to marvel at Michelangelo’s frescoes inside the Sistine Chapel.

data.name: Aperitif and Skip-the-Line Ticket for the Vatican Museums
data.description: Enjoy the skip-the-line ticket for the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel combined with a delicious aperitif in the beautiful setting of the Pinecone Courtyard.The Vatican Museums are one of the most prestigious and fascinating cultural destinations in the world. The collections gathered over the years by successive popes offer a unique journey through centuries of art, history and spirituality. Inside the Vatican Museums you can admire works of art by some of the greatest masters in history: the frescoes of the Sistine Chapel, created by the genius of Michelangelo, Raphael Rooms, the Gallery of Maps, the Pio Clementino Museum, the Gregorian Egyptian Museum, the Gregorian Etruscan Museum, the Chiaramonti Museum and the Pinacoteca containing works by artists such as Raphael, Leonardo da Vinci, Giotto and Perugino, just to give some example.Complete your experience with a delicious aperitif at the Pinecone Courtyard. Your aperitif includes: 1 cocktail or soft drinks, still or sparking water, red pizzette, selection of cheeses and cold cuts, Capressin finger, Porchetta di Ariccia with homemade bread, rice, potato croquettes, cous cous à la Méditerranée.Don't miss to admire the other important sculpture in the courtyard: the "Sphere Within Sphere” by Italian sculptor Arnaldo Pomodoro, donated to the Vatican Museums in 1990. Pomodoro’s circular sphere has a mechanism inside that slowly rotates with the wind.

data.name: Rome Colosseum, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill Small-Group Tour
data.description: Avoid the hassle of keeping up with a large group and instead explore Rome’s top ancient sites with a small group on this intimate Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill tour. Head inside the ancient amphitheater with your guide to admire its arena and tiers of seats. Then stroll through the ruins of the Roman Forum and admire the views from the scenic overlook at the top of Palatine Hill.

data.name: Private Tour Colosseum, Palatine Hill and Roman Forum
data.description: Get an in-depth introduction to three of Rome’s most iconic ancient attractions during this private two-hour tour of the Colosseum, the Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Explore each millennia-old archaeological site with a private guide. Learn about the daily lives of imperial Romans, with plenty of time to ask questions.

data.name: Saint Clement’s Basilica and Roman Houses on Celio Hill Tour
data.description: Uncover what lies underneath Rome on this private tour. Enjoy an itinerary exploring what's at street level and below Saint Clement’s Basilica, as well as the archeological remains of Case Romane del Celio. Perfect for ancient history buffs, as well as visitors looking for a history tour with a unique focus.

data.name: Chopin & Italian Friends Concerts with Traditional Italian Dinner
data.description: Experience an exceptional evening of piano classics at the impressive Chiesa Evangelica Valdese in Rome, featuring masterpieces by renowned composers such as George Gershwin, Giuseppe Verdi, Frederic Chopin, Giacomo Puccini, Claude Debussy, and Pietro Mascagni. The piano concerts are dedicated to the celebrated Polish composer, Fryderyk Chopin, whose compositions resonate in concert halls worldwide. The pianist will showcase his most famous works during the solo performance, including Impromptu Fantaisie, Preludes, and Scherzo No. 2. Despite only visiting Italy once in Genoa, Chopin's exposure to Italian music and culture in Warsaw influenced his compositions. Alongside Chopin's works, the audience will also enjoy unique arrangements of Italian compositions by composers like G. Verdi, P. Mascagni, and G. Puccini. The exceptional venue of the Waldensian Church in Rome, renowned for its superb acoustics and architectural beauty, further elevates the concert experience. Don't miss this unique opportunity to revel in a piano concert within the grandeur of a church setting. Following the performance, attendees are cordially invited to enjoy a traditional Italian dinner at the nearby Enoteca restaurant, creating a perfect end to the unforgettable evening.

data.name: Rome: Borghese Gallery Small Group Tour
data.description: Explore the 17th century home of Cardinal Borghese and discover the stories behind his private art collection during a small group tour of the gallery. Admire masterpieces such as Raphael's ‘Deposition,’ and works by Bernini, Borromini, Caravaggio, and more. Witness the evolution of art through the decades as you discover works from the Roman, baroque and renaissance periods, and learn more about the history behind them.

data.name: Rome Two-Day Tour with Colosseum, Trevi Fountain, and Vatican
data.description: Rome is a treasure trove of world-class art and archaeology. With this two-day tour, check off the city's top sights without the hassle of following a map or guidebook. Stroll through the historic center on the first day to admire iconic landmarks like the Colosseum and Trevi Fountain. On the second day, cross the Tiber River to visit Vatican City, including the Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica.

data.name: Outside Colosseum virtual reality experience with audio guide
data.description: Experience the Colosseum in all its past splendour on this virtual reality tour, complete with an audio guide.Using 3D glasses, delve into interactive reconstructions of the arena, the square surrounding the Colosseum, and the subterranean chambers.Wander around the monument's exterior while listening to enlightening commentary from one of the city's leading academic libraries, and watch as ancient Rome unfolds before your eyes.

data.name: Colosseum, Forum, Palatine Hill Tour
data.description: A visit to the Colosseum is a must-do for first-time, or even repeat, visitors to Rome. Embark on a group tour of the iconic arena as well as the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill in just a few hours. See the amphitheater where the gladiators once fought, learn about its construction, and hear stories about life in ancient Rome from a guide. Booking this tour means you don't have to worry about getting around this large and crowded site independently.

data.name: Skip-the-line Villa Farnesina Raphael Paintings & Trastevere Guided Tour in Rome
data.description: Rome has more to explore than the Vatican or Colosseum, but many travelers don’t know where to start. Discover one of the Eternal City’s most spectacular Renaissance villas on this guided tour that takes in Villa Farnesina and the cobblestoned lanes of the surrounding Trastevere district. See sumptuous works by Raphael and other artists, with skip-the-line admission tickets included.

data.name: Rome Skip-the-Line Religious Sites Private Tour with Catacombs
data.description: Explore some of Rome’s most important religious sites on this private, skip-the-line tour of the Catacombs, the four major basilicas, Vatican Museums, and the Sistine Chapel. Spend the day immersed in centuries of religious history, hear stirring stories of faith, and walk in the footsteps of popes, pilgrims, and artists who dedicated their lives to the Church.

data.name: E-Bike Tour to the Appian Way,  the Aqueduct Park and the Catacombs
data.description: Just outside the historic centre, about 3km from the Colosseum, there is a place you absolutely must visit! Getting there can be a challenge, but you are an explorer!, and the undertaking is absolutely worth it!! Do you want to cycle safely, away from city traffic? Discover the Via Appia Antica, starting directly from the section closed to car traffic, and unleash your desire for adventure! This itinerary unites the present of the golden fields of the Roman countryside still frequented by local shepherds, with the glorious past of the Monumental Tombs and ruins of ancient Rome which stand on the sides of the road and are witnesses of an era in which death was celebrated with grandeur. Every kilometre travelled is a dive into history, which brings you ever closer to the peace and tranquillity you will find in the Aqueduct Park. Here the arches of the imposing aqueducts draw elegant profiles in the sky and tell of the cutting-edge engineering feats of the ancient Romans. In the shade of the centenary trees, enjoy the stories told by your guide, the enchanting landscape will do the rest. The visit to the Catacombs will be an unmissable stop to give a touch of mystery to this bike adventure. In the depths of the earth, among these labyrinths dug into the tuff, let yourself be enveloped by the mystical atmosphere you will breathe. Do you want an even more authentic and personalized experience? Book the “Private Tour” option. You will have the local guide exclusively for you!

data.name: Rome: Authentic Roman Pizza Making Class and Dinner
data.description: Authentic Roman pizza making class and dinner Learn how to make sensational, authentic Roman pizza from scratch! Make a few different pizzas and a dessert, then sit down to enjoy your dinner with the chef. Cook and enjoy a variety of pizzas from scratch like Margherita, Napoletana, and Marinara, as well as a dessert Wine and beer are included Very close to the Almone river in Rome Communal cooking class and dining for 2 to 6 people Sandra is a chef who started giving cooking lessons 7 years ago About your host, Sandra: Having grown up in northern Tuscany, I spent several years in Milan and now live in Rome. I have a broad knowledge of the country's many and varied wonderful dishes. I started cooking when I was little with my parents, and I've worked in restaurants and villas in Tuscany. Eatwith is the world's largest community for culinary experiences with locals. Savor local food and enjoy dinner parties, cooking classes and more in beautiful homes and exclusive venues. STARTER Fried panzerotti stuffed with tomatoes, salame piccante and cheese. PIZZA The basic ingredients of la pizza napoletana are as follows: tender wheat organic flour (which renders the dough soft and sweet!), organic peeled Roma tomatoes, extra virgin olive oil, garlic, basil and mozzarella di bufala D.O.P… The dough has to be soft and the ingredients very fresh. We will make a few different pizzas that we can dress with various toppings (prosciutto, vegetables, different cheeses) DESSERT Tiramisu', panna cotta with chocolate or different flavours of homemade gelato

data.name: Semi-private Tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with Pick-up
data.description: Tour duration: 3 hours Embark on a transformative journey through the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter’s Basilica, where the nexus of art, history, and spirituality offers an unparalleled experience. This exclusive small-group tour grants you a privileged pathway into the heart of Vatican City, bypassing the ubiquitous crowds with reserved access that leads you directly into a realm of artistic and historical magnificence. Your adventure begins at the Vatican Museums, a treasure trove of art spanning several millennia. With over 54 galleries, including the Museo Pio Clementino, Museo Chiaramonti, Museo Gregoriano Etrusco, and Museo Gregoriano-Egizio, the Vatican Museums house a staggering collection of works. Under the guidance of an expert, delve into the stories behind the ancient statues, ethereal paintings, and intricate tapestries that define the collections. Each hall and gallery unfolds like a book, narrating the tale of human creativity across ages. A highlight of your tour is the Sistine Chapel, an iconic symbol of the Renaissance’s artistic achievement. Stand beneath Michelangelo’s The Last Judgment and the mesmerizing ceiling frescoes, where biblical stories are brought to life with unprecedented vigour and emotion. This sacred space, where popes are elected, resonates with the genius of Michelangelo, enveloping you in a sense of awe and wonder. Journey through the Raphael Rooms, where the Renaissance master Raphael Sanzio da Urbino adorned the walls with some of the most sublime frescoes in the world. Your guide will reveal the intricate details and hidden narratives within these works, including the famous School of Athens, showcasing Raphael’s ability to merge classical philosophy with High Renaissance artistry. The tour affords a special privilege rarely extended to the general public - a direct passage from the Sistine Chapel to St. Peter’s Basilica. This exclusive route allows you to transition seamlessly from the artistic to the spiritual heart of Vatican City. Inside St. Peter’s, you will encounter the pinnacle of Renaissance architecture. Marvel at Michelangelo’s Pietà, Bernini’s Baldachin, and the awe-inspiring dome, each element a testament to the basilica’s enduring beauty and significance. As you traverse the sacred spaces and galleries, your guide will provide insights into the Vatican’s pivotal role in history, the intricate processes of art creation, and the stories of ambition, faith, and power that shaped these masterpieces. This tour not only highlights the artistic achievements of legendary figures such as Leonardo da Vinci, Caravaggio, Giotto, Raphael, and Michelangelo but also offers a window into the cultural and spiritual narratives that have influenced humanity throughout the centuries. Embark on this exclusive tour to discover the wonders of the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter’s Basilica in a truly immersive way. Book now to secure your place on this unforgettable journey through art, history, and spirituality, ensuring memories that will last a lifetime. Disclaimer: Please be aware that during the Jubilee Year, certain areas of the Vatican Museums may be inaccessible due to religious ceremonies. Additionally, entrance to St. Peter's Basilica may also experience unannounced closures. These circumstances are beyond our control. Thank you for your understanding

data.name: Pasta and Tiramisu Cookery Workshop in Rome

A glass of wine, a Limoncello, and a cup of coffee are included in your workshop.

data.name: Churches of Rome: A Tour of Sacred Beauty
data.description:
Rome is deeply intertwined with Catholic faith and history, home to over 900 churches. While it’s impossible to visit them all, our walking tour is the perfect way to start uncovering these stunning treasures.

Join us on a relaxed yet immersive walking tour where you’ll discover some of Rome’s most beautiful churches that many visitors miss. You’ll explore Church of St. Louis of the French, home to priceless Caravaggio masterpieces, and Chiesa di Sant'Agnese in Agone, a gem of Baroque architecture.

From the stunning dome of Chiesa di Sant'Ignazio di Loyola to the awe-inspiring Basilica di Sant'Andrea della Valle, this tour takes you beyond the typical landmarks. You’ll also visit the charming Chiesa di Santa Maria di Loreto, nestled in the heart of Rome.

Your professional guide will reveal how these churches played a vital role in shaping Rome's art, culture, religion, and architecture. Plus, enjoy a relaxing stop for an authentic Italian coffee to soak in the atmosphere of Rome.

data.name: Rome food tour in Trastevere
data.description: There’s a saying among foodies; to truly understand people and places, we need to take a good look inside their kitchens! This food tour of Trastevere does exactly that. Expect insider access to Trastevere’s best restaurants, bars, flavors and recipes. Oh, and the best food Rome has to offer.The food tour takes place in the city's most vibrant neighborhood: Trastevere. The area is renowned for its buzzing nightlife and fantastic eateries with delightful aromas spilling out of them. However, it’s also known to have its fair share of tourist traps! The team of expert foodies invites you, and your tastebuds, to try some of the finest flavours in the city! Vacations are too short to eat bad food, right?During the experience, you will try around 11 different Roman dishes and some of the finest local wines. However, this experience is more than just simply trying different local foods and getting tipsy… This is a delicious journey inside the Roman kitchen, the delicacies, the diet, the dos and don’ts, and the culinary traditions. Not only will you experience the mouthwatering flavors of Rome, but you’ll also discover the process, meet the makers, and truly understand why Roman Cuisine is considered one of the best in the world.

data.name: Colosseum Underground Guided Tour
data.description: See a side of the Colosseum that most visitors to Rome miss—and enjoy a stress-free way to discover the world-renowned landmark—with this convenient tour option. Meet your guide at the Colosseum entrance, and head on in. You’ll visit underground areas normally off-limits to visitors and will learn all about the Colosseum’s history, before continuing to the Forum and Palatine Hill.

data.name: Colosseum Guided Tour Small Group
data.description: What sets our tour apart is the perfect balance of expert storytelling, exclusive access, and a small-group experience that brings ancient Rome vividly to life. Led by licensed guides with deep historical knowledge, you’ll explore the Colosseum from a panoramic viewpoint, walk in the footsteps of emperors on Palatine Hill, and uncover hidden gems in the Roman Forum. We don’t just visit monuments—we unlock their stories. With pre-arranged access as part of a fully approved experience package, you’ll enjoy a seamless, immersive journey through Rome’s most iconic landmarks. Our tours are designed for curious minds and passionate travelers—expect in-depth insights, interactive commentary, and real connections to the past. Whether you’re a history lover or simply seeking the best way to experience ancient Rome, this tour delivers unforgettable value.

data.name: Rome Small-Group Sightseeing Tour by Vintage Vespa
data.description: When in Rome, travel like a Roman aboard a vintage Vespa on this small-group sightseeing tour. Hop aboard your classic scooter and follow your guide on a scenic route around the Aurelian Walls, along the Tiber riverfront, and out to explore the ancient ruins of the Appian Way and the idyllic Orange Garden of Aventine Hill.

data.name: Rome by Night Small-Group Walking Tour
data.description: Experience Rome after the peak midday crowds and heat with this uniquely picturesque walking tour that takes in the city's top monuments after sunset. Admire highlights of the Eternal City such as the Pantheon, Piazza Navona, and Bernini's spectacular fountains under the stars, plus learn about the history of the ancient Roman empire as you enjoy the vibrant energy of the city at night.

data.name: Private Walking Tour of Roman Squares and Fountains Plus the Pantheon
data.description: This private tour is a perfect introduction to those visiting Rome for the first time. It includes the three most important and monumental squares: Piazza di Spagna, the Trevi Fountain, the Pantheon and Piazza Navona. This 3 hour walking tour will give you the sensation of walking inside the Dolce Vita Roman's charming atmosphere, discovering its beautiful baroque fountains, its romantic cafes and living the authentic Italian style. Hotel pick-up and drop-off will be provided, with two start times available (10am or 2pm).

data.name: Rome Ancient Ruins and Domus TIberiana Small-Group Guided Tour
data.description: Step back in time to the era of the ancient Romans on this small-group guided tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, learning about daily life within one of Europe’s most prominent ancient civilizations. After you’ve finished exploring the ruins, visit the Domus Tiberiana, the former residence of Emperor Tiberius and the Julio-Claudian dynasty, to hear how Rome was ruled.

data.name: Rome: Vatican City for Kids Private Tour With Pickup
data.description: The Vatican Museums can feel a bit overwhelming for little ones, but this kids-focused tour gets the whole family involved. Enjoy priority admission to all of the exhibits to skip waiting in long lines. Plus, learn about what you're seeing through a series of trivia questions, quizzes, and even a scavenger hunt. Explore multiple galleries, the Raphael Rooms, the Sistine Chapel, and more.

data.name: Rome Colosseum and Palatine Hill Guided Group Tour
data.description: The Colosseum is one of Rome’s A-list sights, but you won’t learn all about its history by going alone. Get more out of your visit by taking an informative 1-hour guided tour. Learn about its history and design and hear tales of gladiatorial battles. Next, continue your exploration of ancient Rome at Palatine Hill. This is a great combined introduction to two of Rome’s must-visit attractions.

data.name: Oratorio Del Gonfalone: Love of a poet
data.description: Nestled in the heart of Rome, the enchanting Oratorio del Gonfalone presents an evening of musical romance with 'Amor di poeta'. This captivating event invites visitors to explore the emotive depth of love through the profound compositions of Robert Schumann's Dichterliebe op. 48. The venue, renowned for its stunning Renaissance frescoes, offers a fitting backdrop for this evocative performance, where the power of poetry and music intertwine. 'Amor di poeta' is a concert scene that interweaves music and words in a theatrical approach. The performance explores Robert Schumann's Dichterliebe (Poet's Love), a cycle of Lieder celebrating love, hope, sorrow and death, on texts by Heinrich Heine. Through the figure of the translator, musician and playwright, the scene offers multiple levels of interpretation, engaging the audience in an experience that goes beyond the musical performance, creating a deep connection between Romantic music and reflection on its interpretation.

data.name: Rome: Colosseum, Roman Forum Ticket with Audio Guide

data.name: The unconventional Ancient Rome
data.shortDescription:
The Unconventional Ancient Rome and Colosseum Private Tour allows you to explore the best of Ancient Rome.

We will visit the Colosseum in a completely new way, walking right on the arena where gladiators fought.

We will walk on the Palatine Hill and see the House of Augustus, the Horti Farnesorum, the gardens of the Pope built on top of the ruins of imperial palaces and, last but not list, the ruins of the Tiberio Palace, reopened after 50 years of restorations.

We will visit the entire Roman Forum, with the Church of Sant Maria Antiqua, the Rampa Domitianae and the Temple of Julius Caesar.

We will end by taking a real walk in the Imperial Forums!

The itinerary and duration of your trip can be completely customized according to your needs and desires.
Of course you will visit the Colosseum skipping the annoying entrance line.

Let us know what you want to do and see and we will plan for you a unique journey into the past.

data.name: Da Roma: tour giornaliero a Pompei
data.shortDescription:
Raggiungi in soli 30 minuti il sito archeologico di Pompei. Scendi all'ingresso principale degli scavi ed evita la coda utilizzando il voucher salta fila. 

 

Cosa ti aspetta:

  • Esplora gli Scavi di Pompei in autonomia 
  • Salta  lunga fila all'ingresso del sito 
  • Osserva come vivevano gli abitanti dell'antica città Romana

 

Inizia il tuo tour dal centro di Napoli, dall'Aeroporto Internazionale o dalla Stazione Centrale. Dopo circa 30 minuti di tragitto , sarai lasciato nelle prossimità dell'ingresso prinicipale delle rovine. Potrai usufruire dell'ingresso salta fila mostrando il voucher e avrai  3 ore di tempo libero alla scoperta del sito passeggiando in piena autonomia. Viaggia indietro nel passato ed immagina la vita durante l'Impero Romano. Passeggia tra le strade acciottolate costruite più di 2000 anni fa e ammira ciò che resta dei negozi , templi e teatri che vennero ricoperti da lava e ceneri durante l'eruzione del vulcano Vesuvio nel 79 AD. Osserva le piastrelle mosaicate delle lussuose ville dei ricchi mercanti che trovarono la loro fortuna nella prosperosa città. Ammira le Rovine della Dimora del Fauno e scopri come si intrattenevano gli abitanti del luogo tra terme, case di incontri e molto altro.

Incluso :

  • Prelievo da Napoli Centro, Aeroporto Internazionale o Stazione Centrale
  • Transfer di andata e ritorno
  • Biglietto d'ingresso prioritario per Pompei

 

Non è incluso :

  • Guida / audioguida
