data.name: Rome Private Vespa Tour with Hotel Pickup
data.description: Vespas have long been associated with Rome, but driving yourself can be risky if you’re not experienced with scooters or Roman roads. This tour gets you on the back of a Vespa safely, with a driver/guide to show you around and take control of the gears. As an added bonus, you’ll take home souvenir photos of your experience.

data.name: Rome Half-Day Private Pizza, Wine, Gelato Sightseeing Tour
data.description: Make the most of your time in Rome and experience its history, culture, and cuisine in one half-day private tour. Meet your guide near the Colosseum and walk around to see major landmarks including the Pantheon, Spanish Steps, and Trevi Fountain. Along the way, enjoy delicious slices of pizza with wine, topped off with gelato.

data.name: Rome Pizza Making Class with Italian Chef and Gourmet Toppings
data.description: Master the art of Roman pizza-making with a hands-on class led by an Italian chef in the heart of Rome. Craft authentic dough, simmer vibrant sauces, and customize your pizza with gourmet toppings for a personal twist. Enjoy a uniquely Roman culinary experience in a welcoming, relaxed setting.

data.name: Exclusive Colosseum Arena Floor and Ancient Rome guided tour
data.description: Step into the Arena and live this unique experience in the Colosseum. Book this guided tour at a special price, with skip the line tickets and English-speaking guide. The guided tour also includes the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill.

data.name: Semi private half day in Pompeii from Rome extraordinary afternoon opening
data.description: Explore the ruins of the ancient city of Pompeii on a day trip from Rome. Skip the hassle of navigating train and bus schedules on your own and enjoy semi-private transportation directly from Rome to Pompeii. You’ll explore the remarkably intact city of Pompeii, nearly perfectly preserved by volcanic ash and lava when Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD, with an archeologist guide and learn about the history and culture of ancient Rome. You will leave big urban centers, impressive buildings and modern buildings to cross the countryside characterized by fantastic relaxing landscapes and cultivated fields. Reach the famous Campania Felix, the region of happiness famous for the sun, the sea and pizza, you will visit a small village and from here a hill that until 500 centuries ago was still covered with lava and concealed a secret lasted years: Pompeii 2000 years ago. Are you ready to discover how modern our ancestors were? How their cities were well structured? how do their homes have every comfort? Pompeii is still there, frozen in time and with this tour we will bring it back to their life

data.name: Rome: Pasta Making and Tiramisù Cooking Class
data.description: Held either in a 17th Century Palazzo near Piazza Navona or just steps away from the Pantheon, this interactive class is led by an enthusiastic English-speaking chef. Perfect for kids and adults, locals and visitors, this class is designed for anyone with a passion for delicious food, having fun, and learning something new.Compose creamy layers of bitter-sweet flavor in traditional tiramisù. You will start by assembling scrumptious layers of smooth cream, rich coffee, and sweet cocoa.While the tiramisù settles, you will mix, kneed, and roll out our fresh handmade pasta before infusing it with our favorite seasonal flavors. Vibrant pumpkin tortellini in the autumn, light coils of fettuccine dressed in eggplant in the summer, and succulent ravioli dumplings stuffed with rich, creamy ricotta di pecora… well, essentially any time of the year! Sprinkle on a selection of sumptuous Italian cheeses and your mouth-watering meal is ready to be eaten! Celebrate with friendly, festive company and a perfect selection of red and white wines and soft drinks.

data.name: Rome Baroque Fountains and Squares Private Walking Tour
data.description: Rome has some seriously spectacular fountains and piazzas, and while wandering between spots is the most charming way to explore, it's also the easiest way to get lost. Stay on track while immersing yourself in Roman history on a private tour, which wraps up with an included meal at a local restaurant.

data.name: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel Private Night Tour
data.description: Skip Rome's crushing daytime crowds with this exclusive after-dark Vatican tour. Your private, English-speaking guide provides skip-the-line access to 54 museum rooms, Raphael's Rooms, Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel frescoes, and more, including the narrow passageways to the Borgia Apartments. You'll experience Renaissance masterpieces in a peaceful evening atmosphere without the tourist chaos—a rare experience in Rome.

data.name: VIP Experience Private Transfer from Fiumicino Airport to Rome
data.description: Traveling has never been so comfortable. A journey is not just a transfer from one place to another, but it is an experience. For that reason nothing is left to chance. A driver will be waiting for you inside the Terminal to monitor your flight before you leave, to make sure you can avoid any inconvenience. After comfortably passing the checks you will see him waiting for you with a sign with your name written on top so you can easily recognize him. After collecting the luggages, pass through the sliding glass door. You will find your driver at the arrival terminal. At this point he will take care of you and your personal effects, you will just have to sit in a luxury Mercedes vehicle, where you can find a bottle of water and a map of Rome. From this moment, Rome is in your hands and if you choose the tour option, the driver will stop in front of all the iconic places of the city and will explain some little anecdote and a bit of history to make you feel like you're no longer a foreigner but a local friend.

data.name: Modern Italian Dinner Near the Vatican
data.description:
Join the latest culinary trend of immersive and social dining where local hosts invite you into their homes for a magical meal.

Join Chef Debora for a culinary journey and wine pairing, through the different regions of Italy. Take a seat at her table and enjoy a refined 4-course menu prepared with fresh ingredients from the farmers' market! The menu depends on the season and on the products availability; the wines will be chosen accordingly to the specific dishes of the night. You can't miss it out!

data.name: Rome Private Cascata Delle Marmore Day Trip
data.description: Visiting Cascata Delle Marmore, one of the highest artificial waterfalls in the world, can be a challenge if you don't have a car. This private tour makes getting to the fall—which was created over 2,000 years ago—a breeze, thanks to private transportation and the services of an English-speaking guide.

data.name: Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel Skip-the-Line Hosted Entrance
data.description: Waiting in admission lines in Rome can be daunting, especially during summer when crowds swell and temperatures soar. With this prebooked ticket, save time by skipping admission lines with an escorted entrance to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel, among the most visited—and crowded—attractions in the world.

data.name: Rome by Night: Romantic Private Tour (Hotel Transfers Option)
data.description: The Eternal City comes into its own at night, when the crowds die down and lights sparkle across Rome. Feel the romance on this private tour, just for you and your beloved, as you soak up rooftop views, sip prosecco, wine, or a soft drink on Janiculum Hill, and pose for photos with icons including the Colosseum. Upgrade for an even more relaxing experience, with round-trip hotel transfers.

data.name: Vatican Museums Small-Group Tour with Skip-the-Line Entry
data.description: The Vatican Museums can be intimidating for first-time visitors, both for the wealth of its art and for the vast area it covers. With this small-group tour, see the highlights with a guide for a comprehensive introduction to the Vatican Museums, Raphael Rooms, and Sistine Chapel that won’t overwhelm. Plus, skip-the-line entry ensures getting inside is quick and as easy as can be.

data.name: Florence Castel Sant'Angelo Private Skip-the-Line Guided Tour
data.description:
Make your way to Castel Sant’Angelo to meet your private guide in time for a 3pm departure. Then, set out to discover the mighty fortress of Castel Sant' Angelo. With skip-the-line entrance tickets, you'll breeze past the long lines at the entrance and head straight in.

The ancient site was built in 139AD to house the tomb of Emperor Hadrian. Many of his successors were also buried here. It was later converted to a castle in the 14th century.

Learn about its fascinating history as a one-time castle, refuge, prison, and site of public executions from your guide as you explore the ruins, admire sculptures by Bernini, Raggi and Morelli, and walk in the footsteps of former Popes as you visit the papal apartments. Then, and head straight to the star attraction – the grand mausoleum of Emperor Hadrian.

Finally, enjoy a spectacular view over Rome from the castle's panoramic terrace.

data.name: Rome: Santa Maria Maggiore & Liberian Museum Small-Group Tour
data.description: Discover the chuch where late Pope Francis chose to be entombed on this small-group tour of the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore and the adjacent Liberian Historical Museum of religious art. Learn about the history of this papal basilica from your guide as you admire highlights including the Loggia of Blessings, Hall of Popes, and Bernini Staircase. End with a guided stroll through the museum to touch on its most important artworks.

data.name: Fast Track - Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel & Raphael rooms
data.description:
Meet your guide at the designated tour office and enter the Vatican Museums with a skip-the-line ticket, bypassing the usual queues. Inside, marvel at one of the world’s largest collections of Renaissance and Baroque art, assembled by various popes over centuries. Listen as your guide unveils stories of powerful pontiffs, controversies, and the rich history behind masterworks such as the frescoes in Raphael’s Rooms—take note of The School of Athens, where Raphael cleverly included portraits of Michelangelo and himself.

Stroll through ornate galleries like the Gallery of the Masks and the Gallery of the Maps, then step into the revered Sistine Chapel. Once reserved for the pope’s private worship, this sacred space is now world-famous for Michelangelo’s transcendent frescoes, The Creation of Adam and The Last Judgement. It’s the perfect capstone to a journey through the Vatican’s unparalleled artistic trove.

data.name: Rome Private Skip-the-Line Vatican Tour
data.description: Specially suited for travelers short on time, this private skip-the-line tour of the Vatican Museums covers top sights in the iconic papal collections in just a few hours. Admire world-renowned masterpieces, from the iconic painted ceiling of the Sistine Chapel to the Raphael Rooms and the Galleries of Tapestries and Maps. Pre-booked, no-wait admission tickets let you breeze past the entrance lines, saving time for taking in the sights.

data.name: Pantheon Fast-Track Ticket with Audio Guide App
data.description: Skip the line and step into the Pantheon’s timeless grandeur with an audio guide app and fast-track ticket. With towering Corinthian columns and its famous oculus casting light from above, this self-paced audio tour unveils the secrets behind one of Rome’s most remarkable architectural feats. Hear the stories of emperors, artists, and engineers who left their mark on this ancient wonder.

data.name: Rome Private Naples Pizza Class by High-Speed Train
data.description: Take a high-speed train from Rome to Naples, the birthplace of pizza, for a private pizza-making class with a master pizza maker. Learn the secrets behind authentic Neapolitan pizza dough in a UNESCO-recognized "Pizza Lab," then bake your own creation in a traditional wood-fired oven. Afterward, enjoy a delicious true Neapolitan pizza with wine while taking in stunning views of Naples' waterfront, Mount Vesuvius, and Castel dell'Ovo.

data.name: Amalfi Coast and Positano Day Trip From Rome With Cruise
data.description: Discover the highlights of the Amalfi Coast without the hassle of organizing an itinerary or hiring a car on this full-day trip from Rome. Relax onboard a comfortable, air-conditioned coach with Wi-Fi, and soak up the scenery as you head out to the coast. Explore the charming towns of Positano and Amalfi, sip limoncello, and hop aboard a boat cruise in Salerno to take in the beautiful views from a vantage point on the water.

data.name: Hadrian’s Villa and Villa d’Este Private Photo Tour from Rome
data.description: Escape the bustle of Rome and discover two spectacular photography destinations with this full-day private photography workshop. Set off from Rome with your professional photographer guide to visit Hadrian’s Villa and Villa d’Este (entrance fees extra) in Tivoli. Capture the ancient ruins and lush gardens, with the assistance of your guide, so you come away with unforgettable shots and improved photo taking skills.

data.name: Sunset Rome Food & Wine Tour around Prati District
data.description: Experience Rome like a local on this mouthwatering evening tour of the Prati District. Stroll through charming streets with a knowledgeable guide, sampling cured meats, cheeses, and unforgettable pizza from hidden culinary gems. Meet passionate artisans who share their recipes and food-making secrets. With groups capped at 13, this intimate tour fills quickly—reserve early.

data.name: Rome to Designer Outlet Castel Romano: Private Transfer
data.description: Don’t waste your precious vacation time waiting for a bus or dragging your shopping bags through the Rome Metro. Instead, let a driver handle all your transfer needs while you relax in a car that’s just for you. Get between your city hotel and the Designer Outlet Castel Romano with ease, thanks to a driver who knows the route like the back of their hand.

data.name: Castel Sant’Angelo Skip-the-Line Ticket with Audio Guide & Gelato
data.description:
Avoid the crowds and make the most of your visit with this convenient and enriching experience. Your ticket includes skip-the-line access to the museum, allowing you to enter smoothly without the hassle of waiting in long queues.

Explore at your own pace with an optional premium audio guide created by expert historians, designed to give you deep insights, engaging stories, and cultural context that bring the artworks to life.

To sweeten the experience, enjoy a complimentary gelato at one of the best ice cream shops near the museum—perfect for a refreshing break after your visit.

data.name: Caravaggio's Art and Life Private Walking Tour in Rome
data.description: Get an in-depth look into the life and legacy of Italy’s first Baroque master on a Caravaggio tour of Rome. Visit several churches in the heart of the city to admire the painter’s original, groundbreaking work, learning the background of each piece and what sets it apart from Renaissance styles. Feel free to ask all the questions you like on the private tour, led by a professional art historian guide.

data.name: Private transfer from Ciampino Airport to hotel in Rome
data.description: Book this comfortable private transfer by luxury Mercedes-Benz from Ciampino Airport to hotel or other accommodations located within the Aurelian Walls of Rome, and start your vacation or business trip in style. An experienced driver will be waiting in the arrival’s hall with a sign with your name on it for ease of contact. There’s no need to worry about flight or customs delays as the driver will wait up to 1.5 hours without extra charge. Then, sit back and relax as they navigate the busy and unfamliar roads to quickly get you to your hotel. Forget the stress of finding a taxi on arrival, or dealing with the public transportation system. The service is available from 7am to 8pm.

data.name: Rome Best of Tour of Trevi Fountain, Pantheon & Spanish Steps
data.description: Join this 90-minute stroll through the very heart of Rome. Delight in the majesty of the Spanish Steps, toss a coin into the iconic Trevi Fountain, marvel at the timeless beauty of the Pantheon, and so much more. With an expert local guide, you'll be transported through centuries of history and culture in the blink of an eye. Prepare to be captivated by the true essence of Rome on this once-in-a-lifetime tour.

data.name: Colosseum St Clements Underground & Crypts for Families
data.description: Explore the Colosseum and the lesser-known Saint Clement’s Church during this archaeologist-led, two-for-one guided tour, specially tailored to families with kids. Visit four underground levels of the fresco-filled basilica, including the ruins of an ancient temple. Colosseum admission is included.

data.name: Vatican Museums with St. Peter’s Basilica small group tour
data.description: Embark on guided walking tour of the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter's Basilica with a small group of up to 20 people. With priority access, you can delve straight into exploring these historic sites. Discover fascinating tales about the characters that walked these corridors. Your guide will escort you to the Vatican Gardens balcony for your initial view of St. Peter's Basilica's majestic dome before strolling through the Pinecone Courtyard, home to ancient statues and contemporary sculptures.To reach the Chapel, your guide will navigate you along the Hall of Maps, through the Gallery of Tapestries and into the Gallery of Candelabra. These masterpieces will spring to life as you listen to your guide's commentary via your dedicated audio earpiece. At the Sistine Chapel, take a moment to appreciate the intricate details adorning the walls and ceilings.After immersing yourself in the chapel's rich Renaissance history, use your skip-the-line access to enter St. Peter's Basilica. Here, you'll encounter Michelangelo's Pietá, a poignant depiction of Mary. After this, feel free to linger inside St. Peter's Basilica to further explore this awe-inspiring church or step outside to St. Peter's Square to admire Bernini's optical illusion and the Basilica's façade.In just a span of three hours, you'll be introduced to the artistic treasures of the Vatican in a relaxed and enjoyable way.

data.name: Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill from Rome
data.description: After pick up at your hotel (in selected hotels in central Rome), you will reach the Archeological area with no stress, ready to get the most complete tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Access the Palatine Hill with no line and discover the hill where Rome was founded. Then reach the Colosseum and be blown away by this monument that is the symbol of Rome across the world. The Amphitheater created to entertain ancient Roman citizens with bloody shows of gladiators, animals and cruel games, is now one of the most fascinating landmarks of the City. Then, walk on the original path of ancient Rome along the Via Sacra and see the Temples of Vesta, Antonino and Faustina, the ancient Basilica Julia and Aemilia and dream about the glorious past of the Roman Empire. Truly an unforgettable day!

data.name: Vatican Museums Private Tour
data.description: The only museum that includes others museums. Inside you will find in fact: the Vatican Art Gallery, the Gregorian Egyptian Museum and the Gregorian Etruscan Museum, the Vatican Historical Museum, Gallery of Candelabra and Gallery of Maps. These are only some examples of its incredible variety. If you want to access one of the places that most represents Rome's art patrimony, you can't absolutely miss this tour. Walking tour locations: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. A great symbol of Catholic church and of Italy in itself. Well-known around the globe, it attracts every day millions of visitors. Its Museums are the most eminent representation of the art collections accumulated by all the popes through the centuries. The splendor of the Vatican Museums is due to its limitless artistic beauty without equals in the world. It would take a whole day to admire and appreciate every detail of all its works of art: paintings, frescoes, statues, tapestries that give testimony of our history.

data.name: Rome to Florence, Venice, and Sorrento 10-Night Italy Tour
data.description: Want to explore without having to plan a thing or worry about driving? Check off many of Italy's highlights on this multi-day tour from Rome, which takes care of all the details for you. Visit some of the most popular destinations in the country, from Tuscany and Assisi to Venice, Capri, and UNESCO World Heritage-listed Pompeii. Travel hassle-free with accommodation at 3- or 4-star hotels included throughout the trip, plus many meals.

data.name: Skip the Line Vatican Museums with Sistine Chapel
data.description: Avoid wasting time during your Vatican visit on this Vatican Museums and St. Peter's Basilica tour at the no-wait access entrance. Join a knowledgeable guide to pass right by the long entrance queues and start touring the massive museums. See the incomparable Raphael's Rooms, Michelangelo's stunning Sistine Chapel, as well as other museum highlights like the Maps Gallery and Tapestries Gallery. Then visit the impressive St. Peter's Basilica next door.

data.name: Vatican: Quick Access Skip the Line Museums and Sistine Chapel
data.description: Book now to experience the Vatican's top treasures with zero wait! Our Skip-the-Line ticket offers fast-track entry, allowing you to dive right into the Vatican Museums’ rich galleries, without losing time in long lines. Explore the grandeur of the Raphael Rooms, marvel at intricate ancient sculptures, and finish with the Sistine Chapel’s awe-inspiring ceiling, painted by Michelangelo. With this ticket, you'll have the freedom to explore at your own pace while enjoying priority access to some of the world’s most famous masterpieces. Don’t miss this chance to save time and fully enjoy the Vatican's incredible heritage!

data.name: Colosseum Skip-The-Lines Guided Tour for Kids and Families
data.description: Navigate ancient Rome, touring it uniquely in the company of a small group and a tour guide, providing you with a semi-private guided experience. Skip the lines with fast-access tickets and explore the Colosseum, Palatine Hill, and Roman Forum alongside an expert, licensed tour guide. Over a fascinating walk, immerse yourself in the captivating stories of Roman glory and drama while uncovering the rich history and lifestyle of this remarkable civilization. Step into the past with unmatched convenience and expertise.

data.name: Pompeii, Amalfi Coast, Positano Day Tour from Rome
data.description:
Begin your day at Piazzale Flaminio in Rome, where you’ll board a comfortable, air-conditioned bus bound for the ancient ruins of Pompeii—a journey of roughly three and a half hours. Upon arriving at the archaeological site, join an expert guide (an archaeologist) for an in-depth look at the city buried by Mount Vesuvius, admiring centuries-old structures and artifacts preserved by volcanic ash.

Afterward, return to your bus for a scenic drive along the famed Amalfi Coast, arriving at Positano. Stroll the narrow lanes of this charming seaside town, perhaps stopping to sample local cuisine (at your own expense). Then, reboard your bus and head back to Rome, taking with you lasting memories of southern Italy’s rich history and natural beauty.

data.name: Villa Borghese Gardens by Golf Cart
data.shortDescription: Rent a golf cart and explore the Villa Borghese gardens
data.description:
Walking's great, but wouldn't you prefer to explore the stunning greenery of Villa Borghese Gardens in an electric golf buggy? Of course, you would! 

Move at comfortable, non-threatening speeds as you roll gently around 80 hectares of lush landscape garden near the famous Borghese Gallery (inaccessible by golf buggy... for now).

data.name: Ancient Roman Baths & Michelangelo’s Renaissance Basilica in Rome
data.description:
Experience the grandeur of Rome on an exclusive tour through the Baths of Diocletian and the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels & Martyrs, designed by Michelangelo. Discover Renaissance elegance intertwined with ancient ruins and witness the intricate meridian line and astronomical clock inside the basilica. This journey blends history, art, and science in a setting where ancient engineering meets Renaissance design. Opt for a small group or private tour. For an even richer experience, add a visit to Palazzo Massimo, home to some of Rome's finest ancient art and mesmerising frescoes.

Please note that the itinerary may vary. Depending on the schedule, you may begin your visit at the Baths of Diocletian and proceed to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels & Martyrs, or vice versa

data.name: Rome: Private Driving Tour of the Most-Important Highlights
data.description: Check off 10 of Rome's most-important landmarks in just one day on this private driving tour. Journey around the city, from the Pantheon to Piazza Navona and St. Peter's Basilica, and, with insights from your guide, see the history of Rome unfold through its architecture, from the ancient Colosseum to baroque Trevi Fountain.

data.name: Rome Handmade Pasta and Carbonara Small-Group Cooking Class
data.description: It’s hard to think of an Italian dish that’s treated as badly outside its home territory as carbonara. Get to the heart of Italy’s traditions as you make your own pasta and prepare an authentic Italian carbonara, with guanciale not pancetta, pecorino Romano not Parmesan, and definitely no cream or bacon. For added authenticity, enjoy an aperitivo with wine and snacks, plus wine as you sit down to your meal.

data.name: Rome's Charm Exclusive Private Chauffeur Tour
data.description: Experience the timeless charm of Rome in style with an exclusive private chauffeur tour. Visit top landmarks in the city like the Colosseum, St. Peter's Square, and the Trevi Fountain with ease. Discover history and culture along the legendary Appian Way, all while enjoying fascinating insights from an English-speaking chauffeur.

data.name: Via Crucis Catholic Pilgrim Tour in Rome
data.description: Embark on a spiritual experience like no other with the Via Crucis flagship Rome tour, an essential itinerary for Christian pilgrims to the heart of Christendom before and during the Holy Year.Created by and for traditional Catholics, the tour takes in the sacred Relics of Christ’s Passion, including part of the Holy Cross, the Holy Nails, the Crown of Thorns and the Title of the Cross, bearing the infamous inscription “Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews”. You'll also have the opportunity to see the Holy Stairs which Jesus climbed in condemnation, the pillar upon which He was scourged and other priceless artifacts from Christendom such as the Salus Popoli Romani icon by St. Luke and an example of Acheiropoieta in the Holy of Holies.This tour visits two of Rome's four Holy Doors along the way, at the Major Basilica of St. Mary Major and the Arch-Basilica of St. John Lateran, the Mother Church of the World. Your devout Catholic guide will interpret the Catechesis in the stunning artworks and mosaics, blending history and faith to create a truly unforgettable experience.

data.name: Vatican Guided Tour Skip The Line Entrance

data.name: Small Group Tour Colosseum, Roman Forum & Palatine in English
data.description: Get to know in depth the glorious years of Rome and what life was like for its inhabitants at that time. Duration 3 Hours About The visit starts at the Forum. It was the center of the ancient city. All civic life was concentrated in the Roman Forum, which was the place where trade and politics took place, justice was dispensed, the gods were worshiped and social relations developed. You will be able to differentiate, from the hand of your guide, the remains of different buildings, temples, and areas of the forum such as the "Roman Curia" the "arches of Septimius and Titus" or the "temple of Julius Caesar". From here you can see Palatine Hill. Here is the imperial residence and you can tour the different spaces of these impressive ruins. Do not miss the Palatine Museum which contains pieces of great interest that will help you better understand what you are seeing. Afterward, the tour continues with the visit to the Colosseum. It was the place of public entertainment in Roman times. Up to 50,000 spectators would gather here to watch gladiatorial games, sea battles, or animal fights. Its interior was divided into five levels in which attendees were separated according to social class: increasing their social rank the closer they were to the arena. The Colosseum was built during the 70s and 80s AD. and has a height of 48.50 meters and an area of 24000m2. The views from the top are impressive, especially if you imagine the gladiators fighting several meters below your feet. data.name: Ancient Rome: from the Capitoline Hill to the Colosseum along the Imperial Fora  – Private Tour
data.description: Your itinerary begins in Piazza del Campidoglio, one of Rome’s most scenic locations. Designed by Michelangelo and a symbol of the Renaissance, this square offers a perfect introduction to the sacred hill, home to Rome’s civic institutions and the famous Capitoline Museums. From here, we’ll descend toward the Via dei Fori Imperiali. As we stroll along this historic route, you’ll enjoy breathtaking views of the Roman Forum, the vibrant heart of ancient Rome, stretching out at the foot of the Capitoline Hill. Highlights include the remains of the Temple of Saturn, once the repository of the state treasury, and the Basilica Julia, a hub for legal and administrative affairs. Your guide will also delve into the significance of the Curia, the Senate's meeting hall, and the stories surrounding the imposing Arch of Septimius Severus, a monumental symbol of victory and imperial power. Continuing along the road, we’ll reach the Forum of Trajan, home to the exquisite Trajan’s Column, which narrates the emperor’s military campaigns through intricately carved reliefs. Just a short distance ahead, the Markets of Trajan stand as a remarkable testament to the commercial ingenuity of ancient Rome. These markets, considered precursors to modern shopping centers, were more than a simple marketplace. They served as the economic hub of the city, housing administrative offices, shops, and storage facilities, all ingeniously designed into the terraced slopes of the Quirinal Hill. A brief detour will take you to the picturesque Monti district, which in ancient times was the heart of the Suburra. It was the unhealthy and overcrowded “red-light” neighborhood, located just beyond the Fora where sub-proletarians and small traders lived. It was home to lupanari (ancient brothels) and notorious taverns, frequented by criminals, but also by aristocrats and matrons seeking forbidden thrills, and home to illustrious figures such as Julius Caesar and the poet Martial. The walk culminates at the awe-inspiring Colosseum, the ultimate symbol of Rome. Here, your guide will recount tales of gladiatorial battles, imperial festivities, and the grand spectacles that once captivated thousands. Even today, this iconic amphitheater enchants visitors from around the globe. This experience is perfect for those who wish to explore Rome at a leisurely pace, savoring every detail of an itinerary that spans more than two thousand years of history.

data.name: Vatican Museums 3-Hour Private Skip-the-Line Tour
data.description:
Meet your private guide at Vatican Museums entrance and begin your tour at the Belvedere Courtyard, which was designed in the 16th century by Donato Bramante and is considered an influential architectural work. Then, see a large collection of classical Roman and Greek statues in the Pio Clementino Museum.

Browse an important display of tapestries and Renaissance maps in the Gallery of Maps, see the Vatican's largest canvas painting in the Sobiesky Room, and learn about the 19th-century frescoes that decorate the Immaculate Conception Room.

Next, see the Raphael Rooms, commissioned by Pope Julius II in the early 16th century.

Head into the Sistine Chapel to view famous frescoes by Botticelli, Michelangelo, and other renowned artists. Hear about the papal conclave that is held in the Sistine Chapel to elect a new Pope.

End your tour in Saint Peter's square to see the Pope's Palace and the Swiss Guards.

data.description: Embark on a remarkable journey with an exclusive ticket that opens the doors to the historic Castel Sant'Angelo and the Passetto di Borgo, a clandestine corridor once utilised by Popes during perilous times.This combined ticket offers you the chance to delve into Rome's history. Begin your exploration at the Passetto di Borgo, a silent testament to extraordinary historical events such as papal escapes during conflicts. This passage connects the castle to St. Peter's Square. Following this, uncover the formidable walls and artistic treasures of Castel Sant'Angelo accompanied by a downloadable audio guide, a structure that has served as a fortress, mausoleum, and papal residence for centuries.This is an unmissable experience that transports you directly into the heart of Rome's concealed past, brimming with art, history, and legends that moulded the fate of the Popes. Seize this opportunity to discover two of the city's most emblematic attractions in one visit.

data.name: Rome Circus Maximus and Aventine Hill Private Walking Tour
data.description:
Meet a guide at a central location in ancient Rome, then set out on a route through the city that can be tailored to your group’s interests and needs.

The first stop of the day is the Circus Maximus, where ancient Roman charioteers raced before hundreds of thousands of spectators—the Circus Maximus could accommodate at least four times more people than the Colosseum.

Your guide helps bring the ancient world to life throughout the tour, telling stories and using an iPad as a visual aid; take advantage of your time with a private guide to ask questions about Roman life, history, and culture.

Continue to Aventine Hill to see some of Rome’s most elegant houses, on quiet streets lined with fragrant pine trees. Stop to see the medieval churches of St. Alexius, Boniface, and Sabina, which contain remarkable collections of art and relics. Keep walking to the “Aventine Keyhole,” where you find a gorgeous view of St. Peter’s Basilica from a tiny hole in a garden door.

The final stop of the tour is the Orange Garden, also called Savelli Park, where you finish the tour strolling between rows of bitter orange trees and looking out over gorgeous views of Rome.

data.name: Jubilee of Hope 2025: A Prayer in Music

data.name: Rome Catacombs & Appian Way: Private Golf Cart Tour
data.description: This tour will whisk you away to the cobbled lanes and idyllic fields of the Italian countryside to visit the Catacombs and drive along the famed and historic Appian Way. On your private tour, you will: Enjoy pick-up in central Rome and a panoramic drive past the iconic Colosseum, Roman Forum, Arch of Constantine, Circus Maximus and Imperial Palaces on Palatine Hill; Drive along the historic Appian Way, the ‘Roman Queen of Roads’ - and step on the actual paving stones laid by Ancient Romans; Visit the Roman Catacombs with tickets for a guided tour included; Venture off the beaten trackRome to discover ruins, relics and curiosities hidden from the eye; Learn about Roman engineering on your drive back into the city, and admire an Ancient Roman Aqueduct hidden in plain sight! Combine the intimacy of a walking tour with the comfort of a driving tour with your private golf cart. Your experience starts with a pick-up in central Rome and a panoramic drive past the iconic Colosseum, Roman Forum, Arch of Constantine, Circus Maximus and Imperial Palaces on Palatine Hill, before you embark on an adventure across the less travelled side of beautiful Rome - the majestic Appian Way. The Via Appia Antica (Appian way) was at one time, the most important road in the Roman Empire rolling from Central Rome to the beautiful hills and fields of the neighbouring countryside and eventually all the way to the City of Brindisi. Sided by sleepy churches, farmhouses and crumbling Roman ruins, it is a truly magical picturesque route. You will stop at one of Rome's ancient catacombs to explore the network of underground burial grounds that date from the second to the fifth century, and then drive out to the city’s remaining visible network of aqueducts. Please note: Private guides are not allowed to guide inside the Catacombs so you will join a small group with an official Catacombs tour guide. Once the pride of Roman engineering, these wonderful aqueducts transported water over long distances to towns and cities, providing the means to construct complex sewage irrigation systems, and supply fresh, clean water for baths, fountains, and drinking water for its citizens. Your four-hour tour will end with a drop-off back in your hotel or any central Rome location.Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. data.name: Amalfi and Positano small-group day trip from Rome: across the sea, earth and history
data.description: Just a few kilometres south of the splendid city of Naples, a marvellous peninsula bends towards the Mediterranean nuances of the Italian sea: the Amalfi Coast is such a charming and evocative place that it has been chosen by UNESCO as one of the most superlative examples of the majesty and luxury of Italian landscapes. Could we at Gray Line I Love Rome not think of all those who would love to discover this wonderful region with one of our most famous Day Trips? This is a region traditionally deeply connected to its sea, verdant landscapes and centuries-long history. Did you know that the beautiful Amalfi was one of the four Maritime Republics of Italy, together with Genoa, Pisa and Venice? Maritime Republics were independent city-states in Italy - during the Middle Ages – that had naval supremacy over a vast territory; they each had their own impressive fleet of ships for their protection, but also for large-scale trade networks across the Mediterranean basin. They were the bridge that connected the old European continent to the Middle East, to Africa and Asia, not only for trade purposes, but also cultural and artistic. During the golden years of the international jet set, in the 1960s, the Amalfi Coast was the favourite retreat for the most important international political, movies and show-biz personalities: from Jaqueline Kennedy to the Agnelli family, from Sophia Loren and Greta Garbo to Rudolf Nureyev. Among the most popular and visited destinations are Amalfi and Positano, included in this activity, but also Ravello, Procida and the spectacular Sorrento, that are definitely worth a few days’ trip. If you wish to become an expert of the region, ask our staff for all the other experiences: whether it is a day trip or a multi-day excursion, we guarantee you it will be unforgettable! This tour will allow you the chance to visit two of the most famous and popular villages of the Amalfi Coast: Amalfi and Positano. You will join a group of no more than 15 people, when meeting with your tour leader at the Roma Termini railway station to leave for Salerno onboard the high-speed train included in the package. Once in Salerno, you will reach Amalfi by ferryboat, which is truly the best way to explore the Coast and get the best possible view of the hills plunging into the sea, the coloured little houses and the majestic nature that surrounds you: you’ll feel like a movie star! Amalfi will be the first destination you reach: nestled in a ravine surrounded by stunning cliffs, it was known as the Duchy of Amalfi during the Middle Ages. Here you will have free time to explore the town, its public squares, shops and the Cathedral on your own. After visiting Amalfi, you will take the ferry back to Positano to discover all its charm and elegance: you will feel as if you ended up in a painting! Its coloured buildings, shops and sandy beaches will put a spell on you: visit the Marina Grande beach, just where the town meets the sea, or stroll around Fornillo or Arienzo beaches. You will spend about two and a half hours in Positano before taking your ferry back to Salerno and heading for the railway station to take your high-speed train back to Rome, where you will be at around 08:30 PM

data.name: Rome Underground Catacombs and Crypts
data.description: Important: Depending on different closing days, you will visit two catacombs between Domitilla’s, Saint Sebastian’s, Priscilla’s, San Callixtus's Catacombs. Discover the ancestral and underground area of Rome.You can admire several burial chambers and various pagan burial sites. These places were formerly used as burial grounds because it was forbidden to bury or cremate corpses in the city.  You can visit the largest and oldest underground cemetery in Rome. The catacombs of St. Callixtus were the official cemetery of the Church of Rome and half a million Christians were buried there among many martyrs and popes (the Crypt of the Popes). You will also admire the Crypt of St. Cecilia: the popular patron of music, she was martyred and entombed where the statue now lies.  Domitilla's catacombs are one of the most extensive catacombs in Rome, they are spread over 17 kilometers of underground caves, some of which are inaccessible, and they are situated over 16 meters underground. Some Christians have built these catacombs in the Ardeatina's area, after Domitilla had been banished in the III century. There are about 150000 burials, some of them are decorated. Saint Sebastian's catacombs, situated in Via Appia, are very important because historians believe that this place had hosted Saints Peter and Paul bodies. They are located in a slope that has always been used as a cemetery also before Christianism; later it was converted in a cemetery for slaves and freedmen.  Priscilla's catacombs are one of the most ancient underground cemetery. The first burials should go back to the second half of the II century AD and because of the big amount of graves in it, it is called "regina catacombarum". This cemetery was ransacked around the XVI century so there are no tombstones, coffins and tuff, nevertheless there are many well-preserved paintings.

For departure from the hotel, your driver will meet you at the lobby of your hotel. Then, sit back and relax en route to Civitavecchia Port. Pick-ups from Civitavecchia Port at the end of your cruise are direct from the pier where your cruise ship docks. Forget the stress of everyday life, and enjoy the services of a chauffeur-driven service by luxurious Mercedes. Before getting on board book a 1-hour tour of Rome.

data.name: Private Tiramisu and gelato-making class
data.description: Become a pastry chef for the day with us and learn how to make tiramisù and gelato from scratch during your Roman holiday: this 2-hour-class is suitable for foodies of any age and even for gluten and lactose intolerants. Reach our trusted local gourmet at our meeting point in the Campo De’ Fiori area and let the magic begin. In a group of 2 up to 10 people, you’ll learn everything about this lovely dessert: what to buy, how to bake ladyfingers, how to whip the perfect eggs and mascarpone cheese cream. You’ll work in a proper laboratory, inside a tiramisu shop, and a professional pastry chef will assist you all the time. Thanks to the step-by-step approach of this class, you’ll truly grasp the secrets and learn all the correct techniques that are required to make a perfect, creamy, luxurious tiramisu. During this class, you’ll also find out the actual difference between ice-cream and gelato, you’ll learn how to make sorbet, a delicious water-based fruit gelato, and...of course, there’ll be plenty of tastings during all the class, so don’t come on a full stomach! Afterward, you’ll receive the recipes, so you can show off your skills once you’re back home: don’t forget to post the pictures on your social media pages and tag us.

data.name: Audiencia Papal + Almuerzo + Museos Vaticanos
data.description: Experiencia Completa! En los museos vaticanos: Ingreso sin esperas - max. 15 personas Acerca de Por la mañana nuestra guia les acompañará a la Plaza San Pedro donde esperaremos el inicio de la Audiencia Papal (puede celebrarse en la Sala de Audiencias). Por la tarde, a las 14.00 h. nuestro guía se reunirá con Ud. en el restaurante y leo llevará a los Museos Vaticanos, para dar inicio a la visita de una de las colecciones de arte más ricas del mundo, para admirar, entre otros, la mundialmente conocida Capilla Sixtina, la obra maestra de Miguel Ángel. Desde los museos entraremos directamente a la Basílica de San Pedro, la más grande e importante Iglesia Católica del mundo, con sus tesoros como la escultura de Miguel Ángel La Piedad y el altar Baldaquín de Bernini. El tour finaliza en la Plaza San Pedro, dominada por la imponente cúpula de Miguel Ángel y rodeada por la famosa doble columnata del arquitecto Bernini. Duración 10 horas Idioma Inglés y español Incluye pase de admisión para la la Audiencia del Papa asistente por la mañana durante la Audiencia tiquets para saltar la cola de accesso a los Museos Vaticanos guía, auriculares almuerzo Punto de encuentro Via della Traspontina, 6 o servicio gratuito de recogida de hoteles céntricos. Final Plaza de San Pedro – traslados a los hoteles no esta incluido. IMPORTANTE: El Museo requiere que los clientes en silla de ruedas sigan un itinerario diferente y no estan autorizados permitido a realizar nuestro tour habitual. No es permitido entrar en la Iglesias en pantalón corto, hombros descubiertos, minifaldas. Esta asimismo prohibido entrar en el Museo con objetos de metal, paraguas y mochilas. Si la Basílica de San Pedro está cerrada para cerimonias religiosas,en sostitucion se visitará la Galeria de arte. Solo para la Audiencia Papal: el asistente o guía puede hablar en dos idiomas y e grupo puede se superior a 15 personas. El asiento durante la Audiencia Papal no está garantizado. Los tiquets de admisión para la Audiencia Papal son gratuítos.

data.name: IKONO Roma: Immersive Experience
data.description:
Step out of your comfort zone and dive into a unique experience you will never forget!

IKONO is the new immersive experience in the heart of Rome, just steps from the Pantheon.

Unleash your inner creativity in an exciting and unforgettable one-hour journey through nine surreal, and immersive exploration zones.

During your visit, you will interact with more than 12 never-seen-before interactive and artistic installations that combine sensory stimulation with cutting-edge technology.

Unlike traditional art galleries, in IKONO you're the real protagonist!

From the "Roman Thermae" with its giant ball pit to the "Tokyo Street" with its surreal atmosphere and exciting activities, IKONO Roma is an experience like no other.

This extraordinary adventure is suitable for people of all ages. The only requirement is to make each space yours! Are you ready to dive in?

data.name: Vatican, Sistine Chapel, and St Peter Basilica Private Tour
data.description: Uncover the history of Rome on a private tour of the Vatican, Sistine Chapel, and St Peter's Basilica on this private tour. Avoid getting overwhelmed by the sheer amount of beautiful art, and get insight into Italian history, culture, and art you would miss while visiting independently. Immerse yourself in the spectacular scenery without being held back by crowds or heat. Get ready for an unforgettable tour.

data.name: Private Rome by night
data.description: Meet your expert guide at your hotel by 5:30 PM and enjoy a relaxing panoramic tour of Rome by car. Discover the magical charm of the most famous monuments viewed under another light. Stop at Trevi Fountain, where you can throw your coin to make a wish and come back to Rome! After the three-hour tour, your guide will take you to a traditional Italian restaurant (the dinner is not included*). After dinner, your driver will drop you off at your hotel. *We inform that dinner is not included. If customers wish, we can book a restaurant according to their needs and budget, the menu will be a la carte and payment by customers to the restaurant. Please inform at the time of booking if customers want a table reservation in a restaurant.

data.name: Rome Private Sightseeing Day Tour With Lunch and Pickup
data.description: Short on sightseeing time but long on Rome landmarks you want to check out? Tick a host of essential city sights, like the Colosseum and Trevi Fountain, from your bucket list with this private sightseeing tour. With lunch at a classic Roman joint and convenient round-trip hotel pickup included, the experience is even more seamless.

data.name: Rome Private Evening Golf Cart Tour, Aperitivo
data.description: Discover the magic of Rome at night with this private golf cart tour through the Eternal City. Starting at the historic Piazza della Repubblica, you’ll cruise past iconic landmarks like the Circus Maximus, the Aventine Hill with its stunning Orange Garden, and the enchanting Trevi Fountain. Along the way, indulge in Italian aperitivos, prosecco, craft beer, and local snacks as your guide shares stories of Rome’s rich history and culture.

data.name: Rome Squares Private Piazzas Walking Tour
data.description: Wander through Rome’s most iconic public squares on a private walking tour from Piazza Venezia to Piazza della Minerva. While many travelers rush through the piazzas en route to Rome’s more well-known landmarks, this immersive stroll takes in the beauty and history of the city’s favourite gathering spots. Explore grand fountains and tucked-away courtyards and learn about the role of piazzas in daily Roman life.

data.name: Barberini Palace & Galleria Corsini: Entry Ticket
data.description: Age before beauty? Not when it comes to art! See both combined at Palazzo Barberini, home to Renaissance highlights from Raphael, Caravaggio and more. See the frescoed ceiling, crucifixes and works by regional painters of popes and cardinals and get free access to Palazzo Corsini.

data.name: A Day in Tuscany: Siena & San Gimignano by Minivan
data.description: A step back to Medieval Tuscany! About Visit two of the gems of Italy, both declared by UNESCO A World Heritage Site: Siena, famous for its medieval cityscape and the “ Palio”, the traditional medieval horse race held twice a year in Piazza del Campo, heart of the city, one of the most remarkable squares in Italy; the charming town of San Gimignano, a small village enclosed with 13th century walls, that still retains its feudal atmosphere and appearance, famous also for the production of the white wine called Vernaccia. Walking through the old city means plunging into the Middle Ages. In between, there will be a stop for wine and food tasting of local products (8 different types of wine, a selection of salami and cheese, the ” Ribollita” vegetable soup and the typical Lasagna with truffle). Duration 13 hours Itinerary Siena San Gimignano Rome Language Tour may be in two languages: englis and Spanish What is included transportation by A/C minivan with English speaking driver (2-7 pax) or English speaking tour escort (8-14 pax) guide in Siena headsets wine and food tasting Meeting point our Agency in Via Santamaura, 28 at 06:45 a.m or free pickup service.

data.name: Rome: Small-Group Cocktail-Making Class (Drinks Included)
data.description: In Italy, the pre-dinner cocktail, known as the *aperitivo*, is an institution; but how can you recreate the experience once your vacation ends? During this cocktail-making workshop in Rome, learn how to concoct three classic Italian mixed drinks, just like an Italian bartender. Then, sit back and enjoy your creation, paired with complimentary snacks.

data.name: Rome: Private Photography Walking Tour
data.description: Capture your time in the Eternal City on this private photography tour of Rome. Go beyond the usual tourist attractions as you follow your local guide to ancient, medieval, and modern neighborhoods, canals, cafes, hidden alleys, and markets for those perfect shots that capture the city's colorful atmosphere.

data.name: Rome National Gallery of Modern Art kid-friendly art workshop
data.description: Bring the whole family for a cultural exploration of the National Gallery of Modern Art on this child-friendly private tour. After exploring the museum’s various modern art installations, your kids will have the chance to create their own pieces of art inside the museum, while you learn more about the movements and ideas behind each exhibit.

data.name: UNESCO Jewels: Florence by high-speed train & Uffizi Skip-the-Line Tickets
data.description: Optimize your time and visit one of the most beautiful cities in the world, Florence. On board of a high speed train you'll reach Florence city centre in just 1 hour and 30 min. approx. At the station, meet your assistant and start your trip. The tour includes Access the splendid Uffizi Gallery with no line, Your assistant will indicate the meeting point and time to reach the Uffizi Gallery. Visit at your pace this one of the most important art collections in the world. Masterpieces from Giotto, Cimabue, Botticelli will amaze you! During the day you have the opportunity to discover the jewel of Middle Ages and Renaissance of Italy. Florence is considered the Cradle of the Renaissance, known worldwide for its treasures of art and architecture. Enjoy the squares, the streets, the masterpieces. A nice walk back to the station will complete this day in Florence. Take your return trip to Rome

data.name: Rome Private Highlights Tour with Trevi Fountain and Pantheon
data.description: Seeing the highlights of Rome in just a few hours can be difficult if you don't know your way around the city. Save time and avoid hassle by going with a guide instead. Visit famous attractions such as the Pantheon, the Spanish Steps, and the Travi Fountain and learn about the city's rich history from your own private guide.

data.name: Vatican Museums & St. Peter's Basilica: Fast Track Ticket + Guided Tour
data.description:
Say goodbye to waiting in line – jump straight into the exceptional Vatican collections, Sistine Chapel & Basilica with a knowledgeable guide in a small group.

Step into the grand Basilica of St. Peter and the Vatican Grottoes below. This comprehensive tour is perfect for those keen to see all that the Vatican has to offer.

In the Vatican Museums, you'll find an extensive range of art and numerous gallery displays with incredible pieces inside.

You'll see amazing sculptures, frescoes, and architectural designs that this collection is famous for.

Admire the sculptures, tapestries, paintings, and architectural works of Renaissance masters such as Bramante, Bernini, Perugino, Botticelli, D’Antonio, Rosselli, Signorelli, Della Gatta, Ghirlandaio, Raphael, and the Sistine Chapel, adorned with Michelangelo’s one-of-a-kind frescoes.

data.name: Frascati Private Wine Tasting Tour From Rome
data.description: Visit the hills of the Castelli Romani—a wine-producing region with volcanic landscapes—for wine tasting in a local winery and farmhouse. Meet the winemaker, tour the vineyards and cellars, and learn about local wine production. Taste three varieties of wine paired with specialties such as pizza, olive oil, and fruits and vegetables from the farmhouse garden.

data.name: Sistine Chapel Vatican City Walking Tour
data.description: Embark on an unforgettable journey through the heart of the Vatican with our exclusive, skip-the-line guided tour. Discover the Vatican Museums, home to the world’s most extraordinary collection of art, from ancient sculptures to Renaissance masterpieces. Marvel at Raphael’s Rooms, the Gallery of Maps, and the breathtaking Sistine Chapel, where Michelangelo’s iconic frescoes come to life. Led by an official Vatican guide, you’ll gain deep insight into the history, art, and spirituality of this sacred place. With personal headsets included, you won’t miss a word of the fascinating stories that bring these masterpieces to life. Book now and experience the Vatican like never before!

data.name: Art and History of Florence: Semi-Private Tour of the Uffizi Gallery
data.description: The city played an important role in the civilization of the Western world and Italy. The Renaissance, which began in Florence, was a period of great cultural, scientific, and artistic progress. It was a time when many famous artists, architects, and painters such as Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, and Raphael made their home in the city. Their works can be seen in the many monuments, churches, and buildings throughout Florence. To make it easier for you to experience Florence, our tour provides transportation by high-speed train from Rome to Florence, making the journey quick and convenient. Just meet your tour leader at the meeting point indicated, next to Termini railway station, where they will check you in and escort you to the train. Once you arrive in Florence, our travel assistant will meet you at the train station and accompany you to the meeting point of the guided tour. This will give you the opportunity to ask any questions you may have and to learn more about Florence before the tour begins. On your tour, a local guide will share the city's fascinating history and cultural highlights, including the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, Giotto's Campanile, the Florence Baptistery, Piazza della Repubblica, the Church and Museums of Orsanmichele, the Ponte Vecchio, and Piazza Signoria. Next, it's time to head to the world-famous Uffizi Gallery, where you'll skip the line and have the chance to admire some of the most iconic artworks in history. Botticelli's The Birth of Venus, Caravaggio's Medusa, Artemisia Gentileschi's Judith Beheading Holofernes, Titian's Venus of Urbino, and countless other masterpieces by the likes of Leonardo, Michelangelo, and Raphael await you. Your local guide will contextualize their origins and share fascinating stories about each piece, revealing their secrets and helping you appreciate them on a whole new level. After your visit, you'll have plenty of free time to explore the city at your leisure and grab a bite to eat at a local restaurant or bar (not included in the price). Then, you'll meet your assistant at the designated time and head back to the train station for a cozy ride back to Rome in the late afternoon. Overall, this semi-private guided tour to Florence and the Uffizi Gallery by high-speed train is the perfect way to experience one of Italy's most beautiful and culturally rich cities in a fun and informative way. Don't miss out on this unforgettable day-trip!

data.name: Rome Colosseum Guided Tour With Optional Arena Access
data.description: Navigating the Colosseum, the largest amphitheatre ever built, is a little daunting, especially for first-time visitors. Fully immerse yourself in its ancient history with this tour. Let your guide lead you around, sharing the stories and cultural impact of this landmark. Choose to upgrade your tour to include access to the arena floor, where gladiators fought. Perfect for those wanting to dedicate a little time on their vacation to exploring the Colosseum.

data.name: Castel Sant'Angelo: Hosted Priority Entry Ticket
data.description:
Discover Castel Sant'Angelo, a museum on the right bank of the Tiber River. Originally a grand tomb, the Castel Sant'Angelo has served as a medieval fortress and a defense against invasions.

Explore five floors, go through former Papal residence rooms, and see the chamber of ashes. Here you'll see frescoes and the remains of notable Roman figures.

The visit ends on the castle's roof terrace, with stunning views of Rome, including the Vatican City, the Tiber River, and the Bridge of Angels.

data.name: Skip the line Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel Guided Tour
data.description:
Discover the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel without getting overwhelmed by the massive collections with this guided tour. With skip-the-line tickets, spend less time in line and more in awe inside the galleries and Raphael Rooms.

Through your headset, you'll hear fascinating stories of Renaissance artists like Michelangelo and Raphael from your guide, getting unique insights into their remarkable masterpieces—and lifelong rivalry. End with time to marvel at the Sistine Chapel.

data.name: Saint Peter’s Tour: guided tour of Basilica and Dome (Spanish Language)
data.shortDescription:
A wonderful journey into the heart of Christianity: St Peter’s Basilica and its majestic dome are the very embodiement of faith, a wonderful monument that welcomes thousands of tourists and pilgrims from all over the world every year. The guided tour that we propose will take you inside the the Basilica and up to the top of the Dome: together with one of our guides – all specialised and accredited by the Vatican City – you will discover the priceless treasures hidden inside.

Molded upon the remains of the original Basilica built by the will of emperor Constantine, St Peter’s is the product of the joint efforts by artists who have shaped the history of art: Michelangelo, Bramante and Bernini for nearly 200 years contributed to the creation of the world admired Basilica. With its perfect architectural balance and ageless harmony, St Peter’s Basilica is like a preciuos chest, preserving extraordinary elements of history, culture and above all art.

Among the marvellous works of art preserved inside, you will admire the famous Pietà by Michelangelo, a true hymn to beauty and perfection that Buonarroti sculpted when he was only twenty-four years old and the sole of his statues to bear the artist’s signature. You will admire Bernini’s famous bronze canopy, commissioned by Pope Urban VIII Barberini, with its unique and gigantic twisted columns, between whose tendrils rest the Barberini bees, symbol of the family itself.

Bernini is also the author of the marble basement of the canopy, displaying the face of a woman during the various phases of labor, from the beginning of contractions to childbirth; a highly original homage to the Mater Ecclesia (the Mother Church of all other Churches). After about 3 hrs.of tour inside the Basilica, your guide will take you to the parvis to tell you the story of Bernini’s colonnade and talk about the fountains, the Vatican Obelisk, the Wind Rose and show you the famous Heart of Nero.

data.name: Highlights of Rome Private Bike Tour
data.description: Discover the highlights of the Eternal City on two wheels with this private bike tour. Follow your guide around a selection of Rome’s notable landmarks, including the Colosseum, the Pantheon, and the Mouth of Truth. Enjoy a full itinerary that doesn’t feel overwhelming thanks to the speed a bike offers. This tour is great for visitors who like to keep active while sightseeing on vacation.

data.name: Rome Small-Group Cooking Class with Market Tour
data.description:
Wait in your central Rome hotel for pickup, then travel into the city to discover a food market that traces its roots back to 1928. Breathe in the aromas of fresh food as your guide gives the lowdown on the ingredients you’re about to use.

Leave the market and head to the cooking venue where your masterclass takes place. With the help of a pro chef, then prepare a pasta or pizza dish from scratch. Mix up the ingredients, experiment with different flavors to create your ideal dish, and hear fun tips to help you cook like an Italian.

Take a seat when the class ends, then savor your creations with the rest of your group. Sip on local wine from the surrounding Lazio area, and chat about Italian food with your chef and group. Your experience then ends with a hotel drop-off.

data.name: Rome Small-Group Roman Forum, Palatine Hill, Circus Maximus
data.description: See three of Rome’s most important ancient attractions, save time, and beat the crowds: this small-group tour offers a hassle-free way to discover the sights. Pick from several convenient daily tour times, and meet your group near the Colosseum. Venture first to the Roman Forum, home to legions of artifacts, before venturing up to the Palatine Hill. Finally, discover the largest stadium ever built by mankind: the Circus Maximus.

data.name: Capitoline Museums: Skip The Line Ticket + Multimedia Video
data.shortDescription: Explore the world's oldest museum along with a video introduction
data.description:
Welcome to the oldest museum in the world. The Roman Empire Museum (Musei Capitolini) dates all the way back to 1471, making it the first art museum in history.

Located at the summit of Capitoline Hill for almost 600 years, this gallery affords timeless views of the Eternal City, and is a fascinating window into thousands of years of Rome's history.

data.name: Roma: San Clemente Underground & Basilica
data.description: A visit of the 12th century Basilica of San Clemente reveals a gleaming gold mosaic above the central apse. St. Clement's transformed over centuries from a private home that was the site of a secret Christian worship in the first century to an imposing basilica. What laid beneath the Basilica was unknown until 1860, when flooding led an Irish Dominican Roman Catholic priest and archaeologist into the levels beneath the basilica floor. Excavations are ongoing. Today, you can descend up to 100 feet underground over three levels. At the first level we will find a 4th century Basilica, long forgotten after the construction of the 12th century Basilica above. Underneath, find the remains of an ancient pagan Mitraic temple. Lower still, ruins of ancient Roman homes.

data.name: Colosseum's Attic Tour with 3rd, 4th and 5th Levels
data.description: Venture up to the rarely seen attic levels of the Colosseum—the 3rd, 4th, and 5th tiers—for a unique perspective on ancient Roman life. Once home to the lower classes, these upper sections reveal preserved inscriptions, traces of white plaster, and unforgettable views of Rome. Accessible by panoramic lift and steep stairs, this experience offers a powerful glimpse into the Colosseum’s grand scale and the vibrant atmosphere of its ancient crowds.

data.name: Pasta Academy Private lesson
data.description:
Immerse yourself in the culinary traditions of Rome with our hands-on cooking class. Led by expert chefs in a historic Roman wine cellar, you will discover the secrets of Italian cuisine passed down through the generations.

From rolling out pasta by hand to creating the perfect sauces, this intimate and interactive experience guarantees personalized guidance and a deep understanding of traditional Italian cooking techniques.

data.name: Rome Pizza and Gelato-Making Cooking Class with Wine
data.description: Take advantage of your time in Rome and go a step beyond simply eating pizza and gelato by taking a cooking class. Whether you’re confident in the kitchen or consider yourself a beginner, you'll improve your skills with insights from a professional chef. Get access to premium toppings during this hands-on workshop.

data.name: Colosseum Attic Tour
data.description:
Explore the upper levels of the Colosseum with a visit to the Belvedere, where you can experience breathtaking views and uncover the hidden layers of Rome’s ancient past. Climb to the 3rd, 4th, and 5th tiers to witness how spectators once watched gladiators clash far below. Walk through restricted areas, gaze out over the Roman Forum, and capture stunning photos from above the arena floor. Discover the genius of Roman engineering as you stand where history echoes in every stone. Feel the atmosphere of the amphitheater from a whole new perspective and immerse yourself in the grandeur of Imperial Rome.

In short, the Colosseum Belvedere elevates your visit, literally and figuratively, by offering history, views, and atmosphere you can't get at ground level.

data.name: Hills of Ancient Rome Segway Tour
data.description: Rome wasn't built in a day but you can see its glory in just a few hours. Ancient Rome will take shape before your eyes as your Segway brings you up and down the city’s famous 7 hills, discovering many monuments and hidden sites of the 'eternal city'.

data.name: Typical Italian dinner with a Roman family
data.description:
Join the latest culinary trend of immersive and social dining where local hosts invite you into their homes for a magical meal.

Join Andrea and his wife at their home in Rome for a delicious Italian dinner that will make you feel like a member of their family! • 3-course Italian dinner in a family atmosphere • Wine is included • Easily accessible by public transportation • Communal dining for 2 to 6 people • Andrea is an engineer and hosts with his wife About your host, Andrea: "I spent my whole life traveling around the world. I enjoy meeting new people and sharing good meals with them."

data.name: Rome Small-Group Tour with Pantheon Entry Ticket
data.description: See Rome's highlights in just 90 minutes on this small-group walking tour with Pantheon entry. For travelers short on time, this experience offers a meaningful way to explore without feeling rushed or overwhelmed. Stroll from Piazza Venezia to the Trevi Fountain, and conclude your experience with access to the Pantheon.

data.name: Turano Valley Private Day Trip With Hiking and Lunch
data.description: Located just one hour from Rome by car, the Turano Valley may be the Lazio region’s best-kept secret. This private tour covers much of the area, hiking to an abandoned medieval village, stopping for a guided tour of Castel Di Tora, and offering lunch with wine at a local agriturismo. Arrange pickup from Rome or Carsoli for an added cost.

data.name: Florence and Tuscany Day Tour from Rome by High-Speed Train
data.description: Make the most of your time in Italy with a day trip to Florence from Rome. Cut travel time in half with a 1.5 hour high-speed train, and arrive ready for a walking tour of its landmarks, from the Duomo to the Ponte Vecchio. Travel to a Tuscan vineyard for an intimate wine tasting and light lunch, followed by a wander around the medieval town of San Gimignano.

data.name: Tour of Rome:Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps,Pantheon with Italian Ice Cream
data.description:
Begin at Piazza della Minerva and meet your local guide before entering the Pantheon, one of Rome’s best-preserved ancient sites. Learn how it was once dedicated to all gods, and admire the world’s largest unreinforced concrete dome, complete with an open-air oculus. You’ll also glimpse the tombs of the painter Raphael and Italy’s former royals, including King Victor Emmanuel II and Queen Margherita.

Next, head to the Gothic-style Basilica of Santa Maria sopra Minerva, built where three pagan temples once stood. Highlights include a Michelangelo sculpture, 15th-century frescoes, and an altarpiece believed to be by Fra Angelico. Beneath the altar lies the headless body of Saint Catherine of Siena, adding one more layer of history to this fascinating tour.

data.name: VIP Experience Private Transfer from the Civitavecchia Port to Rome
data.description: Traveling has never been so comfortable. A journey is not just a transfer from one place to another, but it is an experience. For that reason nothing is left to chance.  A driver will be waiting for you outside the Cruise ship, to make sure you can avoid any inconvenience. After comfortably passing the checks you will see him waiting with a sign with your name written on top so you can easily recognize him. At this point he will take care of you and your personal effects, you will just have to sit in a luxury Mercedes, where you will find a bottle of water and a map of Rome. From this moment, Rome is in your hands and if you choose the tour option, the driver will stop in front of all the iconic places of the city and will explain some little anecdote and a bit of history to make you feel like you're no longer a foreigner but a local friend.

data.name: Galleria Borghese Entrance Ticket with Optional Guided Tour
data.description: Exploring Galleria Borghese is a must-do in Rome, showcasing the brilliance of Bernini, Caravaggio, Canova, and Raphael. We have the perfect options for you! Choose from a guided tour for an insightful exploration or an independent visit with our skip-the-line ticket.Embark on a journey through art history within the majestic walls of the former Villa Borghese. Behold the cardinal's remarkable collection, including Canova's neoclassical depiction of Pauline Bonaparte and the dynamic sculptures of Bernini and Caravaggio.For those opting for the ticket-only entry, dive into the art world at your own pace, enjoying the liberty to immerse yourself in each masterpiece individually. Our guided tour promises a profound and memorable exploration of the gallery's treasures.The Borghese Gallery houses important works collected by Cardinal Scipione Borghese, including stunning sculptures inspired by. Notable are Canova's portrait of Pauline Bonaparte and Bernini's iconic sculptures like Apollo and Daphne, highlighting the gallery's rich history and artistic diversity.Caravaggio's, Titian's, and Raphael's paintings add to the gallery's allure, showcased alongside numerous other masterpieces. The sale of a significant part of the Borghese collection to Napoleon led to the foundation of what is now part of the Louvre Museum's collection.

data.name: Skip-the-line Vatican and Sistine Chapel Private Tour including St.Peter's
data.description: The Vatican Museums houses an extensive collection of artworks, gathered by the Popes over the centuries, including the masterpieces by legendary authors such as Raphael, Michelangelo, Caravaggio and many more. Skip the long lines with your fast access tickets and head straight inside to explore the most remarkable pieces of art. You will see the gallery of statues, the gallery of geographic maps, the Raphael's Rooms, the Sistine Chapel, Michelangelo's Last Judgment, the Pietà, the Basilica of St. Peter and other significant art treasures.With your top-rated guide you will discover small curiosities, learn more about important artworks and enjoy entertaining commentary with lots of facts and anecdotes only an expert insider knows.During this tour you will discover all the most important masterpieces of the Vatican Museums, the Sistine Chapel, and the St. Peter's Basilica.First, your guide will take you through the gallery of statues. You will discover the most famous and important artworks from Greek and Roman art, including the Apollo of the Belvedere, the Laocoon, the Torso, the busts of Hadrian and his lover Antinous. Here you will also see the sarcophagi of Helen and Constance, the mother and the daughter of Emperor.Next, you will visit the Gallery of Candelabra with the exotic statue of Ephesian Artemis,  the Gallery of Tapestries, the Sobieski Hall, and the famous Rooms of Raphael, where the painter and his disciples decorated the apartments of Pope Julius II.After that, you will reach the Sistine Chapel, the most visited attraction of the Vatican City. Decorated by Michelangelo between 1508 and 1512, this magnificent Renaissance masterpiece comprises a series of frescoes of great artistic importance. You will see the Last Judgment, the Stories of Moses and Jesus, the Creation of Adam and many more.After visiting the museums you will discover the Saint Peter’s Basilica, the largest Catholic Church in the world and a true architectural wonder. Here you will  see another one of Michelangelo’s masterpieces, La Pietà.Your Vatican tour will end a tthe beautiful Saint Peter’s Square, the great work of architect Bernini with plenty of symbols, saints and more than 200 columns.

data.name: Private tour Assisi & St. Franci's Basilica with pick-up
data.description: Join us on this classic journey, departing from Rome to explore the beauty of the Umbria region and its many treasures. Assisi Assisi is a beautiful medieval town that was founded by the ancient Roman Empire. After the fall of the Roman Empire it was dominated by the Goths and later, the Logobards. After the year 1000, it saw the extraordinary spread of the monastic movement and particularly the Benedictines. Around 1180 Saint Francis was born, the most famous of the sons of Assisi. The son of a rich merchant, he grew as a young noble of Assisi but dissatisfied with his life, he turned to prayer and service to the poor. In 1206, he publicly renounced his father's wealth. Pope Innocent III approved his way of life, gave him and his disciples permission to preach on moral topics, and had Francis ordained a deacon. With the collaboration of Saint Clare of Assisi, Francis founded a branch of his order for women, called the Poor Clares. St Francis is one of the most important and beloved Saints of Catholicism. St Francis Basilica The church of St. Francis of Assisi stands today in the place where the Saint had asked to be buried. The building of the basilica began in 1228 and was completed after just two years. The building is consists of two churches, one above the other with each in a completely different style: the upper level is Gothic and the lower is Austere. Inside you'll admire frescoes by Giotto and see the shrines of St Francis, discovered in 1818, through excavations of the space beneath the altar. St. Claire Basilica The Basilica of St. Clare of Assisi, constructed in pink stone native to the region, houses many precious frescoes. It is dedicated to Santa Chiara, daughter of a noble family. During her years of education, the Saint followed the crusaders to the Promised Land. Then during the night of Palm Sunday on March 18th 1212, she made the major life decision to secretly join St. Francesco at the "Porziuncola". As a ritual of initiation, the Saint was covered with a Franciscan frock and her hair was cut as a sign of penitence. This marked the beginning of her new life, retired from the world to a place of extreme poverty and simplicity. Within the Basilica, there is a chapel on the right that is dedicated to her and an amazing Crucifix in the center of the church which, according to tradition, invited St. Francesco to the church of St. Damiano in order to "reset up the Church". St. Mary of the Angels in Assisi Santa Maria degli Angeli is a small village close to Assisi that takes its name from the sixteenth century Basilica which dominates the flat base of Assisi. After the year 1,000, this area took the name of Porziuncola. This place is considered the home of the Franciscan order. In 1216, St. Francis saw a vision in which Jesus stated that anyone who had visited the church, duly confessed and communicated, would receive forgiveness for their sins. Pope Honorius III approved this indulgence and officially declared the 1st and 2nd of August each year to be Days of Forgiveness. To this very day, this yearly event continues draw a large number of religious tourists from around the world.
