data.name: Ancient Rome: Colosseum, Palatine Hill & Roman Forum
data.description: About This tour is a chance to visit the 3 sites of the Colosseum's Archaeological Park with a licensed guide. Also known as the Flavian Amphitheatre, the Colosseum is one of the most famous monuments in the world. Opened with a solemn inauguration that lasted 100 days, it was used for gladiatorial fights and wild animal hunts. It had a capacity for more than 50.000 people and the ability to protect the spectators with a large awning called Velarium. It’s 2.000 years old but the Colosseum is still the symbol of the Eternal City. The Palatine Hill, one of the seven hills of Rome, is considered "the first nucleus of the Roman Empire" because has been the location where Romulus and Remus were found by the she-wolf and where Rome has its origins. With the development of Rome, it became the most exclusive neighborhood where emperors and patrician families built opulent palaces and the site is now mainly a large open-air museum. From the Palatine, the tour will across the Roman Forum, for centuries the center of Roman public and economic life, where the most important structures of the ancient city were located. data.name: Appia Antica and Rome's Underground Labyrinth by Ebike: an experience between light and shadow without comparison
data.description: Imagine cycling on the Via Appia Antica, one of the oldest and most historic roads in the world. Feel under the wheels the same stones that supported Roman chariots and pilgrims. The air smells of history, and the landscape transports you back in time.Cycling along the Appian Way is like leafing through a living history book. Every kilometer traveled is a chapter to discover: monumental tombs, majestic aqueducts, ancient villas... Every stone tells a story, and you are the protagonist of this adventure.But the real surprise awaits you underground. In the Roman Quarry of the Caffarella park, a labyrinth of hand-dug tunnels opens up to your eyes. It is a unique experience, a dive into the heart of underground Rome. Here, where pozzolana was extracted for centuries to build the city, you can cycle through the ancient tunnels, touch the walls dug by slaves and imagine the life of those who worked in these dark depths.Whether you are a history enthusiast, a nature lover or simply an explorer, this tour is the perfect combination capable of offering you unique emotions. Leave the usual tourist itineraries and book now to immerse yourself in an authentic and evocative atmosphere.Do you want an even more authentic and personalized experience? Book the “Private Tour” option. You will have the local guide exclusively for you!

data.name: Colosseum & Ancient Rome+ Lunch + Vatican Museums

The itinerary includes Pio Clementino Hall, Laocoon and Apollo Belvedere, Maps Gallery, Candelabra Gallery, Tapestries Gallery and one of the most celebrated masterpieces in the world: the Sistine Chapel, with the breathtaking frescoes by Michelangelo. Leaving the Museum, follow your guide along the gigantic walls of the Vatican City and reach St. Peter's Square, dominated by Michelangelo's imposing Cupola and surrounded by the famous Bernini's double Colonnade, which houses St. Peter's Basilica the most important Christian church in the world Duration 8 hours Highlights Colosseum Palatine Hill Roman Forum Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel St. Peter's Basilica (from outside) St. Peter’s Square Language English Included Skip the line entrance tickets Professional licensed guide Headsets Lunch (drinks non included) Pick up service from centrally located hotels (when selected) Not included Drop off at the hotels Please note Not wheelchair accessible The itinerary may vary depending on Colosseum entrance time availability It is forbidden to bring metal objects and big bags It is not permitted to wear shorts, miniskirts and have uncovered shoulders Please advise for any food allergies, dietary restrictions or other special requirements Meeting point Big Bus Tours / Brastours Kiosk in Piazza del Colosseo or pick up from centrally located hotels

data.name: Private Tour to Siena and San Gimignano with Visit to a Wine Cellar in Tuscany from Rome
data.description: From Rome, enjoy the Tuscany culture and get to know its famous wines, aperitifs, and cultural heritage up close Duration 12 hours About Tuscany is one of the most beautiful and easy-to-love places in Italy, and it's hard not to see why. The limitless number of vineyards, rolling hills, wine, great-tasting cheese, gelato- the list goes on and on. The region is full of greenery, character, and friendly locals. You would truly enjoy your visit to Tuscany. The first destination planned in Tuscany is San Gimignano. This small area is located on top of a large hill that overlooks the rolling hills of Tuscany. From the top of the tower in San Gimignano check out the best views of Tuscany and the wineries, which are just a stone's throw away. Siena is the next name on the list to visit Tuscany. Over the years, the city has accumulated so much wealth due to successful banking, which has aided them in maintaining an element of grandeur in many ways. The landscape in Siena is unparalleled, and upon arrival, you would feel as though you've been taken right back into the Middle Ages. In this area, you see a sea of terracotta-toned houses lined up in the neighborhoods, along with gigantic sights (especially the cathedral!). All these sights give you the impression of being in the backdrop of a movie. There is much to discover and enjoy in Siena; the tour leader will engage you in activities to partake in while in the city. Tuscany has a wonderful wine culture, and it is a huge part of its history, one of the most important is the Chianti wine. The world's most famous wines are from the heart of Tuscany, and you get to visit a winery near San Gimignano. Here you will be able to taste 15 varieties of wine and oil, besides local appetizers like Tuscany cheese, salami, and the famous bruschetta! Among the perks of this tour, you get to be transported in an air-conditioned bus, and you are ensured of comfort throughout the journey from Rome to Tuscany. Along the tour to the winery, you not only get to taste great wines but also have a light lunch there in the winery. Learn about the history of Tuscany, its wine, and the beloved cities from the tour leader. And enjoy a beautiful day trip to one of the great regions of Italy. data.name: The Catacombs of Saints Marcellin and Peter: Guided Tour
data.shortDescription: See where the martyrs of the persecution of Diocletian are buried in Rome
data.description:
The two martyrs, St Marcellinus and St Peter were slain in the persecution of 304 AC and lost their heads – quite literally – in Rome. It gets worse. Before they were killed, they were forced to dig their own tomb, with their own hands. 

Explore the gruesome history yourself when you enter the ancient catacombs, which span an area of ​​18,000 square meters. Your guide will lead you through this underground graveyard, which spans three levels and was excavated between the 3rd and 5th centuries AD. Roughly 20,000 and 25,000 people will be resting in peace around you, along with numerous martyrs of the persecution of Diocletian. 

See the tombstones that cover the niches (known as loculi), and get a peek at early Christian inscriptions on the marble tombstones. A fascinating look into the history of Rome.

data.name: Sistine Chapel & Vatican Museums Tour with breakfast
data.description: Don’t miss the chance to enter the Sistine Chapel as a VIP. Thanks to our privileged access to the Sistine Chapel (one hour before usual opening time) you’ll admire Michelangelo’s Last Judgment masterpiece with only a bunch of other lucky people. Usually, no talking is allowed inside the Sistine Chapel, but at this early hour you will have the incredible opportunity to hear the explanations of your guide right as you behold the Chapel’s amazing paintings. After looking at the powerful frescoes inside the Sistine Chapel, your expert guide will lead you to the Raphael’s rooms and the so-called upper galleries. After taking in all the beauty the Vatican has to offer, you will reach the beautiful Cortile della Pigna and have an American-style breakfast, right in the same courtyard where popes entertained their guests for centuries. This Vatican Museums experience will be memorable and intimate, a once-in-a-lifetime experience. data.name: Trevi Fountain Rome: 40-Min Underground Domus Guided Tour
data.shortDescription: Discover the most famous fountain in the world and what lies beneath
data.description:
Did you know that a 2,000-year-old Roman aqueduct supplies water to the most famous fountain in the world?

Meet your guide and find out how the Trevi Fountain is much more than a throw of a coin. Go beyond its captivating beauty and discover all the details that most tourists miss.

Learn about its fascinating history and discover the mythological figures that take shape gracefully out of the raw stone below. 

Feel and hear the power of water, and perceive the message of this iconic masterpiece exactly as intended by its designer. Take a moment to admire the fusion of beauty and genius. 

Then immerse yourself in the newly uncovered archeological site nine meters below the ground! Find the only functioning ancient aqueduct which still supplies water to the fountain above, and visit the remains of an imperial Domus.

Don't forget to throw a coin in the fountain before you go, but first, discover the legends about the origins of this peculiar tradition.

data.name: Roma Antigua: Coliseo, Palatino y Foro Romano - Tarde
data.description: Paseando a través de la historia: visita al Coliseo, símbolo de los tiempos de la antigua Roma y el área que la circunda, el sitio arqueológico más hermoso e importante del mundo. Ingreso sin esperas, max. 13 personas Sobre También conocido como el Anfiteatro de Flavio, el Coliseo es uno de los monumentos más famosos del mundo. Abierto al público con una solemne inauguración que duró 100 días, era usado para las luchas de los gladiadores (munera gladiatoria) con caza de animales salvajes (venationes) y, con la arena llena de agua, simulando batallas navales (naumachiae). Fue construido donde anteriormente había un lago artificial en la Domus Aurea de Nerón. Tenía capacidad para unas 73.000 personas con un gran toldo (velarium) el cual protegía a los espectadores del sol y la lluvia. Tiene 2.000 años de antigüedad, pero todavía hoy es el símbolo de la Ciudad Eterna. El Palatino, con el desarrollo de la ciudad, el continuo embellecimiento del Foro, y su proximidad al poder, se convirtió en un lugar de moda para vivir, con una exclusiva vecindad donde emperadores y familias patricias construyeron opulentos palacios. El Foro Romano fue durante siglos el centro de la vida pública y la economía de Roma, y allí fueron construidas las más importantes estructuras de la antigüedad. Duración 3 horas Idioma Español Incluye entrada de “salta la cola” guía auriculares. IMPORTANTE: esta prohibido entrar en el Coliseo con maletas, mochilas y bolsas voluminosas. No hay depósito de bolsa en el Coliseo. data.name: Basilica San Clemente: Underground Guided Tour
data.description:
Explore the 12th-century Basilica of San Clemente, an archaeological wonder near the Colosseum. Descend through three levels of subterranean mystery, each layer revealing over 2,000 years of intriguing history. The basilica boasts a gold mosaic that adds a shimmering glow to its central aisle.

Initially shrouded in mystery, the depths of San Clemente were uncovered in 1860 when a flood prompted an Irish Dominican priest and archaeologist to explore below. Ongoing excavations still unveil new secrets.

Descend a hundred feet, and the first level reveals a forgotten 4th-century basilica, overshadowed by the 12th-century basilica built above it.

Go deeper and find relics of an ancient Mithraic temple with its intact altar. Explore the skeletal remains of Roman houses, preserving a long-gone era. At the bottom, discover the underground spring that sparked the initial discovery.

data.name: Art and History of Florence: Semi-Private Tour of the Uffizi Gallery
data.description: Your adventure begins with a pick-up from your hotel and a short ride to Roma Termini railway station, where you'll be checked in and escorted onto the train by one of our friendly travel assistants. They'll share insider tips and information to help get you in the mood for your day-trip to Florence. Once you arrive in Florence, your assistant will accompany you to the meeting point of the guided walking tour, which starts in Piazza del Duomo. Here, a local guide will share the city's fascinating history and cultural highlights, including the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, Giotto's Campanile, the Florence Baptistery, Piazza della Repubblica, the Church and Museums of Orsanmichele, the Ponte Vecchio, and Piazza Signoria. Next, it's time to head to the world-famous Uffizi Gallery, where you'll skip the line and have the chance to admire some of the most iconic artworks in history. Botticelli's The Birth of Venus, Caravaggio's Medusa, Artemisia Gentileschi's Judith Beheading Holofernes, Titian's Venus of Urbino, and countless other masterpieces by the likes of Leonardo, Michelangelo, and Raphael await you. Your local guide will contextualize their origins and share fascinating stories about each piece, revealing their secrets and helping you appreciate them on a whole new level. After your visit, you'll have plenty of free time to explore the city at your leisure and grab a bite to eat at a local restaurant or bar (not included in the price). Then, you'll meet your assistant at the designated time and head back to the train station for a cozy ride back to Rome in the late afternoon. Overall, this semi-private guided tour to Florence and the Uffizi Gallery by high-speed train is the perfect way to experience one of Italy's most beautiful and culturally rich cities in a fun and informative way. Don't miss out on this unforgettable day-trip!

data.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum: Entry Ticket
data.shortDescription: Explore a museum dedicated to one of greatest minds of all time
data.description:
For over a decade, the Leonardo da Vinci Museum has been celebrating the Renaissance genius of Leonardo as an artist, but also as an inventor, scientist, anatomist, engineer and architect.

Located in the basement of the Basilica of Santa Maria del Popolo, the museum is just a five-minute walk from the Spanish Steps and Villa Borghese, in the charming Piazza del Popolo.

With your Leonardo da Vinci Museum tickets, you can discover interactive machines made by Italian craftsmen, based on Leonardo's manuscripts. Admire studies of some of his most famous Renaissance works, sketches of human anatomy, in-depth videos on _The Last Supper_ and _The Vitruvian Man_, and an immersive multimedia room that will take you on a journey into the life and mind of Leonardo da Vinci.

Divided into themed areas on Leonardo's studies and passions, every year the museum welcomes thousands of visitors from all over the world, making it the most visited Leonardo da Vinci museum in Rome.

data.name: Castel Sant'Angelo: Entry Ticket + Audio Guide
data.shortDescription: Admire the Castel Sant’Angelo museum and enjoy the view from the terrace
data.description:
Discover the history of this mausoleum-turned-museum with skip-the-line, hosted access. Located on the right bank of the Tiber and only a short distance from the Vatican City, the Castel Sant'Angelo is an ancient fortress with centuries of history.

Explore the museum's seven floors and see an extensive collection of ancient artifacts and perfectly preserved frescoes from the Renaissance period. Built in 135 AD for the Roman Emperor Hadrian, the building has played an important part in Rome’s architectural legacy.

Climb the spiral staircase to reach the Chamber of Ashes where a number of historical figures were incarcerated, before continuing up to visit the Papal Residence. Immerse yourself in the stories of different rooms as you admire the art within.

Wrap up your experience with a panoramic view over Rome and the River Tiber from the castle terrace. A great opportunity to take some photos of the Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge, also known as the Bridge of Angels.

data.name: Galleria Borghese: Guided Tour or Ticket only
data.description: Regardless of the chosen option, visiting the Galleria Borghese is absolutely a must during your Rome holiday! This art sanctuary showcases the genius of Bernini, Caravaggio, Canova, and Raphael. With Gray Line I Love Rome, select the experience that best suits your interests: a guided tour with intimate group sizes for a deeper understanding or a more independent exploration with our skip-the-line ticket. Each path leads to the heart of Italian art, amidst the splendor of the former Villa Borghese. Discover the cardinal's collection, the neoclassical allure of Pauline Bonaparte by Canova, and the dynamic expressions of Bernini and Caravaggio. For those choosing the entrance-only ticket, you’re set for an adventure at your own pace, with the freedom to absorb each masterpiece on your own terms. And if you wish for a structured journey, our guided tour ensures a memorable exploration. The gallery's most important sculptures and paintings come from the collection of Cardinal Scipione Borghese (1579 - 1633), patron and art collector, son of Ortensia Borghese, sister of Pope Paul V. The cardinal was a fervent admirer of all expressions of ancient, Renaissance and contemporary art and his strong ambition fostered the creation of sculptures and marble groups inspired by the canons of classical art. The portrait of Pauline Bonaparte Borghese, sculpted by Canova between 1805 and 1808, has been hosted by the Gallery since 1838: the emperor’s young sister is in the centre of the room and poses slightly reclined, with her torso lifted. Her right hand rests on the armrest of the Agrippina, while she clasps an apple in her left. The nude bust and the soft folds of the cloth covering the lower part of the princess' body make this work one of Bernini's masterpieces and one of the timeless icons of Neoclassical art. Bernini's works, including Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpine and The David, to name a few, are also undisputed protagonists of the Gallery's spaces and one cannot remain indifferent to them. The museum's collection of paintings is equally remarkable and includes wonderful works by Caravaggio, Tiziano, Correggio, and Raphael, all exhibited on the second floor of the building along with many others. In 1807, Camillo Borghese sold 154 statues, 160 busts, 170 bas-reliefs, 30 columns, and various vases to Napoleon, forming the Borghese collection of the Musée Napoléon, which was to become the Louvre Museum a few years later. After your visit, consider wandering through the expansive Villa Borghese gardens. This lush retreat, crowned by the Pincio Terrace, offers panoramic views of Rome’s historic landscape, a perfect epilogue to your gallery experience. Note: The total price of this product covers the booking fee and services fees for an enhanced experience

data.name: Florence Renaissance and Uffizi Ticket : Day Trip from Rome by High-Speed Train
data.description: Visit Florence with a comfortable one-day trip from Rome. Depart in the morning from Roma Termini train station and in just 2 hours you will reach the heart of Florence, the city of Renaissance! Once arrived in Florence, your skip-the-line Ticket for the Uffizi Gallery will allow you to visit all the art treasures and of the most renowned Renaissance artists in a completely independent way, without stress and wasting time! Included in your ticket entrance, our interactive and easy to use App will guide you inside the Museum. Feel free to spend as much time as you wish! Strolling down the marvelous halls of the gallery, you will be overwhelmed by the unrivaled beauty of the Ognissanti Madonna by Giotto, the Spring and Birth of Venus by Botticelli, the Annunciation and the Adoration of the Magi by Leonardo, the Tondo Doni by Michelangelo, the Bacchus by Caravaggio and many others. The rest of the day is at your leisure: you will have free time to explore the historic center of Florence, walk to the spectacular Piazza della Signoria, the iconic and picturesque Ponte Vecchio, and admire the beauty of the monumental complex of the Duomo, with the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore and the famous Brunelleschi's Dome. You can also enjoy some shopping, discovering unique art crafts in the numerous Florentine artisan shops, taste local products in one of the restaurants on the first floor of the Central Market or just sit at the table of a historic café in Piazza della Repubblica.

data.name: Rome in 1 Day: Colosseum & Vatican guided tour
data.description: Discover the masterpieces of Rome in one day on this tour of the Colosseum area & the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. You won't have to worry about waiting in long lines on this tour, we are here to ensure that you skip the lines and our expert guides will be there to give you an insider's point of view. The Colosseum One of the most popular and amazing buildings in the entire world. Access the Colosseum with no line and be ready to enter into the legend. Learn about architecture and history of this massive amphitheater which hosted ancient Romans, Senators, Emperors and Gladiators as well as animals from all over the world. You'll finally have the opportunity to visit the Palatine Hill, the place of foundation of Rome, and the Roman Forum from the inside. Get ready, as you will be visiting the Vatican Museums in the afternoon! Your trip to the Eternal City will never be complete without a visit to this unique site, which is home to 54 galleries that include 4 statue museums: * Museo Pio Clementino * Museo Chiaramonti * Museo Gregoriano Etrusco and * Museo Gregoriano-Egizio Get charmed by Michelangelo’s outstanding Sistine Chapel and Last Judgement, visit the extraordinary Raphael Rooms and get your fill of the stories behind the famous “School of Athens”, walking along the same hallways walked by some of the most famous artists in the world: Leonardo da Vinci, Caravaggio, Giotto, Raphael, and Michelangelo, to name a few.

data.name: Historic Pigneto Candlelight Happy Hour
data.description: Explore the vibrant and historic Pigneto district with our unique "Candlelight Happy Hour in the Pigneto District". Known for its bohemian atmosphere, this neighbourhood has been the backdrop for classic Italian films such as Pasolini’s "Accattone" and has evolved into one of Rome’s most dynamic areas for arts and nightlife. Your experience begins in the late afternoon, meeting at the Via Casilina exit of Metro C Pigneto Station. This area is deeply rooted in history, transitioning from an ancient Roman vineyard to a working-class suburb, and played a significant role during the resistance in World War II. Today, Pigneto is celebrated for its pedestrian streets lined with colourful murals, hip bars, and a diverse culinary scene. As the sun sets, you’ll be guided to an exclusive local venue known for its charm and historical significance. Here, beneath the modern streets, lies an ancient subterranean space where your happy hour takes place. This hidden gem provides a cool reprieve from the city buzz where you can enjoy the soft glow of candlelight and the rustic ambiance of aged brick walls. During the happy hour, you will indulge in a selection of specially chosen wines, each representing a different era of Italian winemaking history. These wines will be paired with a variety of traditional appetisers, including local cheeses and cured meats, homemade gnocchi, and classic focaccia. Each pairing is thoughtfully chosen to highlight the flavours and history of the region. Our food and wine connoisseur will provide insights into the historical significance of the dishes, the evolution of Pigneto’s culinary landscape, and the storied vineyards from which the wines hail. This tour not only offers a taste of Pigneto’s nightlife but also an immersive experience into the historical layers that define this unique Roman district, making it a must-do for those looking to discover the city beyond its tourist paths.

data.name: Piazze e Fontane di Roma
data.description: Scopriamo insieme i più suggestivi luoghi di Roma Riguardo il tour Piazza Navona, la piazza più elegante di Roma, un punto d'incontro cosmopolita con la famosa Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi del Bernini. É circondata anche da gelaterie, bar e ristoranti tipici. Chiesa di San Luigi ai Francesi, famosa perchè al suo interno conserva alcune delle opere più famose di Caravaggio. Pantheon, tempio Romano del 27 a.C. dedicato a tutti gli Dei, unico edificio Romano rimasto quasi intatto. Piazza Colonna prende il nome dalla presenza della colonna eretta dal Senato e dal Popolo Romano in onore di Marco Aurelio dopo la sua morte avvenuta nel 180 d.C. La piazza è rettangolare e circondata da edifici importanti, tra questi Palazzo Chigi, sede del governo. Fontana di Trevi, una delle fontane più famose del mondo, icona di Roma, la fontana barocca più grande. Piazza di Spagna, caratterizzata dalla famosa fontana de la Barcaccia, e dall'immensa scalinata di Piazza di Spagna che conduce fin su alla Chiesa di Trinità dei Monti. Zona elengante e ricca di boutique che rappresentano sia il lusso internazionale che il nostro Made in Italy. Durata 3 ore circa Itinerario: -Piazza Navona -Chiesa di San Luigi dei Francesi -Pantheon ( no visita all'interno) -Piazza Colonna -Fontana di Trevi -Piazza di Spagna Incluso nel tour : Guida autorizzata Auricolari Servizio di transfer da alberghi centrali al punto d'incontro del tour se prenotato ( no riaccompagno in albergo ) Non incluso nel tour: Riaccompagno in albergo con transfer a fine tour Punto d'incontro Largo Argentina di fronte al Teatro Argentina per le 09:15 o transfer da alberghi centrali.

data.name: Isola Bella with Blue Grotto Included!
data.description: Enjoy a legendary event: Capri's unique combination of Nature’s beauty and hedonism has charmed Roman emperors in the past and Hollywood stars and VIPs in the present. It’s the perfect microcosm of Mediterranean appeal: breathtaking views, blue skies mixing up with the sea and the Caprese sweet summers are the perfect scenarios to live the island with its typical piazzas and alley and its relaxed and elegant atmosphere. Already inhabited in the Palaeolithic period, Capri was briefly occupied by the Greeks before Emperor Augustus made it his private playground and Tiberius retired here in AD 27. Its modern incarnation as a tourist centre dates from the early 20th century. It’s also a hugely popular day-trip destination and a summer favourite of holidaying VIPs: with this tour, you will have the chance to spend a night on this amazing Island with more time to explore beyond the surface. You’ll find that Capri retains an unspoiled charm with grand villas, overgrown vegetable plots, sun-bleached, peeling stucco and banks of brilliantly coloured bougainvillea. All of this overlooks the deep blue water that laps into secluded coves and mysterious grottoes. Day 1 | Rome > Capri * Departure from Rome. If your hotel is located in central Rome you will be picked up starting from 6:00 a.m.; * 06:45 a.m. - If your accommodation is not on our pick up list, reach us at Viale Luigi Einaudi in front of S. Maria degli Angeli e dei Martiri; * 7:00 a.m. - Departure for Naples by motorcoach (one piece of luggage per person is allowed); * Arrival at Naples Port and boarding the ferry to Capri Island; * Arrived in Capri we make our way directly to the Blue Grotto; * From the small seaport of Marina Grande we will continue onboard a minibus reaching Anacapri; * Explore Capri at your own pace; * Check-in at the Hotel and overnight stay; Day 2 | Capri Island * Breakfast at the hotel and spend the day exploring Capri at your leisure Day 3 | Capri > Rome *Breakfast at your hotel and free time. Departure back to Rome in the afternoon. Estimated arrival in the late evening, depending on the traffic. The Tour ends at the hotel or nearby

data.name: Private Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
data.description: Immerse yourself in the grandeur of ancient Rome with our exclusive guided tour, retracing the footsteps of emperors and gladiators alike. Delve deep into history as you explore the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill, each revealing layers of the city's storied past. Begin your journey at the iconic Colosseum, an architectural marvel that once hosted epic gladiatorial battles. Step inside this ancient amphitheatre, and with the guidance of our passionate experts, breathe life into its bloody past, imagining the roars of the crowd and the clash of steel. As you emerge from the Colosseum, marvel at the majestic Arch of Constantine, a testament to Rome's enduring legacy. Continue your exploration through the Roman Forum, an open-air museum preserving the ruins of temples, basilicas, and government buildings from antiquity. Stand amidst the remnants of ancient civilization, contemplating the lives of those who walked these hallowed grounds millennia ago. Your journey culminates atop the Palatine Hill, the legendary birthplace of Rome. Here, Romulus and Remus, the city's mythical founders, were said to have been nursed by a she-wolf, shaping the destiny of an empire. As you gaze upon the sweeping vistas of the Eternal City, reflect on its timeless allure and enduring significance. Embark on this unforgettable journey through Rome's illustrious past, where every step brings you closer to the essence of the Eternal City. Join us and experience history come to life in the heart of Italy's capital

data.description: Rome can be daunting to explore on foot or by public transportation but on this golf cart tour, take in all the top sights without breaking a sweat. data.name: Rome: Private Pasta-Making Class
data.description: Immerse yourself in a private pasta-making class at a local host's home, learn the secrets of the region's most famous pasta dishes and taste the fruit of your labour over lunch or dinner accompanied by local wine. During the lesson, the host will reveal the tricks of the trade of 3 authentic regional pasta recipes. Have fun putting your cooking skills to the test. Participants will have a workstation equipped with utensils and all the ingredients to make the dishes. Then, taste everything you have prepared over a meal accompanied by a selection of red and white local wines. Behind every Pasta shape there is an ancient tradition and a personal story. Your host will welcome you like part of the family as they teach you their family cooking secrets for an authentic culinary experience. In Italy, cooking comes from the heart, and nothing compares to real Italian pasta prepared in the comfort of a local home. Feel the love for genuine produce from Rome and enjoy great conversation with a welcoming new friend. When you cook the recipes you’ve learned back at home, you’ll remember your time in Rome with a smile. Cesarine is Italy’s oldest network of more than 1000 home cooks all over the country in more than 500 cities. They are passionate and welcoming hosts that open the doors of their own homes to curious travellers for immersive culinary experiences.

data.name: Colosseum and Vatican Small-Group Tour Over 2 Days
data.description: Hit two of Rome’s signature sights over two days on this intimate tour in a group no larger than 10. Spend the first morning discovering the heart of ancient Rome: the Colosseum where gladiators fought, the Roman Forum, where business was done, and Palatine Hill, where the city was founded. The next afternoon, continue to the Vatican Museums, including the Sistine Chapel and Raphael’s Rooms, famed for their dazzling frescoes.

data.name: Rome: Spritz & Pasta Making Class
data.shortDescription: Make Italian homemade pasta and discover the secrets of the world's best cuisine
data.description:
Refine your culinary skills in Rome, with a cooking class of two classic Italian dishes, and learn to make authentic Fettuccine and Maltagliati that any Italian nonna would be proud of!

Begin the workshop by mingling with the other participants of the class and making the perfect spritz cocktail. Then, you'll start to work on your own dough. 

The chef will show you the various type of cut you could make with this recipe: tagliolini, pappardelle, fettuccine, and maltagliati or “badly cut.” You will cut your own fettuccine and maltagliati and choose the sauce for your pasta, such as amatriciana, cacio e pepe, tomato and basil, etc.

After that, you will sit and you will enjoy an appetizer of bruschetta with tomatoes and basil, sipping a good glass of wine. 

Then, you will taste your creation for lunch or dinner and conclude your meal with a glass of limoncello. 

When in Rome...

data.shortDescription: Tour the city on a compact e-bike and visit the Circus Maximus
data.description:
You don't need a Vespa to whiz around Rome anymore. With three hours of rental time on a Hi Bike, you'll be able to cycle from one Roman monument to the next in no time. After you've enjoyed the sights of the city, and a scoop or two of gelato, you can use your ticket for a virtual experience at the Circus Maximus.

Don a VR headset and watch as the home of chariot racing turns from ruins to reality. Using historic research, you can get a sense of the area as it was during Rome's prime.

data.name: Rome: Private Day Trip to Roman Castles Region with Driver
data.description: Escape the bustle of the city with this full-day private tour from Rome to the scenic Roman Castles region. Travel in comfort with your personal English-speaking driver and explore charming towns like Frascati, Ariccia, Nemi, and Castel Gandolfo. Enjoy leisurely walks, volcanic lakes, and the option to savor local wines, traditional foods, and even visit a former Papal residence. Hotel pick-up and drop-off make your experience even more relaxing.

data.name: Share your pasta love in local's home in Rome
data.description: Experience the essence of Italian hospitality and cuisine with this immersive pasta-making class in Rome. Perfect for travelers and food lovers alike, this 1.5-hour cooking experience offers a hands-on opportunity to create, taste, and celebrate traditional homemade pasta. Your journey begins with a warm welcome from your local host, who will introduce you to the art of Italian cooking over a small appetizer and aperitif. Then, it's time to roll up your sleeves and dive into the magic of fresh pasta-making! You’ll learn step-by-step techniques to mix, knead, and shape classic Italian pasta—whether it’s tagliatelle, fettuccine, or ravioli. Once your pasta is ready, the celebration begins! Gather around the table, toast with a bottle of wine (one per three guests), and indulge in the delicious dish you've just created. If you’d like, you can end your meal in true Italian style with an optional homemade dessert or an authentic espresso. This Rome-based pasta-making experience isn’t just a cooking class—it’s a cultural journey, a chance to share laughter, connect with fellow travelers, and take home unforgettable memories and skills.

data.name: Rome Hop-On Hop-Off Sightseeing Tour
data.description: Let the sights of Rome unfold before you on an open-top, double-decker, hop-on hop-off bus. Climb aboard to admire top Rome attractions including the Vatican City, Colosseum and Trevi Fountain on this comprehensive tour. Enjoy 360-degree views from the open deck and hop on and off as you wish at any of the eight stops. Choose1 Loop., 1 Day, 24, 48 or 72 hours of sightseeing, and if you opt for a 48-hour ticket, upgrade to include entrance to Rome’s showpieces such as Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and Colosseum.Download now Sightseeing Experience APP: an easy and practical way to orient yourself, move, visit and discover the city. Inside the APP you find a free walking tour of the center available in 5 languages and an interactive map that shows you the position of the buses in real time, the waiting time at each stop and your position so you can easily reach the nearest stop.

data.name: Crypts and Catacombs of Rome Skip-The-Line Tour
data.description: Embark on an unforgettable journey through ancient Rome's underground wonders, exploring crypts, catacombs, and burial chambers with an expert guide. The Original Crypts and Catacombs of Rome Tour begins in Piazza Barberini, where human corpses were once publicly displayed. The tour's highlight is the Capuchin Crypt, featuring Caravaggio's "St. Francis in Meditation" and the artistic arrangement of 4,000 Capuchin monks' bones.Next, travel comfortably to the Christian Catacombs, a network associated with the first Christians in ancient Rome. Descend into volcanic rock corridors, discovering frescoes and burial places doubling as places of worship during persecution. Led by an expert guide, navigate extensive catacombs revealing tales of a bygone era.Complete your underground experience with a historic visit to the Basilica San Martino ai Monti, a church rich with hidden layers of history. Built on the remains of ancient Roman buildings, it offers a rare look at the early days of Christian worship. Step beneath the basilica to explore age-old chambers once used by early Christian communities and uncover relics and remains that reflect the deep spiritual roots of the Eternal City.No matter which venue becomes your favorite, the seamless combination of these three distinct elements offers an unforgettable exploration of Rome's hidden treasures.This is a unique tour of Rome which will give you a different perspective on the fascinating culture of the Eternal City.

data.name: Rome Small-Group Jewish Ghetto Walking Tour
data.description: Delve into the rich history and culture of Rome’s Jewish community on this small-group walking tour through the Jewish Ghetto. From Trajan's Column to the Great Synagogue, uncover the vibrant culture and thriving community that flourished despite adversity. Wander charming streets, admire architectural wonders, and see a different side of Roman history.

data.name: Tour of Rome Colosseum, Forums & Palatine Hill with Local Guide
data.description:
In the company of a local, expert guide this tour takes you to explore some of Ancient Rome’s most famous sights.

The Arch of Constantine, the Senate House, the Temple of Julius Caesar, the Triumphal Arches, the House of the Vestal Virgins, the Basilicas, the Golden Mile, the Temples of Saturn and Concord and the interior of the Colosseum. You will forego visiting the Colosseum 3rd tier and underground so you can spend more time exploring other more interesting areas of the amphitheater and Roman Forum.

data.name: Rome Pantheon Guided Tour
data.description: Explore the Pantheon in depth, and discover its secrets, with this guided tour of the ancient wonder. Unravel hidden secrets as your guides lead you through centuries of history. Hear echoes of the past, admire the architecture, and touch marble steeped in history. Your seasoned guides offer unique insights and details, turning your visit into an enlightening journey.

data.name: Rome Pantheon: Fast Track Ticket + Small Group Guided Tour
data.description:
Embark on a 40-minutes fascinating journey back in time with your guide at the harmonious Roman temple dedicated to all the gods. Discover the engineering secrets of this architectural jewel and see why the Pantheon is the only ancient Roman building to remain nearly intact after almost 2,000 years!

Walk through the Corinthian columns quarried all the way from Egypt and marvel at the original marble floors of the temple. Be charmed by the beautiful proportions of the building, as Michelangelo did, and discover the pagan rationale behind them.

Learn about its transformation during the centuries and its present use as a Christian church. See the resting place of Christian martyrs, Italian royals, and world-famous artists.

data.name: Rome: Small-Group Light Painting Circus Maximus Photoshoot
data.description: Capture your Rome vacation in a way most tourists won’t—with a small-group light painting illusion photoshoot in front of the Circus Maximus. A professional photographer is here to help capture you at your best angles in the city, utilizing eye-catching lights to make the pictures in front of this major Roman attraction truly stand out.

data.name: Capitoline Museums Admission with Percy Jackson, Olympian Gods
data.description: Come face to face with the characters from the Percy Jackson novels on this educational and entertaining walking tour. Visit the Capitoline Museums to learn about ancient Olympian gods, goddesses, and mystical creatures. The museums’ collections feature masterpieces like the bust of the poet Homer, the Capitoline Wolf, and Boy With Thorn. Your guide uses scavenger hunts, quizzes, games, and multimedia tools to encourage discussion and conversation about the the mythical creatures in the Jackson novels.

data.name: Trevi Fountain Rome: Underground Domus Guided Tour + City Walking Tour
data.description:
Explore the lively Piazza Navona, a bustling square in Rome, home to stunning fountains like Bernini's Fountain of the 4 Rivers.

Visit the Pantheon, an ancient temple dedicated to multiple deities, remarkably preserved through time and the stop by the Trevi Fountain to toss in a coin and make a wish.

Join a guided tour to uncover Rome's hidden treasures and delve into its rich history, from ancient times to the present by exploring the underground passages of the Trevi District during a 45-minute guided tour, learning why it's known as the "City of Water."

data.name: Colosseum, Vatican Museums, and Sistine Chapel Package
data.description: The Colosseum, Vatican Museums, and Sistine Chapel are Rome’s hottest tickets. Ensure admission to all three—plus the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, both included with your Colosseum entry—when you prebook this convenient package, online, in advance, in the currency of your choice. Instead of a guide, your experience starts by watching an informative video on ancient Rome when you collect your tickets.

data.name: Rome Secrets Small-Group Walking Tour
data.description: Discover Rome’s secrets on a small-group tour, starting from Piazza Venezia and ending in the charming streets of Trastevere. Visit historic sites such as Teatro di Marcello and the Jewish Ghetto and wander Trastevere’s vibrant cobblestone alleys. A licensed local guide shares fascinating stories throughout, offering an authentic glimpse into the rich history and magic of the Eternal City.

data.name: Rome: Pasta and Tiramisu Workshop
data.shortDescription: Learn to make authentic Italian dishes with a cooking workshop in Rome
data.description:
Upgrade your culinary repetoire in Rome, with a cooking class of two Italian classics, and learn to make authentic tiramisu and pasta that any Italian nonna would be proud of!

To start, you'll learn make tiramisu from scratch. Along with gelato and panna cotta, tiramisu is perhaps Italy's most famous dessert. Made with simple ingredients, like savoiardi (ladyfingers), mascarpone cheese and egg yolks, it's one of the world's favorite desserts for a very good reason – it's delizioso! 

Then, learn to make your own pasta from flour and eggs. The chef will show you which kind of pasta you can prepare with this recipe, from tiny tagliolini to large pappardelle, you'll get to practice cutting out each. Then all you need to do is choose your topping sauce (tomato and basil, amatriciana, or cacio e pepe).

After the cooking class ends, sit down with your fellow classmates and savor your creations with a glass of wine – an essential part of Italian cooking!

data.name: Guided Tour of St. Peter's Basilica With Dome Climb
data.description: Scale to the top of the Vatican with this guided tour of St. Peter's Basilica with included dome climb. Led by a tour guide, enjoy an introduction to Vatican history before heading into the Basilica itself. Learn the stories and the significance behind the Basilica’s priceless art collection before ascending to the top of its Dome. Perfect for travellers who are particularly interested in the history of the Basilica and may have visited the Vatican before.

data.name: Papal Audience
data.description: The tour Attending the Papal Audience is an amazing once-in-a-lifetime experience and an opportunity to see the Pope himself. Every Wednesday morning the Holy Father holds a public Audience on St. Peter's Square. He will be passing by the faithful on his Pope mobile, on his way to the podium in front of St. Peter's Basilica, from where will be delivering his message and finally give the Papal Blessing. Although Papal Audience tickets are free, organizing your own can be a difficult process. We eliminate the hassle by reserving, picking up and bringing the invitation to the meeting point. Then we guide you through the crowds, getting to the area available for us. data.description:
With this ticket, you can skip the line at the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel. You can also benefit from the guidance of an expert to unlock the world's most distinguished art collections.

data.name: Appian Way And Catacombs Golf Cart Tour: Small Group Rome
data.description: Experience the charm of ancient Christian Rome on a small-group golf cart tour. Travel along the iconic Ancient Appian Way while taking in views of the towering city walls, imperial gates, and the Pyramid of Cestius. The highlight? A guided exploration of the Christian catacombs, where frescoed tunnels unveil stories of early Christianity.

data.name: Ostia Antica
data.description: Discover the fascinating archeological site of Ostia Antica. Ostia is a derivation of the Latin word os, meaning mouth: Ostia was Rome's seaport and today a district of the metropolitan city of Rome. The site is known for the excellent preservation of its ancient buildings, enriched with magnificent frescoes and mosaics. Take the opportunity to admire buildings from the 3rd century BC. Excavations of Ancient Ostia started at the beginning of the 19th century and projected a light on the everyday life in this corner of the Empire. You will have the chance to see fascinating remains of old streets, apartment blocks and statues and even get inside Ostia Antica amphitheater.

data.name: Rome Papal Audience, Vatican Museum, and Sistine Chapel Tour
data.description: Visit the Vatican Museum and the Sistine Chapel, attend the papal audience, and witness the Pope deliver the Apostolic Blessing during a group tour. Afterward, skip the lines and explore the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel at your own pace with a professional audio guide. Highlights include Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel frescoes, Raphael’s tapestries, and the ancient Laocoön sculpture—an essential experience for those interested in faith, history, and art.

data.name: UNESCO Jewels: Tivoli and Its Villas
data.description: Visit Tivoli, an ancient resort area famed for its beauty and its good water, enriched by many Roman villas, the most famous one, of which the ruins remain, is Villa Adriana. Take a comfortable transport to the little town of Tivoli, located a few kilometers from Rome, in a splendid natural environment between the Eternal City and the high hills to the east of Rome. Since ancient times this little town has been blessed by a great climate and always had a key importance due to its location. The most remarkable architectural complex is Villa Adriana, dating from the Ancient Roman time, created in the 2nd century AD by the Emperor Hadrian. It combines different architectural styles from Egypt, Rome and Athens, in the shape of an "ideal city". For this reason a visit to the Villa cannot be missed: it is a masterpiece that uniquely brings together the highest symbols of cultures of the world in ancient times. The Villa covers more than 120 hectares and was the House of the Emperors for more than 50 years. After this amazing visit, come to discover the Renaissance-style Villa d’Este, a gorgeous palatial setting surrounded by a spectacular terraced garden. Enjoy the beauty of its cascades, water tanks, and fountains. Villa d'Este is a masterpiece of the Italian Gardens, decorated with a massive and impressive number of fountain nymphs, grottos and marvelous courtyards inspired by the gardens of Babylon, one of the wonders of ancient world. Strongly desired by the Cardinal Ippolito II d'Este, the Villa was enlarged and enriched by all his descendants with the contribution of incredible artists of the times, like Gianlorenzo Bernini. Return to Rome in the afternoon.

data.name: Rome Borghese Gallery Skip-the-Line Small-Group Guided Tour
data.description: Housed in the Borghese opulent family’s former villa, the Borghese Gallery is one of the world’s most prestigious art collections. Witness works of art by Caravaggio, Raphael, Titian, and many more on this small-group guided tour that includes skip-the-line access to the gallery, so you can avoid the long queues and start exploring as soon as you arrive.

data.description: About 25 miles (40 kilometers) from Rome, the Valmontone Outlet offers incredible value on brands like Levi’s, Benetton, and Tommy Hilfiger, but it’s fiddly to reach on public transit. Skip the drama of driving in Roman traffic and relax with this small-group tour that includes pickup from central Rome addresses. You’ll have a full day to enjoy the village’s 170-odd outlets as well as its range of food options.

data.name: Borghese Gallery: Reserved Entrance + Digital Audio Guide
data.description:

See classical sculptures, such as the gladiator mosaic, and a fresco by Mariano Rossi.

Look at Gian Lorenzo Bernini's sculptures, including Apollo and Daphne, and David. Learn about the portrait busts of Pope Paul V and Cardinal Scipione Borghese.

data.name: Rome: Vatican, Sistine Chapel, and St. Peter’s Private Tour
data.description: Enjoy the perks of a more personalized sightseeing experience—and save up to hours of waiting time—when you book this comprehensive, private Vatican tour. Pick between morning and afternoon start times, and head directly into the Vatican Museums with skip-the-line tickets. With your guide, cover the highlights and key treasures before marveling at Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel frescoes. Finally, end the tour with a guided stroll through St. Peter’s Basilica.

data.name: Rome Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel Guided Tour
data.description: The Vatican is home to a wealth of art and historical treasures, not to mention its rich architectural heritage. This guided tour takes visitors through its museum complex and Sistine Chapel in just a few hours, highlighting stories behind its collections and the landmark itself. data.name: Golf Cart Around Imperial Rome
data.description: Give your feet a rest on Rome’s cobbled streets, and explore the city’s historical sites by golf cart, instead. On this 3-hour tour, you’ll see some of Rome’s top attractions and squares, including the Pantheon, Colosseum, Piazza Navona, Piazza Venezia, Circus Maximus, the Spanish Steps and Trevi Fountain. You can get closer to the landmarks than you would in a regular vehicle but still enjoy comfortable transport around the city.

data.name: Hard Rock Cafe Rome
data.shortDescription: Skip-the-line access to Hard Rock Cafe Rome, plus a burger and a soft drink
data.description:
It's hungry work touring the sites of ancient Rome. Take your gladiator's appetite for a spot of people-watching at the Hard Rock Cafe Rome, where the food is good and the windows are open wide on the Roman world.

While you're surrounded by rock 'n roll memorabilia, bite into the Original Legendary® Burger – a taste of America that comes with a Black Angus steak burger, smoked bacon, cheddar cheese, leaf lettuce, vine-ripened tomato, and a crispy onion ring. A cold, refreshing soft drink is included too!

data.name: Tuscan Countryside: Day Trip from Rome with Lunch
data.shortDescription: Enjoy a relaxing guided tour of Tuscany from Rome, with lunch and wine!
data.description:
Take a break from the eternal bustle of Rome and escape to the country, on a guided tour of beautiful Tuscany. Take in the postcard-perfect rolling hills and world-famous scenery of this stunning region, while an expert, English-speaking guide provides insightful commentary to color in the historical and cultural details.

Stop for delicious lunch and wine at a Tuscan winery, explore the medieval town of Montepulciano, peek inside the St. Biagio Church, and savor the stunning pastoral views before you're whisked back to Rome.

data.name: Galleria Spada: Entry Ticket
data.description: Want to see a real home in Rome? Experience the atmosphere of a private Baroque residence as you browse impressive 16th and 17th-century works by Caravaggio, Titian and more. The forced perspective gallery by Francesco Borromini is rightfully renowned. And there's even a secret garden!

data.name: Ostia Antica: Guided Tour from Rome + Lunch
data.shortDescription: Wander through ancient ruins and explore historic temples
data.description: Tour the ancient ruins of Ostia Antica on a 5-hour tour from Rome. Walk through well-preserved streets, see old temples, and visit historical theaters. After exploring, eat lunch at a local trattoria with traditional Roman dishes. Lastly, learn about the city's past from knowledgeable guides and discover this historical site.

data.name: Rome's Experience Pass with Entrance to Top Attractions
data.description: The Vatican and Rome Experience Pass is your ultimate key to exploring the Eternal City. Choose from 3, 5, or 7 selections to create a personalized pass that grants access to iconic sites such as the Colosseum, Vatican Museums, and the Sistine Chapel, with priority admission included. With expert curation and exclusive options like walking tours and visits outside Rome, this pass ensures a seamless and unforgettable Roman adventure.

data.name: Capri Island with Blue Grotto: Day trip from Rome
data.description: Tour duration: full day. Leaving Rome by coach or mini-van, you’ll travel south, passing through Roman countryside and the Castelli Romani. In Naples, you’ll see the Mediterranean, Mount Vesuvius, and countless historic sites. After a 1-hour ferry trip, you’ll be on the island of Capri. Discover the charming beauty of the island with our enthusiastic tour guide. Explore the island’s famous alleys and the Piazzetta. You’ll visit the Blue Grotto, named for the blue reflection caused by sunlight shining into the sea cave. After an afternoon touring Capri, you’ll return to Rome via Naples, arriving back in the evening

data.name: Passetto di Borgo: Skip The Line Ticket
data.shortDescription: Walk through the escape route for popes during times of danger
data.description:
Visit the Passetto di Borgo, a historic path linking Vatican City to Castel Sant'Angelo. This passage, used for centuries, served as an escape route for popes, including during the Sack of Rome in 1527.

Walk through the Passetto di Borgo, a silent witness to significant historical events, and learn about its role in stories of power and intrigue. Fans of Dan Brown's _Angels & Demons_ will recognize the Passetto from the novel. 

Explore the passage and learn about its impact on Vatican City and Rome’s history.

data.name: Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel: Skip-The-Line Guided Tour (Spanish Language)
data.shortDescription:
Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: Saints Tour has prepared for you a unique and unforgettable experience. The present tour includes:

  • privileged entrance to the Vatican Museums
  • guided tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel

You will have at your complete disposal one of our specialized and accredited by the Vatican guides. The route of this guided tour has been designed to let you discover – in approximately two and a half hours, with the assistance of a skilled tour guide trained in art history – unique masterpieces without wasting time in long queues.


TICKET INFO

Free: from 0-5 years old;
Reduced: 6 to 18 years old;
Students (reduced): from 19-25 years old. This offer is valid only upon presentation of a valid student card, to be shown at the time of entry and/or check-in.

 

Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: what awaits you


With this guided tour, you will be able to admire some of the most famous works of art renown all over the world: we are offering a journey into time and space, into history and culture, but, most of all, a fast-starting journey, where no exhausting waits in queue are involved.

Our groups are made up by a maximum of 30 people and are all accompanied by certified Vatican tour guides, who will take you through the priceless artistic treasures enshrined in the seven different museums that make up the very heart of the Vatican Museum complex.
In a relaxed and informal atmosphere, your guide will tell you stories and curiosities that will help
you to understand the historical, artistic and cultural context that has molded the masterpieces hosted in the Hall of the Muses, in the Pio-Clementine Museum, in the Gallery of Maps, in the Gallery of Tapestries, in the Raphael Rooms and in the magnificent Courtyard of the Pinecone that opens in the heart of Vatican City.

The tour of the Vatican Museums will culminate with the visit to the Sistine Chapel; since it is forbidden to speak aloud inside, your guide will deliver explanations and directions outside, using the special panels provided by the Museums. Once inside, you can admire the paintings that truly represent the highest peak of Italian Renaissance art, from the precious frescoes by Botticelli, Perugino, Pinturicchio, Ghirlandaio, Luca Signorelli and Piero di Cosimo, to the extraordinary vault cycle and the Last Judgement by Michelangelo.

At the end of this incredible experience, your guide will briefly tell you about the history of the Vatican and the majestic St Peter’s Basilica.

SOME CURIOSITIES

  • The Vatican Museums were established by Pope Julius II in 1506 from a single statue, the marble group of Laocoon.
  • The Gallery of Maps, 120 meters long, ideally reproduces the line of the Apennines: on the left, there are the regions facing the Tyrrhenian Sea, and on the right those facing the Adriatic Sea.
  • In the Stanza della Segnatura, the philosophers who crowd the School of Athens painted by Raphael, have the features of his fellow painters: Bramante is the mathematician Euclid, Plato displays Leonardo’s hieratic face, Heraclitus borrows the frowning expression of Michelangelo, whose shady character was universally known. In the foreground, Buonarroti’s infamous boots, which he did not take off even to go to bed.
  • A self-portrait of Michelangelo can be found in the Sistine Chapel  more precisely, in the Last Judgment: Buonarroti reproduced his features in the skin that St. Bartholomew holds in his hands.
  • All the conclaves that precede the papal elections, take place today in the Sistine Chapel.

data.name: The Hidden Rome running tour
data.shortDescription:
This is a new experience!

Starting from Piazza Navona we will visit the most hidden places and alleys of Rome. One of the unique experiences that can be done by immersing among small streets with curious names and that smell of antiquity.

We will have the feeling of getting lost, but with amazement we will find ourselves in a new places, never seen before, but which will have something intimate and familiar.

We will know the widest alley, the smallest one in Rome called Vicolo di San Trifone, which connects via dei Coronari with via dei Tre Archi, the one with the most original name, the steepest alley, alleys with curious names, alleys that took their name from “archaeological” discoveries.

We will go to the discovery of all this and we will know its history, anecdotes and the most hidden secrets, in full ArcheoRunning style!

data.name: Appian way running tour
data.shortDescription:
The Appian way is one of the oldest Roman Consular Roads, also known as Regina Viarum.

With this running tour you can take a step back about 2000 years, experience the sensation of running on the ancient Roman paving, with which all Roman roads were built.

You can experience a unique emotion admiring the Villa of Maxentius, the Mausoleum of Cecilia Metella and all the ruins of the funerary monuments that were located on the sides of this ancient road.

We will discover all this, learning about its history, anecdotes and most hidden secrets, in full ArcheoRunning style!

What sets it apart is the seamless combination of street food exploration and insider access to one of Rome’s most iconic kitchens: Roscioli, a place revered by locals and food legends like Anthony Bourdain.

You'll not only taste Rome—you’ll live it:

Bite into the city’s soul with arrosticini and fresh street food in lively Campo de’ Fiori.

Create pasta by hand under the guidance of expert chefs, not just watching but becoming part of the Roscioli culinary tradition.

Savor curated wine pairings as you cook and dine, turning a class into a full sensory experience.

Hear stories and secrets of Roman food culture from locals who live it every day.

Finish with gelato, the classic sweet punctuation to a day immersed in flavor and tradition.

It’s not just a food tour—it’s a deep, delicious dive into Rome’s culinary heartbeat.

data.name: Privileged Entrance Vatican Tour with Sistine Chapel & St. Peter's Basilica
data.description: Most visitors miss the Vatican’s best shortcut. With our expert guide, you’ll explore the Vatican Museums, including the Raphael Rooms and Sistine Chapel, then descend the Scala Regia (Bernini’s regal staircase) into St. Peter’s Basilica through an entrance reserved only for guided groups. This is the Vatican experience you didn’t know you needed.Tour OverviewMeet your local guide just outside Caffé Vaticano, right across from the entrance to the Vatican Museums. With skip-the-line access, you'll breeze past the crowds and head straight through security, even in the busy afternoon. From the Gallery of Maps to Nero’s Bathtub and the Sistine Chapel, you’ll hit all the must-sees. Then follow your guide down the Scala Regia for a grand finale inside St. Peter’s Basilica.Privileged Entrance Vatican Tour with Sistine Chapel & St. Peter's Basilica DescriptionYour 3-hour small group tour includes:Passionate, English-speaking guidePio ClementinoSkip-the-line Vatican MuseumsVatican gallery highlightsSistine ChapelRaphael Rooms & Borgia ApartmentsEnter Scala Regia (passageway to St. Peter's)St. Peter's BasilicaMax group size of 20Morning/Afternoon entryPlease note that the Basilica is closed on Wednesday mornings due to the Papal Audience and will not be included in tours. Afternoon tours will still include St. Peter's Basilica entry.Pio-Clementino Museum and Nero's BathAt the start of your tour, you'll follow your guide to the Bramante Courtyard, designed by Donato Bramante. This part of the Vatican Museums is home to the Apollo Belvedere, Laocoön and His Sons, and the Belvedere Torso. Learn about the myths and legends associated with these iconic sculptures before visiting the oldest and largest bathtub in existence. Nero's bathtub is an incredible 25 feet long and is made from a rare red marble that isn't even available nowadays!Popular Vatican GalleriesYour guide will lead you on through the Vatican Museums, visiting the Candelabra Gallery, Gallery of the Tapestries, and Gallery of Maps. Admire the ancient Roman and Greek statues, the Flemish tapestries created by Raphael's students, and the gorgeous topographical depictions of Italy.At the height of the Roman Empire, pontiffs rarely left Rome. In order to understand the Italian peninsula without endangering his life, Pope Gregory XIII commissioned 40 giant meticulous maps to be created for his use. Most of these maps measure more than 15 by 16 feet, and the end result is nothing short of spectacular.You'll hear the stories behind these treasures from your expert guide as the Vatican secrets are slowly unveiled to you.Raphael Rooms and The School of AthensRaphael, one of the traditional trinity of great masters, reigned during the Renaissance. After the turbulent Middle Ages, European civilization rebounded and experienced a prolific period in which the arts, literature, and thought flourished. As a true Renaissance man, Raphael embraced the ideals of the period and painted the walls of the Vatican Museums with his masterpieces. Among these, you can view his most famous work, The School of Athens, which is a testament to his vision and creativity.Borgia ApartmentsDownstairs from the Raphael Rooms and once occupied by Borgia Pope Alexander VI, these private chambers were frescoed by early Renaissance artist Pinturicchio. As a co-pupil of Raphael’s under master Perugino, Pinturicchio had a penchant for embedding fake jewels and other three-dimensional objects like metal saddle studs in his frescoes. The Borgia Apartments also contain another hidden gem: the first European depiction of Native Americans.Michelangelo’s Sistine ChapelNo trip to Vatican City is complete without stepping inside the Sistine Chapel. Only when you’re beneath Michelangelo’s ceiling does the scale of his work truly hit you. With over 600 figures painted by hand, it’s one of the greatest artistic achievements in the world. Because the chapel is still a place of worship, speaking inside is strictly forbidden. Your guide will prep you beforehand with insights and a handout so you can spot the key details on your own.After your silent visit, you’ll follow your guide down the Scala Regia, Bernini’s ceremonial staircase, for direct entry to St. Peter’s Basilica. This is an entrance reserved exclusively for guided tour groups.To enter the Sistine Chapel, both men and women must cover their knees and shoulders, otherwise, the Vatican might refuse entry to religious sites and you’ll miss out on a portion of your tour. We understand the summers in Rome can be hot, so a great alternative is to bring a shawl/scarf/sweater with you. That way you can cover your knees and shoulders when necessary.Ending Inside St. Peter’s BasilicaYour tour concludes inside St. Peter’s Basilica, the heart of Vatican City and one of the most celebrated churches in the world. Marvel at Michelangelo’s Pietà, gaze up at the soaring dome, and stand beneath Bernini’s monumental bronze canopy. While most visitors exit the Museums and wait again to enter the basilica, your group takes the direct route through the Scala Regia with exclusive access reserved only for guided tours. Once inside, you are free to remain as long as you wish before exiting to explore the rest of Rome.

data.name: Vatican Museums & The Sistine Chapel: Private 2.5 hr Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the dazzling treasures of the Vatican Museums, including world-famous antiquities, frescoes by Renaissance maestro Raphael, and of course the magnificence of Michelangelo in the Sistine Chapel on this private 2.5-hour tour. On your private tour you will:  Explore the Vatican Museums in Vatican City – the smallest country in the world, home to the Catholic Church and the Pope himself; See all the major highlights of these extensive museums with fascinating commentary from your guide;  Admire some of the world’s best-known classical sculptures such as the ApolloBelvedere and the Laocoön; Learn all about the Renaissance of Ancient Greece and Rome; Marvel at the skill of the Gallery of Tapestries and the exquisite Gallery of Maps; Learn the fascinating, complex, and sometimes scandalous history of the papacy; Enjoy the masterpieces by Raphael in Pope Julius II’s private apartments and learn all about the life and times of the Warrior Pope;  Hear all about the famous rivalry between Raphael and Michelangelo; Stand beneath the awe-inspiring frescos on the Sistine Chapel walls and admire the Last Judgment by Michelangelo on the whole altar wall; End inside the Vatican Museums to continue at your own leisure or exit with your guide. Vatican City, located in the heart of Rome, is an independent city-state, and the smallest country in the world. It is the heart of the Roman Catholic Church and the traditional home of thePope. The Vatican Museums with its hallowed halls and galleries, lined with world-famous priceless artefacts, antiquities, and art, is also home to works by the two Renaissance maestros and rivals Raphael and Michaelangelo. Your highlights tour of the Vatican Museums will whisk you through the galleries ensuring you see the most renowned pieces. You will see the Belvedere Courtyard with the Appollo Belvedere and Laocoön sculptures, explore the Gallery of Tapestries with designs of the life of Christ by Raphael and the exquisitely frescoed Gallery of the Maps. You'll hear all about the life and papacy of Pope Julius II who commissioned Raphael to paint his private apartments and Michaelangelo to paint the Sistine Ceiling. Your guide will show you the Raphael Rooms with the School of Athens fresco that would set a new standard in the art world, followed finally by the truly awe-inspiring and magnificent Sistine Chapel with those astounding frescoes painted by Michelangelo in his thirties and later his sixties. Admire the Creation of Adam on the Ceiling and the perfection of the human form with the 392 bodies in the Last Judgement. Most of us have seen reproductions of the Sistine Chapel, but nothing beats the real thing! Your guide will give you fascinating in-depth explanations, stories, and analyses of Michelangelo's life and masterpieces. Your tour ends inside the Vatican Museums. Please note:This tour does not visit St. Peter's Basilica. It ends inside the Vatican Museums, allowing you to spend as long as you wish inside to get food and keep exploring at your leisure. During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.description: Delight in an unforgettable night celebrating Giacomo Puccini, a towering figure in the realm of classical music. An Evening of Passion and Music Indulge in the powerful tunes of Puccini at the historic and cozy St. Andrew’s of Scotland. With seating for only 100, this exclusive venue captures the ambiance of 19th-century music salons, allowing audience members to enjoy a near, personal musical experience. Prepare to explore the emotive world of Puccini, featuring some of his most impactful compositions, such as the mighty 'Nessun dorma', the poignant 'Vissi d’arte', and the stirring 'E lucevan le stelle'. A Unique Location in the Heart of Rome Hosted at Via Venti Settembre 7, a stone’s throw from the Quirinale Palace and opposite the Ministry of Defense, the concert ensures a splendid view from every seat in this intimate location. Seize this chance to hear Puccini’s timeless melodies in an enchanting environment where music, history, and sentiment fuse to create an evening you will always remember.

data.name: Villa Borghese: guided ebike tour to discover the green soul of Rome
data.description: You are in the historic center, you feel the chaos of the city overwhelming you with the noise of the traffic and the frenzy of the crowd. All you want is to teleport yourself to an oasis of peace in the middle of nature! Then get on the electric bike and come with us!! A guided tour of Villa Borghese is exactly what you need! This magical area which extends for 80 hectares is a paradise with a historical, artistic and naturalistic heritage of inestimable beauty. Cycle through tree-lined avenues, breathe in the fresh air and admire the beauty of lush gardens. Discover the Temple of Asclepius, an ancient testimony to Roman history, and enjoy a breathtaking view from the Terrazza del Pincio. Marvel at the Water Clock, an engineering marvel that will transport you to the past.Villa Borghese is much more than a simple park, it is a sanctuary for the soul where nature, history and art blend in perfect harmony. It is the perfect and safe place to unplug from the pulsating rhythm of the city! Are you ready to live an unforgettable experience? Your guide will take you to discover this corner of Paradise in the heart of Rome, involving you with stories and curiosities.Do you want an even more authentic and personalized experience? Book the “Private Tour” option. You will have the local guide exclusively for you!

data.name: Guided tour to the Bernini Ecstasi of Saint Teresa
data.description: Are you ready for a mind-blowing location? This little church hidden in a very busy place in the city was also used in the very famous film Angels and Demons, and hides works of art and countless secrets. The most famous work of art is the Ecstasy of Saint Teresa which will be the subject of our tour. You will be able to get very close to sculpture and discover its secrets. But don't worry, you won't just see the sculpture but I'll take you on a journey into an unknown world!

data.name: Villa Borghese Gallery and Gardens skip-the-line guided tour
data.description: Visit one of the richest and most interesting Villas in Rome. The Borghese Gallery is well known for its vast collection of great Italian masterpieces of artists such as Bernini, Canova, Caravaggio and Titian. Here you'll find sculptures, paintings and pieces that will make this one of the most interesting and varied art experiences of your life.The Villa was once home to Cardinal Scipione Borghese and many of the works of art inside the villa were commissioned by the Cardinal himself, known for being a passionate patron. Wander the luxurious rooms of Cardinal Borghese's Villa and admire the groundbreaking masterpieces in their original settings just as the artists intended them to be seen.With a special gift of recognizing beauty, the Cardinal collected an impressive number of masterpieces, from some of Caravaggio's early works to Gian Lorenzo Bernini's "Apollo and Daphne", Canova's portrait of "Pauline Bonaparte" and Raphael's "Deposition". Your expert and professional guide will accompany you through the collection, allowing you to get the most out of your visit and fully appreciate the peaceful atmosphere that reigns over this incredible gallery.During the second half of the tour, you will pass through the gardens of Villa Borghese, admiring the carefully cut lawns, fountains, ponds and monuments. Enjoy a walk through the park and escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. The tour ends with a breathtaking view from the top of the Pincio Terrace.

Here the arches of the impressive aqueducts draw elegant profiles in the sky and tell of the cutting-edge engineering feats of the ancient Romans. In the shade of the centuries-old trees enjoy the stories told by your guide, the enchanting landscape will do the rest.Do you want an even more authentic and personalized experience?
