data.name: Small-group Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Tour
data.description: Join a group tour of the Colosseum and let your expert guide amaze you with facts you can’t wait to share with friends at home and memorable tales of the glorious gladiatorial games you’ll never forget.The Colosseum in Rome had over 80 entrances and could accommodate around 50,000 spectators. Learn the history behind this magnificent monument and all that surrounds it. Rome's most popular structure was built for three reasons: as a gift to the Roman citizens from the Flavian Dynasty to increase their popularity, to stage various forms of entertainment, and of course to showcase Roman engineering techniques to the world. Festivals, as well as games, could last up to 100 days in the Colosseum. Your guide will walk you through the Colosseum explaining the true brilliance behind the engineering of this structure and telling you tales of the gladiators that so gallantly entertained hundreds of people.Your tour will then lead you on a journey through the Palatine Hill and Roman Forum where you will be able to admire the incredible ruins and enjoy panoramic views of the Colosseum. The Roman Forum was the social, political, religious and financial center of the Roman Empire and the most incredible site of Ancient Roman civilization with various structures still standing. All layers of Roman society rubbed shoulders together daily, whether, for personal, business or political purposes, anyone from homeless beggars to rich senators could be found there. The Palatine Hill is the foundation point of Rome and still holds today, many layers of history. You can find ruins from the early kingdom of Rome, the Roman Republic in the later centuries and the jaw-dropping palace of Emperor Domitian from the Imperial Age. Further, will also see evidence of the more recent presence of the Farnese family during the Renaissance and that of Mussolini in the 20th century.

data.name: Santa Maria Maggiore Basilica with Dome and Underground guided tour
data.description: The Papal Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, a majestic Marian temple and beacon of artistic civilisation, has been a commanding presence in Rome for over sixteen centuries. Perched atop the Esquiline Hill, it is one of the city's four Papal Basilicas. Legend tells that its construction on the Esquiline was inspired and directed by the Virgin herself. This Basilica is a treasure trove where art and spirituality merge seamlessly, offering visitors an unparalleled experience.You will have the opportunity to admire numerous masterpieces such as the Bernini family tomb, the Baptistery, and the Holy Door. The Basilica also holds intriguing facts about various pontiffs. For instance, Pope Francis often visited the Salus Populi Romani before and after his apostolic journeys, seeking its protection. Your guided tour will reveal the astonishing treasures hidden within this Basilica. A visit to the archaeological area uncovers the fascinating subterranean world of the West's most significant Marian shrine. This complex comprises rooms centred around a vast hall from the Imperial period.As you journey through, you'll encounter a thermal bath adorned with mosaics and heating cavities, ancient roof tiles, decorative frescoes featuring geometric patterns, and a rare agricultural calendar fresco.

data.description: Explore the streets and fountains of Rome in a walking tour of 2 hours, combining art and architecture, legends and ice cream! data.name: I Virtuosi dell'opera di Roma: La Traviata in San Paolo Entro le Mura
data.description: Enjoy Verdi's La Traviata! The libretto by Francesco Maria Piave is based on the novel and play 'La Dame aux Camelias' by Alexandre Dumas' son. The much loved opera in three acts was first performed 6th March 1853 at the Teatro La Fenice, Venice. After the highly successful premiere of Rigoletto at La Fenice in March 1851, Verdi was commissioned to deliver an opera for that house, to be performed in March 1853. He spent some time in Paris during the winter of 1851/52 and there he saw a daring new play by Alexandre Dumas: 'La Dame aux Camelias'. However, Verdi did not decide on this subject right away. The theatre forced Verdi to abandon the contemporary setting and relocate the action back to the year 1700. This rankled Verdi enormously, but he accepted, relieved that the libretto had passed the censor quite quickly and with less trouble than he was used to encountering in Venice. It would almost seem that the hallmark of some of the most successful and well-loved operas is a less than favorable - even disastrous - reception of the premiere. This was the case for 'La Traviata' when it was first performed at La Fenice. It was an unmitigated fiasco. But: Exactly 14 months later on 6th May 1854, again in Venice, at the Teatro San Benedetto it was an overwhelming success.

data.name: The Best of the Vatican and St Peter's Basilica: Private Tour
data.description: On this tour of the home of the Catholic Church, you will have the opportunity to visit the important landmarks with major significance to Catholics. Hear about the tumultuous history of the Church and the colourful popes who reside behind these sturdy walls. On your private tour, you will: Discover the Highlights of the Vatican Museums, including the Pinecone courtyard, The Laocoön, the Room of the Maps, and Raphael Rooms; Marvel at the works of Michelangelo Buonarroti, including the Creation of Man and the Last Judgement in the Sistine Chapel, the ‘Sculpture of the Pieta' in St. Peter's and of course the magnificent Dome of the Basilica; Explore St. Peter's Basilica, the largest church in the world, and see the precious marbles and artworks, including Bernini's famed Baldachin!;   Your tour ends at St Peter's Square, where you can keep exploring at your own leisure.  Vatican City is considered the centre of the Roman Catholic Church and is undoubtedly one of the most historically and culturally rich cities in the world. As the world’s smallest independent state, situated in the centre of Rome, Vatican City is home to the Swiss Guards – tasked with protecting the Pope; St. Peter’s Basilica – the centre of the Catholic world; St. Peter’s Square – a large plaza situated in front of St. Peter’s Basilica; Sistine Chapel – the official residence of the Pope; and Vatican Museums – home to paintings and sculptures collected by the Popes for hundreds of years. The stunning St. Peter’s Basilica is the centrepiece of Vatican City, and its huge dome can be seen on the Roman skyline from most points in the city. Although not the mother church of the Catholic Church, it is its largest and holiest shrine and an important place of pilgrimage. Then, your comprehensive tour of Vatican Museums will whisk you through the entire complex. Begin with a stroll through the impressive Belvedere Courtyard, before exploring the many rooms and galleries of the museums. Explore the Gallery of Tapestries, and the Gallery of Maps, and be mesmerised by Michelangelo’s great frescoes inside the Sistine Chapel.Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: VIP St. Peter's Basilica tour with Dome climb and Papal Crypt
data.description:
Begin early in the morning at St. Peter’s Square to climb to the summit of the basilica before crowds gather. Take a convenient elevator part of the way, pausing on the terrace to see ornate mosaics up close. Then face 231 steps to the very top, where a sweeping panorama of Rome awaits.

After descending, there’s time to delve into the basilica’s art and architecture. Gaze at Bernini’s monumental bronze baldachin and Michelangelo’s poignant Pietà, while learning about the rich history, legends, and curious traditions that fill every corner of this nearly 400-year-old space. Notice how visitors often pause to rub the foot of a certain statue, a custom linked to ancient tales.

Finally, head quietly into the Papal Crypt to view the tombs of past pontiffs, a sober and sacred setting where speaking is discouraged. Stories of those interred are shared beforehand, offering insight into the men who shaped centuries of history beneath the very heart of St. Peter’s Basilica.

Sights Visited:

  • St. Peter’s Basilica
  • Dome of St. Peter’s Basilica
  • Papal Crypt (not the Scavi)
  • St. Peter’s Square

data.name: Rome Catacombs Tour and Capuchin Crypts with Transportation
data.description: If you’ve ever tried to navigate Rome’s underground wonders, you know it can feel like piecing together a puzzle, with scattered sites and limited access. With us, skip the line to these historic tombs and step into the Capuchin Crypts adorned with the bones of 3,700 friars. Visit Santa Maria in Cosmedin and Pope Hadrian’s Crypt, uncovering the stories of popes and martyrs buried below. With transportation included, this tour connects you to Rome’s most haunting and fascinating sites with ease.Tour OverviewMake your way to Piazza Barberini in central Rome, where you’ll meet your guide holding a sign in front of the fountain (Fontana del Tritone). Along with a small group of up to 23 people and your engaging guide, you’ll walk a couple of minutes to the Capuchin Crypts to view the hauntingly beautiful Bone Chapels. Afterward, board your air-conditioned vehicle to the entrance of the catacombs, about 20 minutes away. Along the way, you’ll pass the historic Appian Way as your guide shares stories of the slave crucifixions during the revolt of Spartacus. At the Catacombs of St. Callixtus, you’ll skip the line and dive straight into exploring the eerie underground tombs, ancient artwork, and more. Conclude your tour at Bocca della Verità (the Mouth of Truth), a legendary Roman landmark steeped in myth and history.Rome Catacombs Tour DescriptionThis 3.5-hour tour includes:A guided tour of the Capuchin CryptsA guided tour of the Catacombs of St. CallixtusPass by the ancient Appian WayAurelian WallsVisit Santa Maria in CosmedinHadrian's Crypt and Mouth of TruthA fun, English-speaking guidePrivate, climate-controlled transportation between sitesWe ask both men and women to cover knees and shoulders, otherwise the catacomb management might refuse entry to religious sites and you’ll miss out on a portion of your tour. We understand the summers in Rome can be hot, so a great alternative is to bring a shawl/scarf/sweater with you. That way you can cover your knees and shoulders when necessary.Capuchin Crypts and BonesThis crypt contains the skeletal remains of some 3,700 human bodies, believed to be Capuchin friars buried by their order. They were buried between the years 1500 and 1870, during which time the Roman Catholic Church permitted burial in and under churches.The underground crypt is divided into six chapels: Crypt of the Resurrection, Crypt of the Skulls, Crypt of the Pelvises, Crypt of the Leg Bones and Thigh Bones, and Crypt of the Three Skeletons. Lit only by dim natural light seeping in through cracks and small fluorescent lamps, the crypt walls are elaborately decorated with skeletal remains.The Catacombs of St. CallixtusAlong the Appian Way is where the first cemeteries of Rome were built. It’s here that you’ll stop to see the above-ground cemeteries of the Catacombs of St. Callixtus. Then it’s time to head underground to see extensive network of burial sites at one of the most popular catacombs in Rome.Over time, these catacombs became the coveted burial place as prominent martyrs and pontiffs were laid to rest here. Your guide will lead you to the crypts filled with popes from the third century as well as an area with impeccably preserved paintings.The Catacombs of St. Callixtus are typically closed on Wednesdays and sometimes close on other days too. Not to worry though, your guide will take you to another incredible catacombs site if your tour lands on one of these days.The Appian Way and Aurelian WallsAs you ride comfortably in your climate-controlled vehicle, you’ll pass along sections of the legendary Appian Way—one of Rome’s oldest and most important roads, stretching all the way to Southern Italy. You will see the road up close and hear unforgettable stories from your guide, including the dramatic revolt of Spartacus and the chilling fate of his army.You’ll also pass beneath the towering Aurelian Walls, built by Emperor Aurelian in the 3rd century to defend Rome from invaders—another powerful reminder of the city’s resilience through the ages.Santa Maria in Cosmedin ChurchFinish your tour with a visit to Santa Maria in Cosmedin, a charming medieval basilica steeped in history. Step into Hadrian's Crypt, a lesser-known gem that is believed to have been a burial site connected to Pope Hadrian at some point in history. Nestled beneath the church, this crypt offers a fascinating glimpse into Rome’s layered past, blending ancient imperial connections with the sacred heritage of the medieval basilica. Finally, test your bravery at the famous Bocca della Verità (Mouth of Truth), a legendary stone mask said to bite the hand of anyone who tells a lie.

data.name: The Heart Of Rome: Family Friendly Private Half-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the best of Rome on this private family-friendly walking tour through its most famous piazzas, fountains, and landmarks. Visit Castel Sant'Angelo and see where ancient emperors kept their treasures and connect with ancient history! On your family-friendly private tour you will:  Enjoy the personal attention of a private tour guide who will keep the whole family engaged,interested, and entertained; See the major highlights of Rome’s city centre in just 3 hours; Throw a coin and make a wish at the stunning Trevi Fountain - see if you can spot the fake windows; Pass by the mighty Pantheon – the 2000-year-old temple to all the gods; Hear how Rome was built layer upon layer – just like a giant lasagna; Stop for a delicious local Gelato on us;  See the beautiful baroque piazzas and learn about the secret insults between the rival artists, Bernini and Borromini; Spot the hidden insults within the statues and architecture with the help of your guide; Guess the rivers on the Fountain of the Four Rivers at Piazza Navona – your guide will give you clues! End the tour with tickets included for a self guided visit to one of Rome's most historic and magnificent monuments: the Castel Sant'Angelo! Enjoy this engaging, family-friendly walking tour of all the highlights of Rome's stunning historic centre with an expert private guide - including a delicious and well-deserved gelato break! Your kids will love exploring some of Rome’s best-known attractions such as Piazza Navona, chucking coins into the Trevi Fountain, and spotting the fake windows and the odd 'cup' that doesn't quite fit. You'll pass by the amazing Pantheon - designed in the 2nd Century by Emperor Hadrian. How did the Ancient Romans build that heavy cement dome with a hole in it? How did it not collapse? Your guide will share historic facts and other fascinating secrets about the Pantheon, like why the church calls it St Mary of the Martyrs. You'll see the amazing Fountain of the Four Rivers at Piazza Navona by the sculptor Bernini, and the magnificent church of Saint Agnes overlooking it, by his arch-rival Borromini. Your guide will help you to guess which four major rivers are represented in the giant statues by Bernini - he left us lots of clues, and will also help you find the insult left on top of the church by Borromini! You will learn how Rome was built - layer on layer, like a giant lasagna! You'll see how Piazza Navona was built over a horse racing stadium, and a marker showing just how high the river Tiber used to flood. See if you can reach it! Your tour ends with tickets included for a self-guided visit to the amazing Castle of the Angel or the Castel Sant'Angelo. Originally the Mausoleum of Hadrian, it became a Papal fortress with a secret passageway that connects it directly to the Vatican! This is also the site in which, legend claims, Archangel Michael appeared sheathing a flaming sword as a sign of the end of the plague of 590 AD. Climb up to the ramparts for an amazing view of the Eternal City - don't worry the giant bronze statue of Archangel Michael will protect you! Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: Passetto di Borgo night guided tour
data.description: Embark on a rare nocturnal guided tour of the Passetto di Borgo, an enigmatic escape route shrouded in mystery and legend, hidden within the Vatican.This elevated medieval corridor, connecting the Vatican to Rome's heart, has been a silent witness to centuries of clandestine activities, papal intrigue, and daring escapes under the cloak of darkness. Its most notable use was by Pope Clement VII, who sought refuge through this passage during the Sack of Rome in 1527. Under the guidance of an expert, traverse the Passetto after sunset when silence and moonlight lend an eerie aura to this already mysterious space. As you journey through, unravel intriguing tales of endangered popes, Vatican conspiracies, and the covert existence of this concealed passage.For those familiar with Dan Brown’s Angels & Demons, the Passetto will be recognised as a pivotal location in the exhilarating quest for Vatican secrets. Now, you have the opportunity to tread the same path, after hours, away from the bustling crowds, completely immersed in its enigma.

data.name: Unforgettable Rome Day Trip to Pompeii and Sorrento
data.description: Coordinating trains, buses, and tickets to visit Pompeii and the Amalfi Coast in a single day from Rome can be exhausting and time-consuming. With us, you’ll travel in comfort, skipping the hassle of logistics and enjoying the stunning beauty of Positano a lively before engaging in the exploration of Pompeii. Enjoy captivating stories, breathtaking views, and a stress-free adventure designed to give you the perfect day.Tour OverviewHead to Piazzale Ostiense in central Rome, where you'll meet your guide near the pyramid across from the metro stop. Board your comfortable, climate-controlled vehicle for a scenic drive to the picturesque town of Positano on the stunning Amalfi Coast. Enjoy free time to wander the charming streets, relax by the beach, browse boutique shops, and partake in a delightful limoncello tasting, savoring the region’s famous citrus flavors.After your free time in Positano, continue to Pompeii, the most important archaeological site in Italy and the scene of one of history’s most famous volcanic disasters. With a friendly, archaeological guide, you’ll explore the ancient city frozen in time, gaining an in-depth understanding of its fascinating history.At the end of your day filled with history, culture, and breathtaking scenery, you’ll return to Piazzale Ostiense in central Rome with a newfound appreciation for the beauty and history of southern Italy.Pompeii and Positano Day Tour DescriptionYour 13-hour day trip includes:Round-trip, luxury transportation from RomeSkip-the-line at PompeiiAn English-speaking archaeologist guide in PompeiiFree time in PositanoEngaging tour leaderA maximum group size of 49Scenic Drive to PositanoAfter meeting your trip leader and the rest of your small group, you'll begin your day with a scenic drive down the Autostrada del Sole (Highway of the Sun) to the coastal town of Positano. Watch as the picturesque countryside unfolds, dotted with lemon orchards and charming villages.Free Time in PositanoYour trip leader will give you tips on how to make the most of your time here, from browsing boutique shops to soaking in the vibrant atmosphere of this Amalfi Coast gem.Enjoy free time to explore at your own pace, savoring the region’s renowned citrus flavors. Stroll the winding streets, relax by the beach, or simply admire the breathtaking coastal views.Guided Tour of PompeiiA UNESCO World Heritage site, Pompeii was buried under volcanic ash and pumice following the catastrophic eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in 79 A.D. This once-thriving Roman city has been frozen in time, offering an unparalleled glimpse into daily life in ancient times.With your archaeologist guide, explore the remarkably intact streets, homes, and public spaces that reveal the secrets of Roman civilization. Uncovered after nearly 2,000 years, the site provides a vivid snapshot of life in one of the Roman Empire’s most prosperous cities.Led by your engaging archaeologist guide, you'll walk through this once-thriving city and see how the well-preserved structures and evidence of daily life reveals secrets about Roman civilization. The city sat undisturbed for almost 2,000 years until a group of explorers discovered that it was still largely intact. As a result, we now have an unparalleled snapshot of life in the prosperous ancient city.Return to RomeAfter a day filled with history, culture, and incredible scenery, meet your group and relax on the drive back to Rome where you'll end at Piazzale Ostiense, arriving in the evening with lasting memories of an extraordinary journey.

data.name: Colosseum tour with arena floor
data.description: Explore the Colosseum and its surroundings with a guide. This guided tour includes the Roman Forum, seen from the bird’s eye view from the Campidoglio, as well as other sites of Ancient Rome.The tour starts with Trajan’s Column where you’ll pass through Via dei Fori Imperiali overlooking the Roman Forum, the civic historical centre. Once home to a bustling marketplace, ruled by moneylenders and shopkeepers, this was Rome at its finest. Your professional English-speaking guide will talk you through the heart and history of Rome’s historic centre, pointing out the temples, arches, and the sanctuary of Ancient Rome’s famous Vestal Virgins. As you continue your walk, your guide will point out Caesar’s and Augustus’ Forums, among other ruins. As you walk past the Forums you will come to the highlight of the tour – the Roman Colosseum. Your guide will lead you around, telling stories about the history and people that once tread on the same ground. You will roam the arena floor where you will gain a better understanding of the magnitude of Ancient Rome’s greatest amphitheatre. data.name: Early Bird: Basilica Santa Maria Maggiore & Undergrounds
data.description:
This exclusive early morning tour of the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore — the most beloved church of Pope Francis — grants you privileged access to its spiritual and architectural wonders before it opens to the public.

With the basilica bathed in soft morning light, you’ll explore its most iconic and hidden spaces: the Loggia of Blessings, the elegant Bernini staircase, the historic Hall of the Popes, and the intimate museum collections.

Then descend into the archaeological undergrounds, where centuries of buried Christian and medieval history await — a rare experience few get to witness.

As you move through this extraordinary space in near silence, you’ll come to understand why it meant so much to Pope Francis, and why this moment feels like a true Roman privilege.

data.name: Rome highlights private golf cart tour with a local guide
data.description: Hop into your golf cart and for a private guided tour through Rome’s rich history. "From Romulus and Remus to gladiator battles and impressive churches, Rome really ticks all the boxes," says Alessio, one of our local expert guides. "And what better way to explore than in style, rolling through the streets on a golf cart?" You’ll feel like you’re starring in Roman Holiday, zipping around the city and covering more ground than on foot.We’ll kick things off by zooming past the legendary Colosseum, where gladiators once fought, cruising through the Circus Maximus, where chariot races were the ultimate crowd-pleaser, and checking out the ancient ruins at Palatine Hill. After that, we’ll head up to the Orange Garden on Aventine Hill, a peaceful spot where you can snap some birds-eye photos and take in the views of the ancient city. Along the way, your guide will drop insider stories and hidden gems that you won’t find in any guidebook.Next, we’ll weave through the narrow alleyways of Trastevere, a fave for locals with some of the best trattorias around. We’ll also swing by Piazza Navona, home to two of Bernini’s famous fountains. You’ll see bustling markets, the Pantheon, and the 3D illusion at hidden gem, Church of St. Ignatius of Loyola. "When you look at the ceiling, it feels like the sky is wide open, but it’s all just an incredible painting." says Alessio. And, no trip to Rome is complete without stopping at the Trevi Fountain, where tossing a coin is said to ensure your return. You’ll wrap things up at the Spanish Steps – the perfect spot for a final snapshot of your Roman adventure.

data.name: Borghese Gallery guided tour with skip-the-line entry

Open your eyes and be dazzled by the works of Caravaggio, Canova, Bernini, and Raphael.During this tour you'll get to know the story behind the famous sculpture of Apollo and Daphne, you'll be amazed by the wonderful works of Bernini, Canova and the most famous paintings by Caravaggio. Walk through the twenty rooms where you can admire the famous painting of "Young Sick Bacchus" by Caravaggio or the Boy with a Basket of Fruit.Admire the works of Gian Lorenzo Bernini, which comprise a significant percentage of his output of secular sculpture, starting with early works such as the Goat Amalthea with Infant Jupiter and Faun to his dynamic Rape of Proserpine, or the iconic Apollo and Daphne which are considered seminal works of baroque sculpture.

The hustle and bustle of the capital is long gone, and as we pedal we will arrive at an oasis of peace: Castel Gandolfo.Here, the medieval village, the view of the crystal clear lake and the Papal Palace, summer residence of the Popes, will surprise you with its beauty and authenticity. Your guide will be able to recommend an excellent Osteria if you prefer a traditional meal or other kiosks where you can sample more than a taste of authentic Castelli Romani products.We will return to Rome comfortably by train, leisurely scrolling through the photos of the wonderful experience we have just had and enjoying the energy and vitality that these places have given us!Do you want an even more authentic and personalized experience? data.description:

This tour offers a perfect blend of food, culture and tradition, perfect for food lovers and cultural enthusiasts alike.

data.name: Semi-Private Day Trip to Pompeii and Naples from Rome
data.description: The tour starts from your hotel in Rome heading towards the Mediterranean coast. During the journey you will have the opportunity to enjoy the stunning views of the Amalfi coast and make a stop along the highway for breakfast. Once you get to the archaeological site of Pompeii, the guide will take you on a tour along the best places of this Roman city, remarkably intact. You will visit the main areas (such as the food market, the baths and the residences of some wealthy citizens) and come to know the custom of the time and the daily life of this city before the destructive volcanic eruption. From Pompeii, you will drive to Naples and start with a visit to “Spaccanapoli”, Via San Gregorio Armeno, Piazza San Domenico, Piazza del Gesù with the Church of Gesù Nuovo and the Basilica of Santa Chiara (the largest Gothic church in Naples). Continue to visit the monumental area and see the Piazza Plebiscito, where you can see the Royal Palace and the Church of San Francesco di Paola. Then head to Via Toledo, where you will be able to admire the splendid Galleria Umberto I, and on to Piazza Municipio, where there is the imposing Angevin fortress of Castle Nuovo. You will have the opportunity to make a brief stop in a former bakery to taste the famous “sfogliatella.”

data.name: From Rome: Best of Tuscany in One Day (with Tastings)
data.description: Take a break from the Italian capital and its chaotic streets to go on a one day Tuscan holiday. This tour will focus on the famous Val d’Orcia region, giving you the chance to visit historical villages like Montepulciano, Pienza and the rolling vineyards of Montalcino. You’ll explore the winding streets and soak in views of the Tuscan hills and countryside as it spreads out before you. You’ll hear old Gregorian chants and stop for lunch at a typical Tuscan farm, leaving plenty of time to sample world-famous foods and wine, all produced locally. If you are only spending a short time in Italy, but really want to experience Tuscany, this tour is the one for you.You'll leave Rome behind and set off to the Etruscan town of Montepulciano where you'll enjoy a tour of the town's most important sights. Visit ancient Etruscan wells and discover the medieval wine cellars still used today before hopping back on the bus to Montalcino. You'll be dropped off at Sant'Antimo Abbey where stone walls ring with the songs of Gregorian monks as they sing traditional chants that have existed for centuries. Then it's time to enjoy incredible views of Tuscany's most beautiful vineyards where Brunello di Montalcino, one of the country’s finest wines, is made.Next up on this itinerary is lunch at a typical Tuscan farm where you'll enjoy a three course meal with the finest local foods and wines. It's the perfect chance to discover some regional delicacies with local wines. Then you'll enjoy a professional guided tasting of the wines produced on site. Back on the bus, you'll head off to Pienza where you'll see the sights and get an insight into the history of this 'utopian village'. If you have time, remember to sample Pienza's most famous product, pecorino cheese!

data.name: Vaticaan, Sixtijnse Kapel en Sint-Pietersplein tour in kleine groep met Nederlandse gids
data.description: Geniet van een rondleiding door Vaticaanstad in een kleine groep met een deskundige Nederlandstalige gids. Beleef een uniek bezoek in je eigen taal én vermijdt lange wachtrijen aan de kassa met skip-the-line tickets.Je gids leidt je door de Vaticaanse musea met als hoogtepunten de Sala degli Animali, de Laocoöngroep (Griekse sculpturen), de Torso del Belvedere dat dateert uit de 1e eeuw van Christus, het Bad van Nero, de Gallerij met wandtapijten en de Kaartengalerij. Aanschouw Rafaels schitterende fresco's in de Stanza della Segnatura, en de privévertrekken van Paus Julius II. Betreed in alle stilte de Sixtijnse Kapel waar op 13 maart 2013 Paus Franciscus in conclaaf is verkozen. Bewonder Michelangelo's adembenemende fresco's - met meer dan 300 figuren op een plafondoppervlakte van ruim 500m2 is dit een van de meest bijzondere kunstwerken ter wereld.Je gepassioneerde gids heeft elk geheim van de kapel ontrafeld en deelt deze graag. Leer Michelangelo en het Vaticaan kennen als geen ander. De tour vervolgt naar de Vaticaanse Bibliotheek en ten slotte verlaat je de musea via de beroemde 'Trap van Momo' die je naar het Sint-Pietersplein brengt. Je gids onthult hier de highlights van de basiliek en geeft je het gevoel dat je een echte Vaticaan expert bent (bezoek basiliek niet inbegrepen).

data.name: Combined Ticket to Castel Sant'Angelo and Ara Pacis Museum
data.description: Dive into Rome's illustrious past with a combined ticket to Castel Sant'Angelo and the Ara Pacis Museum. This special offer allows you to discover two of the city's most important historical landmarks at your leisure, bypass the ticket queues and benefit from flexible entry.Begin your visit at Castel Sant'Angelo, an imposing fortress initially constructed as Emperor Hadrian's mausoleum in the 2nd century AD. Over time, this renowned edifice has functioned as a papal residence, a military stronghold, and currently, a museum exhibiting Rome's complex history. Wander through its medieval chambers, papal dwellings, and ascend to the upper terraces for sweeping views of the city.Next, proceed to the Ara Pacis Museum, housing the Altar of Peace, emblematic of Emperor Augustus's flourishing Rome. The museum's contemporary design by Richard Meier offers a striking juxtaposition to the ancient altar, crafting an engaging experience that merges past with present-day Rome. Marvel at intricate friezes and restored artefacts, and gain a comprehensive insight into Roman art.Situated along the Tiber River, both sites offer a remarkable journey into Rome's imperial and cultural legacy. With this combined ticket, you're granted the liberty to visit both sites at your own pace, enjoying a flexible and smooth experience.

The Vatican Ratified in 1929 as a sovereign state, the108 acres of ground within the Vatican city walls house St. Peter's Basilica, the Vatican Museums with magnificent works of art including the Sistine Chapel with its famous ceiling painted by Michelangelo, and lush immaculately cured gardens. Since it is governed by the Bishop of Rome, the Pope, its government can be described as ecclesiastical and the highest state functionaries are in fact clerics. The modern-day home of the pope, the smallest independent nation state in the world in terms of area and population. It is the territorial seat of the Holy See, the institutional entity represented by the Pope, and hence the principal ecclesiastical seat of the Catholic Church of both Eastern and Western worlds.

data.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum: Entry Ticket
data.description:
For more than a decade, the Leonardo da Vinci Museum has honored the many facets of Leonardo’s genius—painter, inventor, scientist, anatomist, engineer, and architect. Tucked away beneath the Basilica of Santa Maria del Popolo, near the Spanish Steps and Villa Borghese in Piazza del Popolo, it draws visitors from around the globe and ranks as Rome’s most frequented Leonardo da Vinci museum.

Inside, Italian craftsmen’s creations bring Leonardo’s manuscripts to life through interactive machines, while studies of his iconic Renaissance artwork and anatomy sketches line the displays. In-depth videos shed new light on The Last Supper and The Vitruvian Man, and an immersive multimedia room reveals further insights into his life and mind. Divided into thematic areas reflecting Leonardo’s varied interests, the museum offers a comprehensive journey into one of history’s most extraordinary intellects.

data.name: Castel Sant'Angelo: Skip The Line Ticket + Multimedia Video
data.description:
Discover the history of this mausoleum-turned-museum with skip-the-line, hosted access. Located on the right bank of the Tiber and only a short distance from the Vatican City, the Castel Sant'Angelo is an ancient fortress with centuries of history.

Explore the museum's seven floors and see an extensive collection of ancient artifacts and perfectly preserved frescoes from the Renaissance period. Built in 135 AD for the Roman Emperor Hadrian, the building has played an important part in Rome’s architectural legacy.

Climb the spiral staircase to reach the Chamber of Ashes, where a number of historical figures were incarcerated, before continuing up to visit the Papal Residence. Immerse yourself in the stories of different rooms as you admire the art within.

Wrap up your experience with a panoramic view over Rome and the River Tiber from the castle terrace. A great opportunity to take some photos of the Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge, also known as the Bridge of Angels.

Your multimedia guide will help your imagination reconstruct the grand space of the **Roman Forum** where regular Romans used to live and work. See the **tomb of emperor Julius Caesar**, the toppled columns of this ancient civic area, and **explore the ruins at your own pace**.

Located next to the Roman Forum is **Palatine Hill**, the legendary foundation site of Rome. It's the site where the houses of emperors and kings once stood, and is the centermost hill of Rome where you'll **get the best views of the ancient world.**

With this skip-the-line admission ticket, save hours spent waiting in line as you’re fast-tracked directly through the Vatican Museums' entrance. That leaves more time to explore the 54 galleries with their priceless religious and Renaissance artworks.

data.name: Private Tour In the Heart of Rome
data.description: Have the highlights of Rome in your hands and go inside the Pantheon and San Luigi dei Francesi (National French Church). We will pick you up at your hotel and take you to visit the highlights of Baroque Rome, starting from the Spanish Steps. Moving next to Piazza Navona, enjoying a nice walk through the streets of the Capital. Discover secrets and legends of the most popular stairway of the world, background of many Hollywood movies. Enjoy the 18th century atmosphere of the Square with the beautiful Barcaccia, fountain designed by Bernini father and son. Then head to Trevi Fountain: the imposing set for the Oscar winner movie by Fellini “La Dolce Vita”, icon of the Italian sixties and beloved by visitors for the coin throwing tradition, to ensure a future visit to Rome. The Tour will continue with a stop at the Pantheon, one of the most precious ancient Roman monuments. Once Temple dedicated to all the Gods, converted later in a Catholic Church, this is a real masterpiece of architecture with its original ancient dome with the “oculum” and its interior decorations. The visit will continue with a stop inside the Church of St. Louis of the French, which hosts beautiful works of art by Caravaggio. The tour ends in one of the most beautiful squares of Rome: Piazza Navona with the splendid Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi by Bernini and the imposing St. Agnes Church by Borromini.

data.name: Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill Kids-Tailored Tour
data.description: Explore the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill on this private, kid-tailored tour with fun activities like scavenger hunts and quizzes. See the historic Colosseum, wander the Roman Forum, and climb the Palatine Hill, once home to emperors. With your expert guide customizing the experience to your family’s interests, it’s an engaging and unforgettable journey through history.

data.name: Rome Private Colosseum and Roman Forum Family-Friendly Tour
data.description: If you’re tired of bored children at historical monuments, this private family tour brings ancient Rome to life with captivating stories of gladiators, emperors, and more. Tickets to the Colosseum, Forum, and Palatine Hill are included for easy of entry, while your expert guide entertains all ages with fascinating tales—it’s educational fun that holds everyone's attention and brings the city’s magic to life.

data.name: Leonardo da Vinci Exhibition - The Genius of Leonardo: Priority Entrance
data.description: Immerse yourself in the inventive world of Leonardo da Vinci at an interactive exhibit that offers a hands-on look at his forward-thinking creations. Tinker with life-sized reconstructions of his groundbreaking machines, and see his visionary concepts brought to life through animated holograms. Before you go, venture below ground level to explore a centuries-old burial temple hidden within the same building, adding an unexpected historical layer to your visit.

data.name: ROME| Private tour with personal photographer from FLORENCE
data.shortDescription:
Meeting point

We will meet the participants at the station of Florence SMN and leave by high-speed train.

We will arrive in Rome after about two hours and move by public transport to the Colosseum.

 

What will the itinerary be?

The photographic shooting will take about 30 minutes and continue on foot through the Imperial Forums until reaching Piazza Venezia, where the Altare Della Patria is located. The second shooting will take place on the steps of the monument.

Through Via Del Corso, where you can stop for shopping, we'll reach the Antica Trattoria Al Gallinaccio, where we'll have a lunch based on appetizers and local first courses.

In the early afternoon, it will be the turn of photoshoots at the Trevi Fountain and in Piazza di Spagna, then you'll continue along the famous Via Condotti.

We will go back to Roma Termini station by metro to get the train that will take us back to Tuscany (Florence).

 

When and how will the photos be sent?

All the shots of the photographic services will be sent in 48h by WeTransfer or Google Drive.

The photo format will be high quality jpg only.

data.name: Italian | Guided tour of the Colosseum with access to the Gladiator Arena
data.shortDescription: The Colosseum, stands in the archaeological heart of the city of Rome and welcomes large numbers of visitors every day, attracted by the charm of its history and complex architecture. The building was a spectacle in itself. It is in fact the largest amphitheatre in the world, offering astonishing stage sets and spectator facilities. A symbol of the splendour of the empire, the Amphitheatre has changed its face and function over the centuries, offering itself as a structured space but open to the Roman community. Today, the Amphitheatre is a monument to the works of human ingenuity that have survived the passage of time and still presents itself as a welcoming and dynamic structure that offers a wide view of the interior spaces as well as evocative views of the city when looking out from the outside archways.

data.name: Rome Private Full-Day E-Bike Tour with Lunch
data.description: Walking tours are a great way to see Rome, but you can cover much more if you zoom around town by bike. Cycle past key attractions such as the Trevi Fountain and the Pantheon, stopping along the way for an included lunch. An e-bike tour means you’ll be able to get around easily, but won't have to worry about working up a sweat like you would with a pedal-powered bike.

data.name: Rome Colosseum Private Tour With Palatine Hill and Roman Forum
data.description: Follow in the footsteps of Roman gladiators with the help of a guide on this private tour of the Colosseum. Enjoy a personalized experience and feel very free to ask your guide as many questions as you like while you explore this iconic Rome attraction. Listen to unique stories that the average guidebook won’t give you.

data.name: Rome Highlights Private Tour with Colosseum Entrance
data.description:
Choose from a morning or afternoon tour to suit your sightseeing style, and meet your guide at either the Arch of Constantine or, if you select the driving option, with pickup at your hotel in a private vehicle. With the latter option, a driver will be at your disposal all day to whisk you between hard-to-reach sites and wait while you explore. With either option, take advantage of your guide’s expertise in archaeology or art history to delve into Rome's epic past.

Hear the stories behind the Imperial City’s must-see landmarks, from the ancient mythology of the Pantheon to the Baroque flourishes of the Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps, and Piazza Navona. Make the most of your time as your guide shares insight into Roman history on the way to each landmark, and have a quick rest in between attractions. Since it’s a private tour, you can choose to linger at places that captivate you or take a break for a snack or free time — it’s all up to you!

No visit to Rome is complete without a tour of the mighty Colosseum, so skip the long lines at this popular attraction and step inside to hear grisly tales of gladiators and animal hunts. After a visit here, your tour concludes at a convenient central location or with drop-off back at your hotel (with the driving option).

data.name: Appian Way, Catacombs, Aqueducts Private Tour
data.description: The Appian Way is one of the most interesting and historically rich areas of Rome, but getting to—and around—this rugged and off-the-beaten-track neighborhood can be tricky without private transportation. Hit sights like the Catacombs of Saint Callixtus, the Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the Villa di Massenzio, with hassle-free transfers from central Rome and admission tickets included.

data.name: St. Peter's Basilica and Dome Audio Guided Tour with Entrance Tickets
data.description: Experience the magnificent St Peter’s Basilica with entry to the Cupola and a self-guided audio tour. Enjoy 2000 years of history with delicate mosaics, stunning architecture and intricate sculptures before ascending up to see Michelangelo’s Cupola – the crowning dome.Using a digital map and a self-guided audio tour with 27 points of interest, you'll journey through the Basilica's key highlights from the convenience of your smartphone. You'll climb the Dome and have a close look at the interior mosaics, while listening to informative stories about the church's history. Don't forget to take a scenic snap from the very top of the eternal city, while enjoying the panoramic views of St. Peter's Square and the Vatican Gardens.Situated in Vatican City, St. Peter's Basilica stands as a remarkable symbol of both religious importance and exceptional architectural design. Construction of the Renaissance and Baroque-style building began over 500 years ago on the presumed burial site of St Peter, the disciple of Jesus Christ and Pope of the Catholic Church. Don't miss out on this unique experience to see the greatest of all churches of Christendom for yourself.

data.name: Vatican City Small-Group Tour with Museums and Sistine Chapel
data.description:
Meet your guide and small group in Piazza del Risorgimento, then proceed directly into the Vatican museums with skip-the-line access. The tour group is limited to 15 people to ensure personalized attention from your guide, the chance to ask questions, and an intimate experience. 

See Apollo Belvedere and Laocoön and Sons in the Belvedere Courtyard and stroll through the Raphael Rooms. Explore the Gallery of Tapestries, the Gallery of the Maps, the Gallery of the Candelabra, and the Pinecone Courtyard. 

Pause outside the Sistine Chapel so your guide can explain the history behind the iconic ceiling frescoes, then proceed inside to view one of the world's most famous artworks.

Upon exiting the Sistine Chapel, choose to double back through the Vatican Museums to see more of the collection; or your guide through a special door directly into St. Peter’s Basilica for a guided visit.

data.name: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica and Papal Tombs Tour Reserved Entry
data.description: Beneath St. Peter’s Basilica lie the papal tombs, the final resting place of many former popes, including John Paul II. On this guided tour, explore the Basilica’s opulent marble architecture, adorned with Bernini and Michelangelo’s paintings and frescoes, before descending into the papal tombs to learn about influential former popes and how they’re interred.

data.name: Fast Track Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica Tour
data.description: See the best of the Vatican Museums, including the Sistine Chapel, Gallery of Maps, Cortile della Pigna, Pio Clementino Museum, candelabra, tapestries and much more.Skip the long Vatican Museums' lines and experience a guided tour of its most important rooms. Admire the precious masterpieces kept inside one of the biggest museums in the world.Marvel at paintings and sculptures by Michelangelo, Raphael and Bernini. Then continue to St. Peter's Basilica, where you can visit Michelangelo's Pietà and the papal tombs on your own.

data.name: Rome by Vintage Car: Fiat 500 Cabriolet Tour
data.description: Step into a vintage Fiat 500 cabriolet car for a unique tour of Rome. With a local guide at the wheel, you’ll be able to give the sights your full attention as you visit vantage points such as Janiculum Hill where gorgeous photos are guaranteed, and iconic Rome landmarks like the Colosseum.

data.name: Entrance Ticket to National Museum of Castel Sant'Angelo
data.shortDescription:
Funerary monument, splendid Renaissance residence, museum - Castel Sant'Angelo embodies the history of the Eternal City perfectly...


Castel Sant'Angelo: archaeological site, fortress and prison, was well as papal residence full of episodes of great artistic importance.

Visit Castel Sant'Angelo – archaeological site and museum, with a past as fortress, prison, and papal residence – site of episodes of great artistic and historical importance. The National Museum of Castel Sant'Angelo is home to numerous collections, which are largely accessible to the general public, including furniture, furnishings, and precious sculpture and paintings. Collections also include valuable Renaissance ceramics and fragments of monumental sculptural decoration of the Roman era, brought to light from the ancient tomb of Hadrian in the course of numerous excavations and restoration.

data.name: Rome Trastevere and Jewish Ghetto Small-Group Tour with Crypt
data.description: Experience a different side of Rome on this walking tour through Trastevere, Tiber Island, and the Jewish Ghetto. In a city full of world-famous landmarks, this small-group experience reveals quieter corners and history not often found in the guidebooks. Uncover its oldest synagogue, journey below street level to ancient crypts and hear local anecdotes for a more authentic retelling of Rome's past.

data.name: Rome Trastevere Walking Food Tour
data.description: Trastevere is well-known for its traditional food , in-walled by the second wall circle under the emperor Adrian , it was always a traditional area , lived by fisherman , traders , merchants , the freshest food reached this side of the Tiber river before going to the emperor table! Get wrapped by the authentic Roman atmosphere while tasting local food and learning its secrets.

data.name: Rome Trastevere Quarter Private Walking Tour with Gelato
data.description:
Make your way to a centrally-located meeting point in Trastevere, where you’ll meet your private guide. Stroll to the Sistus Bridge across the Tiber River, then continue to Porta Settimiana, a gate in the fortified walls that Emperor Aurelian built in the 3rd century.

Walk down quiet alleyways past Trastevere’s colorful, historic houses, craft shops, old bakeries, and ancient city walls and ruins. See a lineup of the neighborhood’s highlights including Vicolo del Cinque, the Palazzo San Callisto, Piazza Trilussa, and the Basilicaof Santa Maria in Trastevere, one of Rome’s oldest churches, and the most important church in the area.

The final stop on your walking tour is a beloved gelato shop, or gelateria, that some consider to be the best spot for Roman gelato (you can judge for yourself, as samples are included in this tour). At the end of the walking tour, keep exploring Trastevere on your own, or head to the nearest bus or taxi station with the guide.

data.name: Rome: Audio Guide App
data.shortDescription: Discover over 130 highlights in Rome with your smartphone
data.description: Over 130 points of interests around Rome are yours to explore with this self-guided sightseeing tour, all on a cool new mobile phone app! Get full audio commentary, offline digital maps, walking itineraries, suggested bus and tram routes... even tips for the best photo spots!

data.name: Rome Italian Food Cooking Class With Farmer's Market Visit
data.description: Learn how to cook authentic Italian dishes while sampling a variety of Italian wines on this half-day small-group cooking class. Head into the city to explore farmers' markets while your chef-guide shows you how to shop for the freshest ingredients, before setting up in the kitchen to craft dishes such as handmade ravioli and classic tiramisu.

data.name: San Valentine's Opera Dinner in Rome
data.description: Indulge in an enchanting and romantic Valentine’s evening with a candlelight dinner set in the musical ambiance that only the Italian Opera can provide. This limited and exclusive event takes place in the Innocenzo X Hall at Pamphilj Palace, offering a stunning view of Piazza Navona. In this elegant venue, you will be seated at your reserved table to enjoy the finest Italian cuisine, paired with a selection of exquisite wines. The evening features a musical program with Arias and love Duets from the Opera, performed both before dinner and between the courses, culminating in a delightful surprise finale. Don’t miss this unique event, an unforgettable memory to take home from Rome. Perfect for Valentine’s Day, this experience will make your evening truly special.

data.name: Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel: Skip-The-Line Guided Tour (French Language)
data.shortDescription:
Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: Saints Tour has prepared for you a unique and unforgettable experience. The present tour includes:

  • privileged entrance to the Vatican Museums
  • guided tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel

You will have at your complete disposal one of our specialized and accredited by the Vatican guides. The route of this guided tour has been designed to let you discover – in approximately two and a half hours, with the assistance of a skilled tour guide trained in art history – unique masterpieces without wasting time in long queues.


TICKET INFO

Free: from 0-5 years old;
Reduced: 6 to 18 years old;
Students (reduced): from 19-25 years old. This offer is valid only upon presentation of a valid student card, to be shown at the time of entry and/or check-in.

 

Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: what awaits you


With this guided tour, you will be able to admire some of the most famous works of art renown all over the world: we are offering a journey into time and space, into history and culture, but, most of all, a fast-starting journey, where no exhausting waits in queue are involved.

Our groups are made up by a maximum of 30 people and are all accompanied by certified Vatican tour guides, who will take you through the priceless artistic treasures enshrined in the seven different museums that make up the very heart of the Vatican Museum complex.
In a relaxed and informal atmosphere, your guide will tell you stories and curiosities that will help
you to understand the historical, artistic and cultural context that has molded the masterpieces hosted in the Hall of the Muses, in the Pio-Clementine Museum, in the Gallery of Maps, in the Gallery of Tapestries, in the Raphael Rooms and in the magnificent Courtyard of the Pinecone that opens in the heart of Vatican City.

The tour of the Vatican Museums will culminate with the visit to the Sistine Chapel; since it is forbidden to speak aloud inside, your guide will deliver explanations and directions outside, using the special panels provided by the Museums. Once inside, you can admire the paintings that truly represent the highest peak of Italian Renaissance art, from the precious frescoes by Botticelli, Perugino, Pinturicchio, Ghirlandaio, Luca Signorelli and Piero di Cosimo, to the extraordinary vault cycle and the Last Judgement by Michelangelo.

At the end of this incredible experience, your guide will briefly tell you about the history of the Vatican and the majestic St Peter’s Basilica.

SOME CURIOSITIES

  • The Vatican Museums were established by Pope Julius II in 1506 from a single statue, the marble group of Laocoon.
  • The Gallery of Maps, 120 meters long, ideally reproduces the line of the Apennines: on the left, there are the regions facing the Tyrrhenian Sea, and on the right those facing the Adriatic Sea.
  • In the Stanza della Segnatura, the philosophers who crowd the School of Athens painted by Raphael, have the features of his fellow painters: Bramante is the mathematician Euclid, Plato displays Leonardo’s hieratic face, Heraclitus borrows the frowning expression of Michelangelo, whose shady character was universally known. In the foreground, Buonarroti’s infamous boots, which he did not take off even to go to bed.
  • A self-portrait of Michelangelo can be found in the Sistine Chapel  more precisely, in the Last Judgment: Buonarroti reproduced his features in the skin that St. Bartholomew holds in his hands.
  • All the conclaves that precede the papal elections, take place today in the Sistine Chapel.

data.name: National Etruscan Museum of Villa Giulia Entrance Tickets
data.shortDescription:
The Museum of Villa Giulia was born in 1889 on the initiative of Felice Barnabei (1842-1922), archaeologist and political Italian, based on a coherent program of archaeological explorations.

The Hall of Arts and Sciences (room 27) is dedicated to the history of the Museum.

The new concrete prospects generated by the impending enlargement of the Museum of Villa Giulia are illustrated in the panels to the right of the entrance and modern windows with windows that open out on the Villa Poniatowski to accommodate an extensive review of materials recently acquired.

It is mostly fine ceramics of different age and production, sometimes real masterpieces, stolen by tomb robbers, they have been returned from major museums and private collectors in the United States as a result of a complex operation promoted by Italy. Alongside these include other important objects from seizures ordered by the judiciary as a result of brilliant operation conducted by the Police Command for the Protection of Cultural Heritage.

data.shortDescription:
A tour of the Gardens allows the visitor to be part of a group tour conducted by an official Vatican Guide. The tour is unique, as it takes the visitor through 2000 years of history. Besides the natural beauty of the gardens, the Vatican City is rich in monument and precious works of art.

The reservation allows individual visitors to be part of a Vatican Group Tour conducted by an official Vatican Tour Guide. After clearing security, the meeting point will be at the "Guided Tours" booth, which is located straight ahead up the small staircase on the left.

data.name: Milan City Sightseeing from Rome by high-speed train
data.description: With this High-Speed Train and Bus Pass Package, you have the freedom to travel from Rome to Milan and discover the city at your leisure. Once you arrive at Milano Centrale, the Visitor Centres will provide all the assistance you need. From the nearest stop to the Central Station, hop on a City Sightseeing Milan bus and easily reach landmarks such as the Duomo, San Siro, La Scala and many more. On board, you can benefit from multi-lingual commentary that provides fascinating insights into the city's history and fascinating facts. Free WiFi allows you to download the Sightseeing Experience app, which provides an additional audio guide in 5 languages and real-time bus tracking with waiting times at each stop.

data.name: Pizza & Tiramisu Making Class with Wine and Limoncello
data.description: Discover the ultimate pizza and tiramisu cooking class in Rome, just a short stroll from the iconic Piazza Navona. Under the guidance of a skilled local chef, learn how to prepare the perfect pizza from scratch and create a traditional tiramisu using authentic, high-quality ingredients.This interactive, hands-on experience will teach you how to knead and shape pizza dough like a pro, top it with fresh and flavorful ingredients, and uncover the secrets of making the classic Italian tiramisu with mascarpone, espresso, and savoiardi.Once the cooking is complete, relax and enjoy your homemade pizza and tiramisu in a warm and friendly setting. Pair your creations with a glass of wine, refreshing water, and a taste of limoncello to round off the experience.Perfect for food enthusiasts and travelers seeking a fun and unforgettable activity, this pizza and tiramisu class provides an authentic taste of Italy in one of Rome’s most charming locations. Don’t miss the chance to make your Roman holiday even more special with this unique culinary adventure!

data.name: Small Group Tour of the Vatican, Sistine Chapel and Basilica
data.description: Explore the Vatican’s extensive collections of artwork and historical artefacts in this tour. Led by a guide, small groups of guests learn about the cultural and religious significance of what is on display, as well as the history of the Vatican buildings themselves. Ideal for travellers wanting to take in the highlights of what the Vatican has to offer in a single tour.

data.name: Unique Professional Photoshoot Be the Model of Your Roman Holiday
data.description: Capture your memories of Rome to enjoy for years to come with a private photoshoot package around the city. Visit some of the Eternal City’s most scenic spots such as the Colosseum and St. Peter’s Square as well as smaller square and alleys to capture your trip to Rome. Leave with a digital album of professional photos to cherish for many years.

data.name: Vatican, Sistine Chapel Private Family Tour
data.description: The Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel are among the most popular attractions in Rome, drawing millions of annual visitors. This private tour is tailor-made for families, with skip-the-line tickets so you don’t have to worry about long queues, entertaining commentary designed to keep all ages engaged, and interactive elements such as stories, games, and multimedia tools.

data.name: Vatican Museum Skip-The-Line Ticket With Audio Guide
data.description: Skip the line and spend the time you save on more sightseeing later by pre-booking your Vatican Museum experience. Focus on the parts of the museum that interest you the most, from the Raphael Rooms to the Gallery of Maps to the incomparable Sistine Chapel, and beyond. With an audio guide, you’ll learn things about all the art and artifacts that you wouldn’t get to hear if you explored alone.

data.name: Michelangelo's masterpieces walking tour
data.shortDescription:
Another news for 2025!

Walk through Rome on a tour that explores the life and work of Michelangelo. See some of the artist's most famous pieces and hidden gems, and learn about the art and history of the city.

data.name: Saint Peter’s Tour: guided tour of Grottoes and Basilica
data.shortDescription:
Discover the heart of St Peter's Basilica with our exclusive Vatican Grottoes tour. Start your journey by exploring the underground passages of St. Peter's Basilica, resting place of numerous pontiffs, where our expert guide will reveal stories of faith and power. The Vatican grottoes also hold many extraordinary works of art.

Next, admire the architecture and works of art inside St. Peter's Basilica, with a special focus on its imposing dome, Michelangelo's masterpiece.
The tour does not include access to the Dome, which is optionally available at an extra cost. A unique experience to discover history and spirituality in one of the most sacred places in the world.

data.name: Castel Sant'Angelo: Entry Ticket + Hop-on Hop-off Boat Tour
data.shortDescription: Explore Rome by land and water
data.description:
You're the captain of your itinerary with this combo ticket to Castel Sant'Angelo and the hop-on hop-off boat! 

At the historic Castel Sant'Angelo, the past comes to life around you as you explore every nook and cranny of this majestic fortress. Gaze at the frescoes, stroll down its decorated halls, and get incredible, panoramic views of the city.

Don't forget, you can use the hop-on hop-off boat to get there, as well as to reach a number of other attractions!

data.name: Rome Basilicas Private Guided Tour With Santa Maria Maggiore
data.description: Rome's basilicas are masterpieces of art and architecture, but fly under the radar of most tourists. Discover the treasures inside St. Peter in Chains, St. John Lateran, and St. Mary Major on this unique itinerary that covers the most important basilicas after St. Peter's. See works by Michelangelo, climb the Holy Stairs, and visit the tomb of the late Pope Francis as you learn more about the history and significance of these monumental churches from your guide.

data.name: In Rome like a star: e-bike tour with photo shoot
data.description: Become the protagonist for a day! Strike a pose and let the lens capture your personality and emotions while you experience your unforgettable Roman holiday! A guided bike tour with photo shoot captures your most beautiful moments with Rome in the background and you in the foreground. A unique opportunity to discover the city from a completely new perspective and take home unforgettable memories! Pedal together with your guide, towards the most iconic places in the city, listen to anecdotes and curiosities and show off your best smile!Have fun with us with this new way of visiting Rome, you will be able to discover the city in an original, more intimate and personal way, creating a deep bond with all the places you will visit!Give yourself a gift!: photos are the best souvenir you can take away from an experience, and our photography bike tour is a great idea to celebrate a birthday, share an unforgettable moment with a special person or simply treat yourself to a moment of pleasure.Saddle up with us, your camera is ready!

data.name: Early Morning No Heat No Crowds Rome Tour for Kids and Families
data.description: Explore Rome’s iconic outdoor landmarks on a delightful two-hour walking tour designed specifically for children. Beginning at the historic Spanish Steps, kids can safely climb the 135 steps for a stunning view of the city in the peaceful morning light. Stroll through Rome’s charming streets to the serene Trevi Fountain, where children can learn about the tradition of tossing coins to make wishes. Admire the ancient Pantheon from the outside, capturing young imaginations with its grand architecture. The tour concludes at Piazza Navona, a lively square featuring beautiful Baroque fountains and history, perfect for young explorers to enjoy.

data.name: Classic Italian Pizza-making Workshop in Rome
data.description: Master one of Italy’s most famous food staples on this Italian pizza cookery class in Rome.  With all your kitchen equipment and fresh ingredients provided, listen as your talented local chef shares tips and tricks to produce the perfect pizza dough every time. Mix your flour and water like the real Italian pizzaiolos, and create your tasty masterpiece. Pizza is a real symbol of Italy, and it’s prepared with simple ingredients and just a little Italian flair! Next up, create and bake your own pizza. Choose the toppings to create your favorite pizza, and watch it rise and bake in the oven.  When your pizza is baked and ready, take a seat for a lunch or dinner of homemade pizza and a good glass of wine in the heart of Rome.

data.name: Papal Audience Guided Tour - English Language
data.shortDescription:
An unusual tour combining art, culture and devotion, accompanied by a specialized guide accredited by the Vatican City. The wonder of discovering, every Wednesday, from spring to autumn, a sleepy and quiet St. Peter’s Square disclosing its treasures before your very eyes. Your guide will entertain you with stories from great history and everyday life, anecdotes and explanations of historical, artistic and archaeological nature related to the square and the Basilica.

At the end of the description, you will take place in your exclusive and reserved seat, to attend the Papal Audience. This is not a religious celebration, but a meeting occasion dedicated to devotees and pilgrims, who can meet Pope Francis and receive his blessing. Aboard the Popemobile, the Pope will tour the square departing from the Arch of the Bells; along the path, he will make several stops to greet and embrace the attendees. The duration of the audience is about 1 hour and a half.

data.name: Vatican Gardens by minibus and Castel Sant'Angelo tour
data.description: Discover the beauty of the Vatican Gardens and the Sistine Chapel on this combo experience of bus tour and museums visit. Enjoy amazing views from an open-air minibus, and visit the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel at your own pace with your reserved entrance. Then discover the Castel Sant'Angelo, explore the museum's seven floors to discover an extensive collection of ancient artifacts and perfectly preserved frescoes from the Renaissance period.Take a bus for 45 minutes to the exclusive landscaped area of the Vatican Gardens designed by the great Renaissance architect Carlo Maderno. Then enjoy a visit to the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel. There are countless things to see, but make sure you don't miss the 5 highlights: the 4 dazzling Raphael Rooms that make up the public part of the Popes' apartments, the Torso del Belvedere, the San Girolamo in the desert of Leonardo da Vinci, the Round Room and the Sistine Chapel.Next, discover the history of Castel Sant'Angelo mausoleum-turned-museum with skip-the-line, hosted access. Built in 135 AD for the Roman Emperor Hadrian, the building has played an important part in Rome's architectural history. Located on the right bank of the Tiber only a short distance from the Vatican City, the Castel Sant'Angelo is an ancient fortress with centuries of amazing history not to be missed!

data.name: OT Rome Spanish Guided Tour with Colosseum Ticket, Palatine Hill and Roman Forum
data.description: TOUR HIGHLIGHTSSkip the long queues to the three largest sites of Ancient RomeEmbark on a 2.5-hour tour with a professional experienced Spanish Speaking guideEnjoy a spectacular view over the Forum from the Capitoline HillTimed Entranced access to one of the world’s most-visited and ancient monuments. With this guided tour get into the must-see sites of Roman history: the Colosseum, Palatine Hill, and Roman Forum.

data.name: E-Bike Tour in Parco degli Acquedotti and Via Appia Antica, Rome
data.shortDescription: Explore Parco degli Aquedotti and ride on ancient Roman roads on this incredible e-bike tour through Via Appia Antica, Rome!
data.description:
Explore Parco degli Aquedotti and ride on ancient Roman roads on this incredible e-bike tour through Via Appia Antica, Rome!

Hop on a brand-new e-bike and pedal in the calm and relaxing countryside paths of Rome, far from the hustle and bustle of the city centre. With a local guide, you’ll ride the first 9 km (6 miles) of the infamous Appian Way and cruise through the arches of the Roman aqueduct. 

First, a friendly and local guide will welcome you at the meeting point in Via Appia Antica and brief you about the activity. After hopping on your e-bikes, it’ll be time to leave on this incredible time-travel journey. Follow your guide through this 16-km bike tour and enjoy a first stop at the Villa and Circus Maxentius, the second-largest circus in Rome. After a quick visit, head towards the Tomb of Cecilia Matella and Capo di Bove Baths. Following your guide, you’ll reach the stunning Parco degli Aquedotti, part of the Appian Way Regional Park. Enjoy over 240 ha (593 acres) of natural and historical beauty as you pedal through the park with your group. At the end of this incredible e-bike tour, your guide will take you back to the meeting point in Via Appia.

Join this incredible e-bike tour and live the most authentic experience of Rome, far from the crowds. Book your spot and explore Parco degli Acquedotti and Via Appia Antica!

data.shortDescription:
Decollo, atterraggio e la vista dall’alto delle più belle città del mondo (Dubai, Parigi, Londra, Miami, Roma, Ibiza, Barcellona e New York).

data.name: Appian way Walking tour and Catacombs of Rome
data.description: Explore the lesser-known gems of Rome on our Via Appia and Catacombs of Rome Tour. This tour offers a unique glimpse into Christian Rome, with a visit to the ancient Catacombs of San Sebastian, and skip-the-line access included.Begin your journey along the historic Via Appia, one of Rome’s oldest roads, where you’ll admire landmarks like the Mausoleum of Cecilia Metella, the Circus of Maxentius, and the Mausoleum of Romulus. The tour then takes you underground to the Catacombs of San Sebastian, where you’ll learn about the early Christians who worshiped and were buried there.Step away from the busy city center and immerse yourself in the peaceful history of the Via Appia and the early Christian community. This tour is a unique and enriching experience that showcases a different side of Rome. Don’t miss out!

data.name: Tour of St. Paul's Basilica and Christian History
data.description: Join a spiritual experience exploring the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls. One of the four major Basilicas and sites of the Holy Doors open in 2025 throughout the Holy Jubilee Year, St. Paul's is an essential stop on a pilgrimage to Rome.Step into the hallowed grounds of St. Paul Outside the Walls, where your 60-minute tour delves into the rich tapestry of history and faith that defines this UNESCO World Heritage Site. As you traverse the ancient corridors, guided by the flickering light of faith, you'll discover a sanctuary steeped in centuries of devotion. Here, amidst the intricate artwork and sacred relics, lies the essence of Christian history—a testament to the power of faith.Begin your pilgrimage at the threshold of St. Paul's Basilica and learn of St. Paul's martyrdom and the miraculous preservation of his legacy, as recounted by scholars versed in the annals of Christian history. Immerse yourself in the grandeur of St. Paul's architectural marvels, from the golden mosaic facade to the sacred relics enshrined within. Marvel at the relic of the chain that bound the apostle during his captivity, a poignant reminder of his unwavering devotion.

data.name: Rome Underground Private Tour: Catacombs and San Clemente
data.description: Some of Rome’s most fascinating wonders lie beneath its streets. Discover them without the stress of navigating the city on this private guided tour, with pickup and drop-off at your central Rome accommodation. Learn about early Christian life amid Roman persecution in the Domitilla Catacombs (Catacombe di Domitilla), then descend beneath the Basilica of San Clemente al Laterano into two different layers of Roman history.

data.name: Appian Way Guided E-Bike Tour to Castel Gandolfo with Lunch
data.description: Leave the bustle of Rome behind and follow the ancient Appian Way through the countryside with this guided e-bike adventure. Pass Roman tombs and ruins as you pedal to Castel Gandolfo, where you can take a dip in Lake Albano and explore the historic town. Stop for a two-course lunch with local wine at a traditional “osteria” before hopping on the train back to the city.

data.shortDescription:
Spread over several buildings, including the Palazzo Massimo, Palazzo Altemps, the Crypta Balbi, and the Diocletian Baths, the Roman National Museum preserves the world’s greatest collection of Greco-Roman art. Your combo ticket is valid for three days and gives you access to all connected museums.

data.name: BASILICA |Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel: Skip-The-Line Guided Tour (Spanish Language)
data.shortDescription:
Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: Saints Tour has prepared for you a unique and unforgettable experience. The present tour includes:

  • privileged entrance to the Vatican Museums
  • guided tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel

You will have at your complete disposal one of our specialized and accredited by the Vatican guides. The route of this guided tour has been designed to let you discover – in approximately two and a half hours, with the assistance of a skilled tour guide trained in art history – unique masterpieces without wasting time in long queues.


TICKET INFO

Free: from 0-5 years old;
Reduced: 6 to 18 years old;
Students (reduced): from 19-25 years old. This offer is valid only upon presentation of a valid student card, to be shown at the time of entry and/or check-in.

 

Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: what awaits you


With this guided tour, you will be able to admire some of the most famous works of art renown all over the world: we are offering a journey into time and space, into history and culture, but, most of all, a fast-starting journey, where no exhausting waits in queue are involved.

Our groups are made up by a maximum of 30 people and are all accompanied by certified Vatican tour guides, who will take you through the priceless artistic treasures enshrined in the seven different museums that make up the very heart of the Vatican Museum complex.
In a relaxed and informal atmosphere, your guide will tell you stories and curiosities that will help
you to understand the historical, artistic and cultural context that has molded the masterpieces hosted in the Hall of the Muses, in the Pio-Clementine Museum, in the Gallery of Maps, in the Gallery of Tapestries, in the Raphael Rooms and in the magnificent Courtyard of the Pinecone that opens in the heart of Vatican City.

The tour of the Vatican Museums will culminate with the visit to the Sistine Chapel; since it is forbidden to speak aloud inside, your guide will deliver explanations and directions outside, using the special panels provided by the Museums. Once inside, you can admire the paintings that truly represent the highest peak of Italian Renaissance art, from the precious frescoes by Botticelli, Perugino, Pinturicchio, Ghirlandaio, Luca Signorelli and Piero di Cosimo, to the extraordinary vault cycle and the Last Judgement by Michelangelo.

At the end of this incredible experience, your guide will briefly tell you about the history of the Vatican and the majestic St Peter’s Basilica.

SOME CURIOSITIES

  • The Vatican Museums were established by Pope Julius II in 1506 from a single statue, the marble group of Laocoon.
  • The Gallery of Maps, 120 meters long, ideally reproduces the line of the Apennines: on the left, there are the regions facing the Tyrrhenian Sea, and on the right those facing the Adriatic Sea.
  • In the Stanza della Segnatura, the philosophers who crowd the School of Athens painted by Raphael, have the features of his fellow painters: Bramante is the mathematician Euclid, Plato displays Leonardo’s hieratic face, Heraclitus borrows the frowning expression of Michelangelo, whose shady character was universally known. In the foreground, Buonarroti’s infamous boots, which he did not take off even to go to bed.
  • A self-portrait of Michelangelo can be found in the Sistine Chapel  more precisely, in the Last Judgment: Buonarroti reproduced his features in the skin that St. Bartholomew holds in his hands.
  • All the conclaves that precede the papal elections, take place today in the Sistine Chapel.
