data.name: Rooftop ​Opera Dinner​ in Rome
data.description: Step into a world of timeless elegance and charm as you enjoy an unforgettable evening at Seen by Olivier, the refined rooftop of the Anantara Palazzo Naiadi Rome Hotel. From this breathtaking vantage point overlooking Piazza della Repubblica, embark on a sensory journey where fine dining meets world-class music. Relax in your reserved seat and savor a candlelit dinner under the stars. Each dish, meticulously curated and paired with exquisite Italian wines, is a celebration of the finest culinary traditions. As the evening unfolds, a mesmerizing musical program of opera arias and duets comes to life. Performed by internationally acclaimed artists, the music surrounds you in an intimate setting where every note resonates with power and emotion. A special surprise finale ensures that this experience is truly one of a kind. More than just an event, it is a memory you will cherish forever.

data.name: Love affairs and Papal power small group tour Rome
data.description: Dive headfirst into a whirlwind of Papal power, love affairs, and mystery on this small guided tour through the heart of Rome. Along the way, you’ll meet a colourful cast of characters – from powerful families to influential women – who left their mark on the Eternal City. Valeria, one of our local guides, says, ‘This tour is like a non-stop drama. We'll also step into the very scenes that inspired Puccini's timeless opera, Tosca – a tale of love and heartache.’ Kick start your tour at Castel Sant'Angelo, its ancient walls concealing centuries of Papal secrets. Here, we'll unravel the tragic story of Beatrice Cenci, a member of one of Renaissance Rome’s most illustrious families, whose life ended in tragedy with accusations of her father's murder. ‘Legend has it, that her ghost still roams the bridge on September 10th’, says local guide Valeria. But the drama doesn’t end here. Castel Sant’Angelo also sets the stage for the gripping finale of Puccini’s Tosca – where love, betrayal, and sacrifice reach their climax. Stroll along Via dei Coronari, where you'll uncover juicy tales of secret affairs hidden in the city's shadows, along with scandalous anecdotes about the notorious Borgia family. Soak up the vibrant atmosphere of iconic squares such as Piazza Fiammetta and Piazza Navona, until the tour comes to an end at Piazza Farnese. Snap up those insta-worthy shots in front of the Farnese Palace, where the echoes of Papal power and romance still linger, leaving you with a new perspective on Rome’s captivating past.

data.name: Welcome Rome Semi private walking tour
data.description: Rome is a magnificent city but sometimes it can discourage tourists due to its size and the number of sights to visit. For this reason we have decided to offer this tour that will help you learn more about Rome, what it offers and where to go…when in Rome, do as the Romans do! On this introductory walking tour, discover attractions such as the Pantheon, the Spanish Steps, and the Trevi Fountain. Your guide will shed light on Rome’s famous landmarks, with helpful tips on how and when it's best to visit them.This tour is not just about the history of Rome it is also an opportunity to get suggestions on getting around the city, where to eat, where to do some shopping and get the most from your trip in Rome.

data.name: Rome Colosseum Roman Forum Palatine Hill and Hop-on Hop-off Bus
data.description:
Discover the iconic treasures of Rome with this all-in-one package, featuring access to the Colosseum, Roman Forum, Mamertine Prison, and Palatine Hill, plus a 24-hour Big Bus hop-on, hop-off sightseeing tour.

Begin at the Mamertine Prison, once a feared fortress for Rome’s enemies, now brought to life through an immersive digital audio guide. Step into the grandeur of the Colosseum, explore the heart of ancient Rome at the Roman Forum, and ascend Palatine Hill, the legendary birthplace of the Eternal City.

Then, take in the Eternal City from an open-top bus as it cruises past must-see landmarks like the Vatican, Piazza Venezia, and Circus Maximus. With 8 convenient stops, you're free to hop on and off as you explore the city’s wonders at your own pace.

• Discover the Colosseum, Roman Forum & Palatine Hill.

• Explore Mamertine Prison with a compelling audio guide.

• Tour the city on a 24-hour hop-on, hop-off open-top bus.

• Enjoy panoramic views of top landmarks and attractions.

data.name: Villa D’Este and Villa Adriana: Skip the Line + Roundtrip from Rome
data.description: Get out to where public transport will never take you, and see the beautiful villas in Tivoli, 30 km from Rome. Your ticket includes the ride there and back on a comfy bus, a live guide to fill you in on all the facts, and skip-the-line entrance to both Villa D’Este and Villa Adriana.

data.name: Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel: Small-Group Tour
data.description: Home to a vast collection of treasures, including masterpieces by Michelangelo and Raphael, the Vatican Museums can feel overwhelming for first-time visitors. Head straight to the highlights on a small-group tour that includes skip-the-line admission. An expert guide brings each item's story to life and ensures you make the most of your visit.

data.name: Rome Private Walking Tour With A Professional Guide
data.description: No city equals the history of the Eternal City: one of the roots of western civilization, it has everything to offer, from ancient to new. With its 2700 years of existence, Rome has long reigned as Caput Mundi, the Capital of the World. Its monumental buildings are reminiscent of the era when emperors like Julius Cesar, Nero and Trajan ruled the Roman Empire. But not all is ancient in Rome. Much of its attractiveness is due to the Renaissance, when new squares such as the Piazza del Campidoglio were done and new buildings were constructed including the world's largest church, Saint Peter's Basilica. We will take you to get a better look into Rome’s streets and cobblestone alleys, over through churches, romantic squares, and the famous fountains of Rome. Bring a bottle of water with you! All of Rome’s water fountains have drinkable water. Some of the sites will include the Spanish Steps, the Trevi Fountain, and the beautiful Piazza Navona with Bernini’s four Rivers Fountain.

data.name: Vatican Museums Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Private Tour
data.description: Immerse yourself in art and religious history with this private tour of the Vatican. Enjoy exploring the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and St. Peter’s Basilica in this comprehensive experience. Meet your private guide away from the busy entrance crowds, as they lead you around the Vatican’s highlights. Learn directly from them as you discover the details of the artefacts and the architecture surrounding you. Perfect for guests who want to dedicate a good chunk of time to their visit to the Vatican.

data.name: Rome by Night: Guide E-bike Tour with Salami, Cheese and Wine Tasting
data.description:
What could be more fun than seeing Rome on two wheels, going where regular vehicles can't go? Book this once-in-a-lifetime experience and cross 'seeing Rome by e-Bike' off your bucket list!

Your adventure will begin close to St. Maria Maggiore, one of the most beautiful basilicas of Rome. Pedal up to the top of the Aventino hill for a striking sunset panoramic view of the Eternal city.

Then head on to Fori Imperiali, Campidoglio, and Circo Massimo, which are particularly beautiful at dusk.

Stop for a delicious dinner at one of the best Salumerias in Rome and enjoy a food tasting of salami, cheese and wine.

data.name: Rome Private Guided Photoshoot
data.description: Embrace the moment without the stress of posing with this guided photoshoot to capture the best of your Rome holiday. Choose your shoot location—from the Colosseum and Vatican to Trastevere or Monti—or let your photographer suggest locations to serve as the background of your photos. data.name: Vatican & Colosseum in a Day: Private Full-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Experience the magic of Rome with a fully guided walking tour of the most popular highlights of the Eternal City and discover the Colosseum, the historic centre and the Vatican Museums in a day with entrance tickets included. On your private full-day walking tour, you will: Walk in the footsteps of Gladiators as you explore the Colosseum, the largest standing amphitheatre in the world; Learn about the emperors who built the Flavian Amphitheatre and the opening 100 days of games; See the iconic Triumphal Arch of Constantine, built by Constantine the Great in 315AD; Explore the ruins of the Roman forum, the downtown of Ancient Rome; See the major highlights of Rome’s Centro Storico (historic centre) including the Pantheon, Trevi Fountain and Piazza Navona; Stop for lunch in one of your guide's favourite haunts (lunch not included in the cost of the tour); Hop in a taxi across town to visit the Vatican Museums; Tour the highlights of the magnificent Vatican Museums, including the Pinecone courtyard, the Laocoön, Galleries of the Maps and Tapestries, and the amazing Raphael Rooms; Marvel at the works of MichelangeloBuonarroti in the SistineChapel - the grand finale!; End your tour on the Balcony of the iconic St. Peter's Basilica, after which you are welcome to continue exploring the Basilica at your own leisure. Discover the religious, historical, and cultural significance of Rome, once the Caput Mundi (head of the world) on this magical full-day privately guided tour. Walk in the footsteps of slaves and emperors, gladiators and Vestal Virgins, cardinals and artists as your expert guide weaves together the stories that have made Rome the Eternal City. Relish walking into the Colosseum and step out onto the stage – the most famous monument of the ancient world. Learn about a day in the life of an ancient Roman as you stroll through the Forum admiring the temples and basilicas still standing after two millennia. Then plunge into the friendly hustle and bustle of ‘modern’ Rome as you walk around the historic centre, taking in such iconic sites as the Trevi Fountain, Piazza Navona and the mighty Pantheon – the largest man-made cement dome with an oculus in the world. And it was built in the second century! After a pit stop for lunch, hop in a taxi across town where your guide will lead you through the hallowed halls of the Vatican Museums to wonder and marvel at the masterpieces from antiquity and those extraordinary, god-like rivals of the High Renaissance: Michelangelo and Raphael. On exiting the Sistine Chapel your tour will end on the iconic balcony of St Peter’s Basilica, after which you will have time to explore the Basilica at your own leisure. Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. data.name: The Life of Julius Caesar: Rome Private Half-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Explore the Rome of Julius Caesar, born to an impoverished aristocratic family in the ‘suburban’ with zero political ambitions, Julius Caesar was not expected to become a consul of Rome let alone its sole dictator in perpetuity, and one of the most famous and influential men in history. On your private tour, you will: Begin at the mighty Circus Maximus, where Caesar will have come to watch the races, famous for being the largest stadium for chariot racing in the world, with marble seating for over 250,000 spectators. Learn all about this popular, and highly dangerous sport; Admire the stunning views of the ancient palaces of the Palatine cascading down the hill; Hear all about the importance of public games for the smooth running of society: ‘Give them bread and circuses! Learn all about the early life of Julius Caesar and his unlikely, stratospheric political and military rise to power; Wander down the hill towards the River Tiber and look over the bridge to Trastevere where Julius Caesar had a villa and where he housed Cleopatra; Discover Teatro Marcellus, an ancient open-air theatre used for artistic performances;  See the ruins of the ancient fish market and the Portico d’Ottavia: the building of which was begun by Julius, and completed by his adopted son Octavian - better known as Caesar Augustus, who dedicated it to his sister, Octavia; Head towards the centre of governance in Ancient Rome, the Capitoline Hill;  Be wowed by the spectacular view overlooking the ruins of the Roman Forum, the cradle of the gods and of ancient civilization, and at the far end, the Colosseum; See the buildings that were begun by Caesar including the temple to Venus, the Curia, and his spy's humble resting place in the centre of the Forum; Across the Fori Imperiali (built by Mussolini) you’ll see the ruins of Trajan’s Forum and the firewall built to protect the forum and the suburban from fire; Wander through the ruins to see some of the Suburra where Caesar was born and raised, now a trendyneighbourhood called Monti; Walk back through Piazza Venezia, through the picturesque Jewish Ghetto toward the spectacular ruins at Largo Argentina; End your tour here with the dramatic story of Caesar’s assassination, on those very steps! Stabbed 23 times by his enemies so the blame was shared; including his trusted friend, Brutus, is where the mighty Julius Caesar was finally toppled. ‘Beware the ides of March'. From the slum neighbourhood of his birth to where he met his grisly end, the city, empire and culture of Rome owe much to Julius Caesar. With your private guide, gain an insight into Caesar's dominance as Consul of Rome. Learn all about his upbringing, private life (he was very much a lady’s man) and his military prowess that led to the Triumvirate with Pompey and Crassus – the betrayals and power play, and finally the crossing of the Rubicon. Julius Caesar was very much the people’s politician. He was loved by the people who considered him ‘one of them’. This popularity may have led to his hubris and downfall. Rome’s motto is SPQR (Senatus et Populusque Romanus) meaning the Senate and the People of Rome. Julius had the will of the people but arrogantly stopped consulting the senate. This cost him dearly, and on the ides of March 44 BC, he was assassinated, stabbed 23 times on the steps leading to the temporary senate-house, at Largo Argentina. An astute politician and brilliant military strategist Caesar powered Rome into expansion, decisively defeating enemies and winning the hearts and minds of the common people. Each successful war assured him of the undying loyalty of his soldiers, who followed him into battle after battle. His life and death, are the stories of legends with unions that include a love affair with Cleopatra. The contributions he made have echoed through history - including the introduction of the Julian Calendar in Rome, setting the year at 365.25 days, divided into 12 months. Your Tour of Julius Caesar’s Rome will delve into the archaeological roots of the city to follow in his footsteps. Discover Caesar’s place of birth in 100BCE - Suburra, a down-and-out area where the trendy area of Monti now stands, and end your tour where his life ended brutally on the steps of the theatre of Pompey at Largo Argentina.Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. data.description: With a program featuring the great Tosca, Rigoletto, La Bohème, Pagliacci, La Bohème, La Sonnambula and La Traviata by Verdi, Puccini, Bellini and Leoncavallo, this opera concert at Rome's beloved Palazzo Pamphili is sure to set you to return for more. Treat yourself to a wonderful and romantic experience: a candlelight dinner in a musical atmosphere that only Italian opera can offer. This limited and exclusive event will take place in the Innocenzo X Room of the Pamphilj Palace, from where you can enjoy a magnificent view of Piazza Navona. An elegant venue where you can sit at your reserved seat and enjoy the best of Italian cuisine, accompanied by a selection of fine wines. The musical programme, consisting of opera arias and duets, takes place both before the meal and during the serving of the dishes, with a final surprise at the end.

data.name: Colosseum, Palatine Hill, and Roman Forum Private Tour
data.description: Discover the history of ancient Rome during a private walking tour. Check out the Colosseum and see where gladiators once fought. Continue the private tour at the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Learn about the politics, culture, and customs of ancient Rome throughout the tour. Choose a start time that suits your schedule.

data.name: Private Cooking Class in the Heart of Rome 3 types of Pasta and Wine
data.description:
A gastronomic experience where you will learn all the secrets to prepare fantastic handmade fettuccine, gnocchi and cavatelli with the guidance of our chef Christian, Roman doc with twenty years of experience.

Learn how to prepare homemade pasta amid lots of laughter and fun.

data.name: Jewish Catacombs Private Viewing
data.description: Unlock rare access to the Jewish Catacombs of Vigna Randanini on this private tour through one of Rome’s hidden underground treasures. Don’t worry about the dark as you explore ancient tombs, inscriptions, and frescoes with a flashlight as your guide shares stories from the Roman Empire. Then, walk along the historic Appian Way—once a key Roman road—for a deeper look at the layers of history beneath the city’s surface.

data.name: Rome Small-Group Colosseum Arena Floor, Forum, Palatine Tour
data.description: Explore Rome’s iconic Colosseum unlike most other tourists—from the arena floor where the gladiators fought. You’ll also access the rest of the Colosseum and tour the Roman Forum and the ruins of Palatine Hill with a small group and a local expert who will share history and insights via headsets for ensured hearing.

data.name: Skip-the-Line Tickets to the Leonardo Da Vinci Exhibition
data.description: Immerging yourself in the extraordinary world of Leonardo da Vinci, a luminary of the Italian Renaissance, is an experience like no other. This tour offers you the chance to explore over 200 machines and engage with 65 working wooden models, all crafted from the renowned da Vinci codes. These include flying machines, war mechanisms, and water devices. The journey continues as you discover nine holograms, brought to life by cutting-edge holographic technology. These holograms illuminate da Vinci's studies on water, air, fire, and earth, offering a comprehensive insight into his scientific, military, and aviation inventions. Finally, admire 1:1 scale reproductions of Leonardo's drawings along with their interactive descriptions.The exhibition is housed in the Palazzo della Cancelleria, a late 15th-century building owned by the Vatican and one of Rome's architectural gems. The cherry on top? You'll also gain access to an underground Rome housing the remains of a burial temple dating back to 43BCE. This tour is not just about learning; it's about falling in love with Leonardo and his genius in a playful yet educational way.

data.name: Rome Leonardo da Vinci Museum Skip-the-Line Interactive Tour
data.description: Immerse yourself in the creative world of Leonardo da Vinci on this museum tour in Rome. While most museums keep their artefacts behind glass, this hands-on experience offers a more engaging way to interact with history. Explore 50 full-scale replicas of da Vinci’s inventions, from flying machines to robots, and discover how his ideas continue to shape the world today.

data.name: Shore excursion from Civitavecchia Port to Capalbio and the magic Tarot Garden
data.description: The Garden designed by the artist Niki de Saint Phalle is located in Capalbio and shows incredible sculptures up to 15 meters tall representing the 22 arcana of the Tarots, realized in steel and concrete and covered with mirrors, glasses and colored ceramics.

data.name: Private Tour of Colosseum Underground Or Arena and Forum
data.description: Discover the wonders of the Colosseum—and see sides of the UNESCO-listed landmark that most visitors miss—on this introductory tour. Learn about the Colosseum and either walk on the arena floor or explore the underground areas that few travelers get to see. Next, the tour also includes entry to the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. See the sights with your guide and, once the tour ends, choose to explore further if you wish.

data.name: Vatican Museum access without a tour guide
data.description: Ensure fast entry and admire the masterpieces of the Museums, including the Sistine Chapel, at your own pace.

data.name: Rome Private Sightseeing Tour
data.description: Discover Rome’s iconic landmarks and hidden gems on this private minivan tour, complete with an English- or Spanish-speaking driver. From ancient ruins to stunning fountains, this tour ensures a memorable experience of the Eternal City’s highlights. Enjoy the convenience of exploring at your own pace as well as onboard Wi-Fi so you can stay connected.

data.name: Gladiator school for adult
data.description: this we propose is a hard session for people who want to experience the life and the real training of the real gladiators of 2000 years ago. it will be possible to try fights with gladius and shield, net and trident, all in safety and strict discipline. A unique experience in the world, in a real arena. We supply clothing and accessories for the protection of the body and hands

data.name: Oratorio Del Gonfalone: Hommage à Ravel - 150th anniversary of his birth
data.description: Experience a magical evening at the Oratorio del Gonfalone: Hommage à Ravel – 150° anniversario della nascita, where the intricate melodies of Maurice Ravel will take center stage. Nestled in the historic heart of Rome, the Oratorio del Gonfalone provides a perfect backdrop for this homage to the iconic composer. This event marks 150 years since Ravel's birth and features an enchanting program that includes his seminal works such as 'Pièce en forme de Habanera', 'Cinq mélodies populaires grecques', and the profoundly evocative 'Pavane pour une enfante défunte'. Audiences will also be treated to the rhythmic 'Deux Mélodies hébraiques' and the world-renowned 'Bolero’. The delightful addition of 'Like a tribute to Ravel' by contemporary composer Laurent Boutros further enriches the celebration. The Oratorio Del Gonfalone: Hommage à Ravel – 150° anniversario della nascita promises an immersive experience, with each note capturing the genius of Ravel in the intimate setting of this historic venue. This event is an unmissable opportunity for music enthusiasts and admirers of Ravel's legacy to come together and revel in his timeless contributions.

data.name: Private Vatican Museum Tour

data.name: Rome Private Colosseum and Roman Tour for Kids

Book now for an unforgettable experience !

data.name: Rome Private City Tour With Driver
data.description: There’s so much to see and do in Rome, it can be challenging just getting started. This tour does much of the legwork for you, offering a private driver to take you to many top city attractions in just a few hours of sightseeing. See the Trevi fountain, Spanish Steps, Colosseum, and more. Collaborate with your driver to create a custom itinerary and decide how long to stay at each attraction.

data.name: Rome Christmas Market and Holiday Food Tour
data.description: Join this festive Christmas market and food tour through Trastevere’s illuminated cobblestone streets. Savor authentic Roman pasta paired with local wine, guided by stories of holiday traditions. Then, wander through Piazza Navona's vibrant Christmas market with a rich Italian hot chocolate in hand, followed by classic Christmas desserts like panettone and pandoro to complete the experience. Celebrate the season with the warmth, flavors, and charm of a Roman Christmas.

data.name: Candlelight Happy Hour Tour in Historic Pigneto District in Rome
data.description: Discover the historic and lively Pigneto district with an exclusive Candlelight Happy Hour experience. Start your adventure at Metro C Pigneto Station, immerses yourself in the rich history of this eclectic neighbourhood, renowned for its bohemian allure and artistic vitality. Uncover a hidden underground venue tucked beneath the bustling streets, where you can savour a handpicked selection of three distinct wines, complemented by local delicacies.Guided by a professional food and wine expert, this one-of-a-kind experience provides insights into the district’s historical metamorphosis and gastronomic evolution. data.name: Rome: Express Golf Cart City Tour

Understand Rome’s past glory as you see it in action, from bustling food shops to high-speed races.

data.name: Rome Highlights in A Day: Colosseum, Vatican, Lunch & Transfer
data.description: A convenient opportunity for travelers short on time, this private Coliseum and Vatican tour takes you to multiple landmarks in one day—with a delicious lunch and convenient transfers provided. data.name: Rome Pigneto Small-Group Guided Food Tour

Enjoy authentic Roman-style pizza, fried rice balls, meatballs, roasted pork, and a range of traditional street foods as you navigate the lively neighborhood, chatting to the stallholders and learning the area’s unique culture along the way.

data.name: Rome: Vespa Tour with Pro Photographer Guide
data.description: Capture your Roman holiday in style on this Vespa tour with an accompanying professional photographer. Drive by many must-see landmarks, including the Colosseum and the Castel Sant'Angelo, for a comprehensive overview of the Eternal City. Avoid the disappointment of taking sub-par vacation snaps—your driver–photographer–guide will take you to the most scenic spots, then take beautiful photos of you.

data.name: Florence to Montalcino and Montepulciano Wine Tour
data.description:

data.description: Cruise through Rome in a vintage Fiat 500, stopping to admire the best of the Eternal City. Driven by a knowledgeable guide, see iconic landmarks including the Circus Maximus and the Colosseum, and explore the bustling Trastevere neighborhood. Along the way, enjoy a tasty gelato or a classic cappuccino and pastry.

data.name: Trastevere District Street Food and Sightseeing Walking Tour
data.description: Meet on Tiberine island, where your street food tour of the atmospheric Roman neighborhood of Trastevere begins. Follow the cobblestone streets to discover some authentic hidden gems of this lively area on the other side of the river. Be prepared to sample some authentic Roman and Italian street food! Taste cheese and meat at a local deli, then supplì, a typical deep-fried rice ball filled with mozzarella cheese and tomato sauce. Learn about the history of the district, and visit the Basilica of Santa Maria, the heart of Trastevere, before heading for some pizza. Your guide will help you find your way through local restaurants or bars and pubs where young residents spend the night. See Piazza Trilussa and Ponte Sisto, with a beautiful view of Saint Peter’s dome from the river, before heading to the final desserts on the road. This is an area you may not discover otherwise. The small group will not exceed 12 people, so you will feel like wandering the city in a friendly atmosphere.

Learn about the landmark’s ancient imperial heyday during this small-group, half-day guided tour, which includes a stop at the nearby Roman Forum.

data.name: Rome Highlights Private Classic Vespa and Photography Tour

Forget the selfie sticks and blurry iPhone photos and get whisked away on a classic Italian Vespa while a professional photographer captures your memories. Visit the Colosseum, Orange Garden, Trastevere, and Gianicolo Terrace all in one seamless adventure.

data.name: The "Madonnelle" of Rome power walking tour
data.shortDescription:
Another wonderful tour for 2025 is coming!
​Tiny shrines hanging on the walls of ancient buildings, mostly at a street corner, the majority of which portraying a Madonna, and sometimes so simple and modest that they remain unnoticed by those who walk around the city. The Romans call them “Madonnelle” and are the expression of a profound popular, street devotion that reflects the intensity of the Marian cult in the city. Their use, however, dates back to ancient Rome, when the Lares Compitales, the pagan deities maybe of Etruscan origin, were entrusted with the protection of all street intersections.
Made of oil or fresco paintings, marble or terracotta carvings, or mosaics, they are today about 500 but once they were thousands, surrounded by votive offerings left by the faithful: up to the early 1900s they used to be well cared for by the local inhabitants, whose donations were used for a constant maintenance, and for keeping candles and lanterns burning in front of them at all times. In this way, in the days before gas and electricity, they provided almost the only form of lighting in the streets of Rome.

The starting point will be tailored, because it is possible to start from Piazza Navona or from Spanish steps.
The Path is 5k and along the path we will discover all the History behind every Madonnella, every street and monument of the Eternal city. It will be fun!

For 2025 ArcheoRunning has decided to launch a new idea of experiential tourism, sustainable and outside the usual patterns. Next year, due to the Jubilee, there will be an exponential growth in tourism (very often mass tourism). So to get around all this we want to propose a series of "Early bird experiences" by ArcheoRunning. The project was born to encourage more people to practice sports and at the same time get to know unusual places in Rome, practicing a gentle movement. The added value is professionalism. Art historian, archaeologist, FIDAL technician, Coni physical trainer, qualified tourist guide are just some of the peculiarities of the founder of the project, which guarantee an experience studied in every aspects.

So, what you waiting for?

data.name: Aqueducts Park running tour
data.shortDescription:
The Aqueducts Park with its 240 hectares of size is one of the green lungs of the city of Rome. It is one of the most fascinating parks in Rome because it contains 2000 years of history.

In fact, six of the numerous ancient Roman aqueducts are preserved here, making it an open-air museum. We will run in a unique atmosphere, suspended between past and present, in the golden light of dawn when the imposing arches of the aqueduct stand out against the sun in all their suggestive beauty, framed by pine trees.

We will go to discover all this, learning about its history, anecdotes and most hidden secrets, in full ArcheoRunning style!

Your expert local guide will take you through Rome’s historic center, sharing stories, fun facts, and archaeological insights along the way. This private tour is fully customizable — whether it’s your first time in Rome or you’ve visited before, we’ll tailor the route to your interests.

Ideal for families, couples, or small groups looking for a relaxed and fun way to explore Rome.

data.name: Ancient Rome From the Colosseum to the Forum with the Eyes of a Gladiator
data.description:
Follow the legendary route of Roman gladiators as you enter the partially reconstructed arena floor through the exclusive "Gladiator Gate".Explore the floor of the arena, once the scene of gladiator combat and elaborate spectacles, which offers unparalleled views and a glimpse into the underground mechanisms where magic took place.

Experience the atmosphere of the ancient arena when the stands were packed, the crowd roared and the fate of the gladiators was in their hands.

Continue your journey with a short uphill walk to the Palatine Hill for panoramic views of the Roman Forum. Dubbed the “first nucleus of ancient Rome” for its unparalleled beauty, the Palatine Hill offers a unique perspective on the charm of Rome, animated by an expert guide. End with a fascinating visit to the Roman Forum, the beating heart of ancient Rome, where dramatic events have shaped the course of history.

data.name: Best of Rome Pass
data.description: Visit all the best sites in Rome with a single 3-day pass! Report at the Touristation Piazza Venezia Office to redeem your voucher and get easy access to Rome’s major sights. Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill: Meet the staff at the office near the Roman Forum entrance. Your pass includes the visit to the Roman Forum, where the Roman citizens used to live, and to the Palatine Hill, the site of the foundation of Rome and settlement of the most important houses of emperors and kings. At the end, step inside one of the world's most famous monuments: the Colosseum. The entrance to the Colosseum will be approximately 2 hours after the meeting point time. Explore the immense amphitheater, the largest ever built by the Roman Empire.Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel: you will get to enjoy a hassle-free experience all at your own pace. The Sistine Chapel alone is well worth a trip when in Rome, but get more with this ticket to the Vatican Museums as well. Painted by the greatest Renaissance painters, the chapel’s famous frescoes are quite simply sublime. St. Peter’s Church and Tombs of the Popes: Enjoy more time at the Pope's home at Church and visit the Tombs of the Popes using the official audio guide that's included in your pass. Pantheon: Stand beneath the celestial eye of the Pantheon and visit the eternal home of Raffaello.

data.name: Rome at Night Private Driving Tour With Prosecco Toast
data.description: Experience a different side of the Rome on this private driving tour at night. Travel around the city in comfort and see some of its most iconic landmarks, including the Colosseum, Pantheon, Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps, and St, Peter’s Basilica, illuminated after dark. Then enjoy a prosecco toast over panoramic views of the Eternal City from Terrazza del Gianicolo.

data.name: Rome: Food and Culture Private Half-Day Food Tour
data.description: From pizza to gelato, Rome is one of the best places in Italy to sample the full range of flavors that Italian cuisine has to offer. On this half-day private food tour, visit some of the city’s most popular landmarks, such as the Pantheon and the Galleria Spada, while sampling authentic Italian flavors at restaurants and food stalls.

data.name: Photo Tour in Garbatella, the neighborhood of garden houses
data.description: Garbatella is a unique neighborhood in the world. Born as a housing district for the workers who would build the factories of the nascent Ostiense industrial district, it was conceived in an innovative way: condominiums (called "plots") consisting of 2 or 3-storey houses in neo-baroque style with shared gardens in which the inhabitants could socialize. Over the years the type of houses and their function changed but the charm of the district has remained intact and still today it seems a city apart from the city

data.name: Roma antigua + Almuerzo + Museos Vaticanos
data.description: El tour, de día completo, incluye la visita de dos de los más famosos lugares de Roma. Coliseo – Palatino – Foro Romano – Museos Vaticanos – Aula de Pio Clementino – Mirador de Lacconte y Apolo – La Galería de los Candelabros – La Galería de los Tapices – La Galería de los Mapas – Capilla Sixtina – Basílica De San Pedro – Plaza de San Pedro. Acerca de Por la mañana podrá admirar el Coliseo, símbolo de los tiempos de la Antigua Roma, El Palatino, lugar de origen de la ciudad, y el Foro Romano, el área arqueológica más hermosa e importante del mundo. Tras el almuerzo, el tour continúa con la visita a los Museos Vaticanos, una de las colecciones de arte más importantes del mundo. El itinerario incluye el Aula de Pio Clementino, el Mirador de Laocoonte y Apolo, la Galería de los Candelabros, la Galería de los Tapices, la Galería de los Mapas y la Capilla Sixtina para admirar los frescos de Miguel Ángel, una de las obras de arte más famosas de todos los tiempos. Desde el Museo saldrá directamente a la Basílica de San Pedro, la Iglesia Cristiana más importante del mundo, para admirar, entre otros, la obra maestra de Miguel Ángel, La Piedad, y el impresionante altar Baldaquín de Bernini. El tour finaliza en la Plaza San Pedro, dominada por la imponente Cúpula de Miguel Ángel, y rodeada por la célebre doble columnata de Bernini. Duración 8 horas Idioma Español Incluye entradas de “salta la cola” guía, auriculares almuerzo IMPORTANTE: esta prohibido entrar en el Coliseo con maletas, mochilas y bolsas voluminosas. No hay depósito de bolsa en el Coliseo. El Museo requiere que los clientes en silla de ruedas sigan un itinerario diferente y no estan autorizados permitido a realizar nuestro tour habitual. No es permitido entrar en la Iglesias en pantalón corto, hombros descubiertos, minifaldas. Esta asimismo prohibido entrar en el Museo con objetos de metal, paraguas y mochilas. Si la Basílica de San Pedro está cerrada para cerimonias religiosas, se visitará en alternativa la Galeria de arte. Final Plaza de San Pedro – traslados a los hoteles no esta incluido

data.name: Piazza Navona, Pantheon, Trevi Fountain & Spanish Steps: Guided Walking Tour
data.shortDescription: Set foot in Rome's hidden ancient treasures and see beyond the typical sights
data.description:
Start your walking tour in Rome at Campo de’ Fiori, a busy square known for its Renaissance charm and local cafes.

Next, head to Largo di Torre Argentina, where you’ll see the remains of four ancient Roman temples at an open-air archaeological site.

As you continue through the city’s historic streets, you’ll come across old churches, palaces, and fountains along the way.

Arrive at the Pantheon, a well-preserved monument from ancient Rome that was originally built by Marcus Agrippa in 27 BC as a temple dedicated to all the Roman gods.

From there, walk to the Trevi Fountain, one of Rome’s most famous and romantic landmarks. Toss a coin into the water if you’d like to return to the city someday.

End your tour at Piazza di Spagna, home to the Spanish Steps and surrounded by shops and historic buildings.

Housed in the historic Oratorio del Gonfalone in Rome, this performance brings to life an array of musical delights from delicate fantasies to lively tarantellas. The ambiance of the venue, with its ornate frescoes and intimate setting, adds a unique charm, making it a perfect location for this enchanting event. data.name: Great Symphonies at Piazza Navona
data.description: In this highly-anticipated concert, hear the mellifluous sounds of chamber music by Mozart and Beethoven at Rome's treasured and world-renowned Sant’Agnese in Agone. Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart Perhaps the most important composer of all time, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was an Austrian composer of the late 18th century. Born in 1756 in Salzburg, he showed prodigious musical talent from childhood. Beginning at five years of age, he composed more than 600 works, including concertos, symphonies, religious works and operas before his premature death at the age of 35. Hi influence over successive generations cannot be overestated - Ludwig van Beethoven wrote of Mozart 'posterity will not see such a talent again in 100 years”. Despite the immense success of his compositions, and the acclaim he received across Europe, Mozart achieved little financial security and rwas buried in an unmarked grave in Vienna's St Marx Cemetery. Ludwig van Beethoven Ludwig van Beethoven was a German pianist and composer of the late 18th century. He is well known as the most influential composers of all time as well as crucial figure to the Classical music scene. In fact, he demonstrated his musical talent at an early age, taking lessons from his father and composer/conductor Christian Gottlob Neefe. Later, he moved to Vienna where he gained the reputation of a virtuoso pianist by composing his popular masterpieces. He created his most admired works in his last 15 years of life, all the while being almost completely deaf.

data.name: Capitoline Museums Private Tour
data.description: Welcome to the first museum in the world! The Capitoline Museums (plural as it is four buildings on top of one of the famous seven hills of Rome) host a fascinating collection of art and artifacts that narrate the captivating history of Rome. In 1734, Pope Clement XII decided to make an important collection of works of art and ancient sculptures permanently accessible to the inhabitants of Rome. With this magnanimous act he created the first museum in the world, which stands on top of one of the seven hills of Rome and dominates the ancient Roman Forum. It is a true blaze of history. Watch the famous sculpture of the she-wolf with the founders of Rome, Romulus and Remus, and admire this magnificent casket containing the history of Rome, the ancient Caput Mundi.

data.description: Do not miss this incredible performance of one of the most heartbreaking composition of all time in the sumptuous St. Paul's Within the Walls Church of Rome. data.name: Rome: Angels and Demons Tour Half-Day Semi-Private
data.description: Explore Rome following the trail of Dan Brown's best seller, enjoy the tour discovering Rome's “Angels and Demons” along the path of the Illuminati.The treasure hunt through the Eternal City follows the itinerary of the Illuminati.The tour begins at Pantheon where Robert Langdom, the protagonist of Dan Brown's book, casually arrives because he misunderstood a clue. His actual destination is the church of Santa Maria del Popolo in Popolo Square, that is also our second stop. The church is famous for his beautiful paintings and his Chigi chapel, where Robert Langdom will find the first dead cardinal branded with a “EARTH” on his chest. Next stop will be St. Peter's Basilica, the Centre of Christianity. At the centre of the square there is an obelisk surrounded by a meridian with the wind rose. On the “ West Ponente” oval tile the protagonist finds another dead cardinal branded with “AIR”. Then, Langdom goes to the Vatican secret archives to look for information about the sect of the “Illuminati”. From the Vatican you will head to the Church of Santa Maria della Vittoria, in which you will admire the famous Bernini's sculpture “ Estasi di Santa Teresa”. Here Langdom finds the third dead cardinal branded with the word “FIRE”. After that you will walk through the most important places of the old town centre, such as Repubblica Square and Navona Square, where you will enjoy the wonderful Bernini's “Fountain of the four rivers” and the obelisk. According to the book, in this place Langdom finds the last dead cardinal branded with the word “WATER”. From Navona Square you will reach the last stop that is Castle Sant’Angelo, gathering place of the Illuminati, famous for the “passetto”, an hidden passage that leads to the Vatican City, a shortcut often used by the Popes as a way to escape, and in the book used as a hideout for the assassin. Whether you've read book or not, this tour allows you to visit Rome in a completely unusual and interesting way.

data.name: Rome City Highlights Exclusive Private Tour with Colosseum
data.description: Discover the wonders of Rome during this exclusive half-day tour of Rome's landmarks and highlights, including access to the Colosseum. Your own private guide takes you to some of the city’s most cherished sites—from the Colosseum to the Trevi Fountain, Pantheon, and Piazza Navona—ensuring everything that matters is on your itinerary. data.name: St. Peter's Basilica: Guided Tour + Vatican Grottoes Access
data.description:
Explore the Vatican City, a remarkable citadel with the world's renowned square, St. Peter's Square. Admire the ancient Egyptian obelisk reaching towards the heavens.

Take a fascinating trip through this architectural wonder, appreciating its intricate designs. Uncover visual illusions crafted by Bernini and discover hidden gems within the square.

Enter the Basilica and be amazed by the spectacular artwork adorning its vast interiors. A savvy guide reveals standout features, including the Papal Altar beneath Bernini's *Baldachin* and Michelangelo's timeless masterpiece, *La Pietà*.

The adventure continues with a visit to the mysterious Papal Grottoes, the extensive crypt beneath St. Peter's Basilica.

data.name: Stadium of Domitian & Trevi Fountain Rome: Stadium Visit + Trevi Guided Tour
data.description:

Grab a ticket for the Navona Underground and explore a remarkably preserved area of the once-mighty empire under bustling Piazza Navona. With this double-entrance ticket you'll wander age-old ruins where Rome's first-ever sporting arena once stood, and, in a small group, take an exclusive look around the ancient grandstand.

Continue exploring with a visit to a maze of ancient vestiges, and the archaeological site of Vicus Caprarius, found beneath the famous Trevi district. Touch some of the historic foundations of ancient Roman buildings!

data.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Skip The Line Ticket + Guided Tour
data.description:
Take a journey through Vatican City's highlights on this three-hour guided tour. Explore the Vatican Museums and see the spectacular Sistine Chapel.

Begin this excursion into the Vatican's art and architecture at the Vatican Museums, which house the world's most important ancient art collection. From the Egyptian Museum to the Etruscan Museum, the Greek-Roman section to the Collections of Renaissance Art, there's something for everyone.

Follow your guide to the greatest galleries and see frescoes, statues, tapestries, and historical maps. Find the Borgia Apartment with rooms painted by Raphael, the Vatican Pinacoteca, the Gallery of Maps, the Courtyard of the Pine Cone, and more.

Continue to the Sistine Chapel to admire masterpieces by Botticelli, Ghirlandaio, Pinturicchio, and Perugino. And, of course, you'll have the chance to see Michelangelo's most famous work, the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. This is an experience you'll remember for the rest of your life.

data.name: Colosseum and Roman Forum Guided Tour
data.description: Discover Rome at your own pace with a combined 24/48-hour ticket for a hop-on hop-off sightseeing bus, and a guided tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Walk in the footsteps of Roman emperors and citizens on a tour of Ancient Rome, with skip-the line entrance to the Roman Forum. Walk along the Via Sacra and immerse yourself in Roman history. The main path through the Roman Forum, the Via Sacra once sparkled with festivals and triumphal processions. End at the Temple, which houses the altar where Julius Caesar was cremated. Visitors from around the world still leave flowers and candles at the site to this day.Before reaching the Colosseum, get a general overview of Palatine Hill where legend has it Romulus founded the city of Rome. The hill looks down over the Roman Forum and the Circus Maximus chariot-racing circuit. Once inside the Colosseum, your expert guide will teach you about the amphitheater's bloody past, with tales of gladiators, mock sea battles, and executions. After discovering the highlights of Imperial Rome, you can use your 24 or 48-hour ticket for the open top hop-on-hop-off sightseeing bus to discover more of the city in a convenient way.

data.name: The Roman Food Tour including visit to the Trionfale food market

Stroll around the dynamic food markets, chat with the so-called Michelangelo of pizza at the famed Pizzarium (and sample a slice). Munch on cured meets and cheeses at Paciotti Salumeria, the best gourmet shop in the city. And savor fresh pasta and wine at an award-winning restaurant. Finally, finish off the tour with some delicious gelato.

data.name: UNESCO Jewels: Tivoli and Its Villas
data.description: Visit Tivoli, an ancient resort area famed for its beauty and its good water, enriched by many Roman villas, the most famous one, of which the ruins remain, is Villa Adriana. Take a comfortable transport to the little town of Tivoli, located a few kilometers from Rome, in a splendid natural environment between the Eternal City and the high hills to the east of Rome. Since ancient times this little town has been blessed by a great climate and always had a key importance due to its location. The most remarkable architectural complex is Villa Adriana, dating from the Ancient Roman time, created in the 2nd century AD by the Emperor Hadrian. It combines different architectural styles from Egypt, Rome and Athens, in the shape of an "ideal city". For this reason a visit to the Villa cannot be missed: it is a masterpiece that uniquely brings together the highest symbols of cultures of the world in ancient times. The Villa covers more than 120 hectares and was the House of the Emperors for more than 50 years. After this amazing visit, come to discover the Renaissance-style Villa d’Este, a gorgeous palatial setting surrounded by a spectacular terraced garden. Enjoy the beauty of its cascades, water tanks, and fountains. Villa d'Este is a masterpiece of the Italian Gardens, decorated with a massive and impressive number of fountain nymphs, grottos and marvelous courtyards inspired by the gardens of Babylon, one of the wonders of ancient world. Strongly desired by the Cardinal Ippolito II d'Este, the Villa was enlarged and enriched by all his descendants with the contribution of incredible artists of the times, like Gianlorenzo Bernini. Return to Rome in the afternoon

data.name: The Four Seasons by Antonio Vivaldi at Chiesa Evangelica Metodista
data.description: Immerse yourself in the timeless beauty of Antonio Vivaldi's renowned masterpiece, 'The Four Seasons', at the Chiesa Evangelica Metodista. This captivating concert is a gateway to the mesmerizing harmonies and enchanting melodies of the Baroque era. Unlike other composers of the Baroque period, Vivaldi's 'Four Seasons' offers an unparalleled depiction of the changing moods of each season. His precise and vivid portrayal of nature's wonder is a testament to the era's fascination with the natural world. Through his composition, Vivaldi's work transports listeners back in time. The music of 'The Four Seasons' not only astounds with its stunning representation of nature, but also through its unique musical language. Vivaldi's unconventional melodies, heightened rhythms, and harmonies create a sense of awe and astonishment. The composition allows for a more fluid and expressive musical experience, bringing the story of each season to life. Vivaldi's innovative approach to music perfectly encapsulates the essence of the Baroque era. From the cheerful chirping of spring birds to the intense summer storms, from the sounds of fleeing foxes in autumn to the chilling rain of winter, his music vividly portrays the beauty and drama of nature. This magnificent artwork actively engages the audience in the rapid succession of events. Witness the evocative power of Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' at Chiesa Evangelica Metodista. This revolutionary example of Italian Baroque music, performed by the Opera e Lirica Academy strings quintet and harpsichord, is guaranteed to leave you enthralled. CHIESA EVANGELICA METODISTA Located in the heart of Rome, just steps from Via Nazionale and Porta Pia, the beautiful Chiesa Evangelica Metodista serves as both a church and a concert hall. Built in 1895, the exterior of the building features a sixteenth-century style, with ashlar walls, high pilasters on each floor, and mullioned windows on the ground level. The entrance portal, adorned with a gate, overlooks Via XX Settembre and is crowned with a tympanum supported by columns. Inside the church, you will find a rectangular plan with a horseshoe-shaped women's gallery and a ceiling adorned with circular motifs set within panels. Corinthian style lateral pilasters, resting on a high base, punctuate the space, along with round mullioned windows. The pipe organ, constructed by Carlo Vegezzi-Bossi in 1895 and electrified in 1980, boasts 13 registers on two manuals and pedal. In 1924, Paolo Paschetto adorned the church walls with stunning internal windows, featuring themes and symbols from the Christian iconographic tradition. The Christogram, the dove, the lily, the lamb, the lamp, the palm, the peacock, and the ship are just a few examples. Additionally, the pulpit, constructed in 1930, adds to the visual splendor of this extraordinary venue.

data.name: Pompeii: Day Trip from Rome + Lunch
data.description:
Get swept off your feet and transported back in time with this exhilarating guided tour of the legendary Pompeii.

Starting at the crack of dawn at the Castro Pretorio metro stop, a luxurious, air-conditioned minibus navigated by seasoned drivers will be waiting to take you on an adventure.

By 11:00 a.m., you'll be standing amidst the ruins of Pompeii, with an expert guide breathing life into the stones with vivid narratives.

Take a two-hour tour, uncovering fascinating spots like the buzzing Forum, the luxurious Thermal Baths, the scandalous Lupanare, the majestic Greek theatre, and the haunting plaster casts of Pompeii's inhabitants tragically frozen in time by volcanic ash in 79 A.D.

Post-adventure, indulge in a bit of retail therapy before savoring a delectable pizza and a refreshing drink before your trip home from the starting point.

data.name: Cooking Class in the Roman countryside
data.description: Nothing speaks more authentic Italian than visiting an ancient village off the beaten tourist track, especially if you add cooking and eating to the picture. We chose Mazzano Romano, a special location 35 km north of Rome: this Medieval town is right inside the protected area of the Veio Regional Park. You’ll travel to Mazzano Romano by car. Wear comfortable clothes and avoid your best shoes, because you’ll join our trusted chef to either go grocery shopping at a farmer’s market or, according to season, you’ll reach a lavish farm! Here you’ll pick by hand all of the ingredients required for your lunch: seasonal veggies, fragrant herbs, and freshly laid eggs. Once in the kitchen, you’ll learn how to prepare every item on the menu: antipasti, several kinds of hand-made fresh pasta, a second course and a lovely dessert. This step-by-step class that employs easy techniques is suitable for aspiring cooks of all ages and will let you become a pasta pro, perfectly able to replicate the whole menu once you’re back home. You’ll lunch to your own preparations, perfectly paired with some good wine and maybe you’ll find out that you have a real talent for Italian cuisine! Then, enjoy the countryside and relax: in the afternoon we’ll take you back to Rome

data.name: Florence Renaissance and Medieval: Day Trip from Rome by High-Speed Train
data.description: Visit Florence with a comfortable day trip from Rome. Depart in the morning from Roma Termini train station and in just 2 hours you will reach the heart of Florence, the city of Renaissance! Led by a local professional guide, your day will start with a comprehensive Walking Tour, discovering the most iconic sights of Renaissance and Medieval Florence. You will first explore the Medici district, where you will admire the famous Medici Palace, built in the mid 15th century and the first residence of the powerful and proud family, the ancient San Lorenzo Church and the Medici Chapels, with their mausoleum. A few steps away, you will be breathless in front of the beauty of the monumental complex of the Duomo, with the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, the iconic Brunelleschi's Dome, the elegant Giotto's Bell Tower and the beautiful Romanesque Baptistery of San Giovanni, with its golden “Porta del Paradiso. The tour then goes through the characteristic streets of the medieval district where Dante and Beatrice lived and where you can also admire the imposing and unique Church of Orsanmichele, a masterpiece of Florentine Gothic art. You will be led then to the picturesque Straw Market: don’t forget to rub the nose of the famous “porcellino” (little pig). Going on, you will find yourself in Piazza Signoria, one of the most beautiful squares in the world and the political center of the city. In this “open-air museum”, be fascinated by the beautiful Fountain of Neptune with the imposing marble statue of Ammannati and by the sculptural masterpieces of the Loggia dei Lanzi, including the Perseus by Cellini and the Rape of the Sabines by Giambologna. Dominating the square, the majestic Palazzo Vecchio with Arnolfo's crenellated tower, one of the most famous symbols of Florence. Following from the outside the spectacular elevated path of the Vasari Corridor, you will arrive at the romantic and picturesque Ponte Vecchio, the oldest bridge in Florence, and you will end this amazing walking tour admiring its renowned jewelry shops! In the afternoon, your official guide will lead you to the exciting discovery of the magnificent artistic treasures kept inside one of the most beautiful and largest cathedrals in the world, the magnificent Santa Maria del Fiore Cathedral (if option selected, otherwise enjoy the free time at your leasure !)

data.name: The Heart Of Rome: Private Golf Cart Tour
data.description: Discover the heart of Rome, as you cruise the most popular attractions and hidden backstreets that only small vehicles or pedestrians can access. On this private golf cart tour, you will: Visit the magnificent Spanish Steps that lead to the beautiful Trinita Dei Monti Church; Make a wish at the stunning Trevi Fountain and learn about the various myths behind the coins in the fountain; Pass by the over 2000 years old Pantheon – one of the best-preserved Ancient Roman buildings in existence; See the Colosseum (from the outside), Piazza Navona, Piazza Venezia, and Campo De Fiori; Enjoy the personalised attention of a private tour guide; Combine the intimacy of a walking tour with the comfort of a driving tour. Often referred to as the “Eternal City”, Rome is undoubtedly one of the most historically and culturally vibrant cities in the world. Here, you will come across the Pantheon and the Piazza Navona – two landmarks that date back to the Roman Empire; in addition, you’ll have the opportunity to see the amazing architecture of the Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps from the Rococo (late-Baroque) period. This four-hour golf cart tour is designed to give you a perfect overview of the city: visit the key sites in the centre and be shown all the best-hidden haunts and local hangouts that you might otherwise miss. A golf-cart tour allows you to access parts of the city that cars and tour buses cannot. Stop off at attractions or for gelato whenever you feel like it, go for a wander through Rome’s winding cobbled streets and save your energy for the rest of the day by hopping back on your golf cart, which will be waiting, ready to whisk you away to your next destination. A great way to experience the magic of Rome in a comfortable and flexible manner – and your experience will be unaffected by the weather! Please note: During the Jubilee Year, Rome is expected to experience increased visitor numbers and heightened security measures. While we strive to provide a seamless experience, some attractions may face last-minute closures without prior notice, longer-than-usual wait times, or time restrictions on visits inside certain attractions due to crowd control policies.In such cases, your guide will expertly adapt the itinerary to ensure the best possible experience, using their local knowledge to navigate any challenges. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to make your visit to Rome unforgettable despite these unique circumstances.

data.name: Florence in 1 Day: Renaissance Tour from Rome
data.description: Immerse yourself in the essence of Italian culture, art, and history with a captivating day trip from Rome to Florence, the heart of the Renaissance. Board a high-speed train for a seamless journey, whisking you away to this enchanting city of timeless beauty. Your adventure begins with a guided walking tour through Florence's storied streets, where every corner reveals a piece of history. Marvel at the magnificent Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, its iconic dome dominating the skyline with its grandeur. Cross the historic Ponte Vecchio, a symbol of medieval craftsmanship spanning the Arno River, and soak in the atmosphere of centuries past. After your guided exploration, the afternoon beckons with boundless possibilities. Delight in the freedom to wander at your leisure, immersing yourself in Florence's vibrant atmosphere. Discover hidden gems in the city's boutiques, where master artisans showcase their craftsmanship. Indulge your taste buds with local delicacies at charming trattorias or unwind with a glass of Chianti, the renowned wine of Tuscany. This meticulously crafted tour seamlessly blends curated activities with the flexibility to tailor your experience. Whether you're captivated by renowned landmarks or eager to uncover Florence's hidden treasures, this journey promises an unforgettable immersion into the soul of Italy's Renaissance gem
